## Q. Programme cadence ruling — BUILD FIRST, TEST AFTER (added 2026-08-17)

**Q1. The build-first directive.** Owner verdict 2026-08-17 via Cowork
question session, in response to "the engine is idle — what's the next
move?", verbatim: **"let's move on with the roadmap build we don't have
much time to spend in each one  i want to finish the build then we can test
as much as we want."** This is a STANDING CADENCE RULING for the master
roadmap build (the R1–R8 recovery sequence of `master_roadmap_v3.md` §6–7
and whatever the tracker shows unbuilt on the critical path):

(a) **Minimal per-node dwell.** Sessions build and land the next
critical-path node(s) without opening owner-acceptance round-trips
mid-sprint. Items needing owner eyes are QUEUED in `OWNER_REVIEW_QUEUE.md`
(workspace root, append-only, one dated entry per item with the artifact
path) and reviewed in BATCHES when the owner chooses — not one blocking
review per node.
(b) **Testing regime during the sprint:** existing suites stay green +
smoke/regression tests for new code land with it. The DEEP test campaign
(walkthroughs, fixture expansion, adversarial passes) runs AFTER the build
— "then we can test as much as we want."
(c) **What this does NOT change:** evidence discipline holds — honest FAIL,
never move a bar, never claim DONE for unlanded work. Speed comes from
cadence (fewer round-trips), never from lowering gates. Locked identities
(M3 `4ecc8e9df1d1`, accepted `.ai` sets, PASS_LAW corpus) stay untouched.
Supplier outreach stays WITHDRAWN (§C2).
(d) The H2 arc stands idle-but-open: third product and FB3093 calipers fold
in whenever the owner names them, without interrupting the sprint.

`SIGNED: BBrose (PROJECT_OWNER, via Cowork question session)  DATE: 2026-08-17`

## R. Build-sprint-2 rulings — four answers, given before the sprint opened (added 2026-08-17)

Owner verdicts 2026-08-17 via Cowork question session, answering the four
items `OWNER_REVIEW_QUEUE.md` had queued at the close of build sprint 1.
Each is a SEPARATE ruling and each is to be ingested as its own recorded
work item — a session ingests only what its launcher names EXPLICITLY.

**R1. RBV-4 provider-call budget: UP TO 10 LIVE CALLS FOR BUILD SPRINT 2.**
The `claude_visual_review/1.0` harness is authorized to spend at most ten
real provider calls within sprint 2 — enough for one to two genuine
end-to-end reviews on the RBV-3 P1 V4 package. Conditions, all binding:
(a) every call is cost-ledgered per the contract's `cost_governance` rule,
with the ledger committed as evidence — an unledgered call is a defect;
(b) the budget is per-sprint and does NOT roll over; when it is exhausted
the harness records `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` and continues offline — it never
silently degrades to fixtures while still labelling output as live;
(c) the deterministic offline path is still REQUIRED. The live budget
exists to prove the live path works, not to replace the fixture path;
(d) the budget authorizes EXECUTION only. It does not authorize a review to
approve anything. `Claude must not self-approve any gate` and `the OWNER
remains final authority` stay binding; a live finding is evidence feeding
the fail-closed gate, never a verdict.

**R2. Camera and lighting standards: APPROVED — both move to ACTIVE.**
`real_bottle_camera_standard/1.0` (orthographic FRONT / SIDE / TOP +
CLOSURE_DETAIL, 85mm-equivalent THREE_QUARTER_HERO for presentation only,
sRGB, 1600×2200, 6% crop padding, and the rule that compared images use
identical camera, scale and crop — never differing zoom) and
`real_bottle_lighting_standard/1.0` (flat neutral clay for
GEOMETRY_VALIDATION with reflections suppressed; three-point studio PBR for
CLIENT_PRESENTATION; identical lighting between compared images; geometry
verdicts NEVER made from presentation renders) are both APPROVED. Their
`status` becomes ACTIVE, carrying this §R2 provenance inline. Scope limits,
stated so nothing over-reads the approval:
(a) approving the STANDARD does not approve any RENDER. No render, package
or node gains visual-quality percentage from this ruling;
(b) it does NOT unblock mode B. CLIENT_PRESENTATION packaging stays
`ABSENT_BLOCKED` on rbv2c + the owner geometry gate, exactly as the RBV-3
rescope recorded. An approved presentation-lighting standard is a standard
waiting for a mode — not permission to badge a geometry render as
presentation (§1 two-mode principle, untouched);
(c) `real_bottle_comparison_contract.json` and
`claude_visual_review_contract.json` are NOT approved by this ruling. They
stay `PROPOSED_PENDING_OWNER_APPROVAL` and must still be quoted as such;
(d) amendable later through this sheet; an amendment supersedes visibly and
the superseded text stays on the record.

**R3. Build sprint 2 scope: RBV-4 + RBV-5, and stop there.** R2b
(`pc.vqr2b_reconstruction_measurement`) is NOT in sprint 2 — it depends on
the RBV-5 measurement stack landing first, and a half-landed R2b would put
`silhouette_fidelity` in a worse state than honest UNMEASURED. R2b opens
sprint 3.

**R4. One-time boundary exception for the inherited H2 gate failure.**
Sprint 2 IS authorized to resolve
`ComposedGateTests::test_no_new_occurrences_outside_the_baseline` — the 18
unregistered fallback-class occurrences `h2_design_request.py` inherited at
d04b874. Reason: the boundary rule exists to stop arcs corrupting each
other, not to keep a suite permanently red, and a standing red failure
hides real breakage. Strict scope:
(a) the exception covers ONLY the fallback-class registration decision —
registering the 18 occurrences in
`docs/roadmap/palt_m6/enforcement_closure/gate_baseline.json` as competent
with a per-occurrence justification, or restructuring the code that
produces them. Nothing else in the H2 tree may be touched, and no H2
run-tree state changes (if any index input changes,
`design_request_index.json` regenerates in the same commit);
(b) the gate may NOT be weakened to pass. No blanket exemption, no
wildcard, no baseline-wide rebuild. A negative control must prove the gate
still FAILS on a genuinely new unregistered occurrence after the fix;
(c) if the honest judgment is that an occurrence is NOT competent, it is
recorded as a defect and left failing with the finding written down —
honest FAIL still beats convenient PASS, and this exception does not
authorize the convenient answer;
(d) after this the suite must be genuinely green (0 failed), or the sprint
states exactly what remains red and why.

## S. Post-RBV-4 rulings — the exception at its real size (added 2026-08-17, after commits 81dc7d3 / 6b03ba3 / 176fad8)

Owner verdicts 2026-08-17 via Cowork question session, after the RBV-4
close report established two facts §R could not have known.

**S1. §R4 is EXTENDED to `palette_m7_ai_emitter.py` (2 occurrences / 2
keys).** §R4 was written against the sprint-2 launcher's description of
the composed-gate failure as "18 unregistered fallback-class occurrences
in `h2_design_request.py`". The measured set is **104 occurrences / 27
unique keys across four files**: `h2_design_request.py` (53/8, inherited
H2), `rbv3_review_package.py` (25/8, sprint 1's own, unnoticed because the
test was already red), `rbv4_claude_review.py` (24/9, added by RBV-4), and
`palette_m7_ai_emitter.py` (2/2, PALT-M7). The first three are inside §R4
or inside the RBV arc the executing session owns; only the emitter sat
outside, and leaving it red would have kept the suite red no matter how
well the other 25 keys were justified — which defeats the purpose of §R4
(a standing red hides real breakage). The extension carries §R4's terms
UNCHANGED: per-occurrence justification, no bulk registration, no
wildcard, no baseline-wide rebuild, a negative control proving the gate
still FAILS on a genuinely new unregistered occurrence, and an occurrence
honestly judged NOT competent is recorded as a defect and left failing.
The extension covers the fallback-class registration decision ONLY —
nothing else in the PALT-M7 tree may be touched, and the accepted `.ai`
files and their byte identities stay untouched (§I/§K/§N/§P).

**S2. The RBV-3 contact-sheet legibility defect is fixed inside the RBV-5
sprint, not deferred to the post-build campaign.** RBV-4's live review
reported the `bounds_dimensions` annotations unreadable at sheet scale.
The transmission record shows why it is worse than it looks: the sheet is
sent at 3840×3370 and the provider downscales anything above a 2576px
long edge, so the annotations are illegible to the reviewer as a matter of
arithmetic, not taste. Every remaining budgeted call is degraded until it
is fixed. The fix may address the sheet (larger annotations) or the
transmission (per-view crops at native scale instead of one downscaled
sheet) or both — the executor's judgment — but whichever is chosen, the
legibility claim must be MEASURED and recorded (effective rendered pixel
height of the annotation text after downscale), never asserted. If the
committed P1 V4 package artifacts change, the manifest and sheet hash
regenerate in the same commit and the sheet is LOOKED AT before it lands.

## T. Post-sprint-2 rulings — the threshold, and who judges the executor's own code (added 2026-08-17, after 53361f7)

Owner verdicts 2026-08-17 via Cowork question session, answering the two
items RBV-5 and the §R4/§S1 registration queued at sprint-2 close.

**T1. `PROFILE_DEVIATION_THRESHOLD` is a MEAN threshold at 0.03; max
deviation is retained as a recorded diagnostic and is NOT binding.** This
adopts the executor's own recommendation (queue option 2) and supplies the
number it correctly declined to choose. Basis, stated so the number is
never mistaken for a measurement:
(a) `canonical_self_comparison()` measured the instrument against itself —
max abs deviation **0.1359** (sample 24, a sharp width transition; the
first and last samples also spike at 0.1006 and 0.0588 from end
discretisation), mean abs deviation **0.0100**. Everything below those
figures is instrument noise, not subject error;
(b) the proposed max ≤ 0.05 sat BELOW that floor, so the gate was
measuring the rasteriser rather than the design. The executor refused to
widen it to make the gate pass and recorded FAIL instead — that was the
correct call and the reason this ruling exists;
(c) **0.03 is 3× the measured mean noise floor** — a conventional
signal-to-noise margin, and the tightest choice that is not measuring
noise. The mean is the stable statistic; the max is dominated by three
known-noisy samples and washing them into a binding verdict would produce
failures that carry no design meaning;
(d) there is NO measurement that determines this number. It is a
measurement-policy choice by the owner, and it should be recorded as such
— `OWNER_CALIBRATED` with this §T1 provenance, never `MEASURED`;
(e) the existing guard that asserts the noise floor exceeds the threshold
must be INVERTED, not deleted: it now asserts the binding mean threshold
sits ABOVE the measured mean floor, so nobody can quietly tighten it back
under the noise. Keep max reported on every verdict as a diagnostic; a
diagnostic that starts failing verdicts is a bar being moved.

**T2. The 3 executor-judged fallback keys get an INDEPENDENT pass; the 15
non-executor defects are QUEUED as their own work, not folded into sprint
3.** The executor registered 20 keys and left 18 failing, holding out 3 of
its own as competent-but-self-judged because self-judgment is not the
standard the other 20 met. That instinct is upheld and made procedure:
(a) an independent agent — one that did not write the code and is not the
agent that judged it — re-judges those 3 keys on the real source, tasked
with REFUTING competence and defaulting to refuted when uncertain, exactly
the adversarial method the other 20 passed. Whatever it concludes is the
disposition: cleared keys register with the independent provenance
recorded, refuted keys stay failing as defects;
(b) **no self-clearing.** If the independent pass cannot be run
independently, the keys stay failing. An author clearing their own code is
the failure mode this ruling exists to prevent, and a green suite is not
worth it;
(c) the 15 non-executor defects in the H2, RBV-3 and RBV-4 trees are real
FIXES, not registrations. They do not ride along with R2b. They are queued
in `OWNER_REVIEW_QUEUE.md` as a distinct body of work to be scheduled
after the build, per §Q;
(d) consequently the suite is EXPECTED to stay red at ~15 keys through
sprint 3. That is the honest state, it is documented per key, and every
session must keep re-verifying the failing set is exactly the recorded one
so a new failure cannot hide inside it.

## §U — POST-SPRINT-3 CALIBRATIONS AND THE AUDIT DEFECT (2026-08-17)

Sprint 3 landed §T1 and §T2 and opened R2b. It produced the programme's
first real silhouette PASS, and — more valuably — it discovered that §T1
was one commit away from being silently misapplied. The three rulings
below close the two queued calibrations and dispose of the defect the
independent refuters found. **Owner-answered; do not re-ask.**

### The finding that shapes all three: a threshold binds a STATISTIC, not an axis

Applying §T1 forced apart two constants that had been the same number.
`PROFILE_DEVIATION_THRESHOLD` binds a MEAN over 64 max-width-normalised
samples. `ASPECT_DEVIATION_THRESHOLD` binds a SINGLE absolute delta
between two height/width ratios. They were both `0.03`, so §T1's ruling —
made about the mean — would have landed on the ratio as well, calibrating
a quantity the owner never measured or ruled on. Splitting them is the
correct fix and it is now doctrine:

**A threshold constant carries the name of the statistic it binds, and no
owner ruling transfers from one statistic to another.** There are at least
three distinct silhouette tolerances live in this repo and none of them may
be reused for another:

| constant | quantity | measured floor |
|---|---|---|
| `rbv5.PROFILE_DEVIATION_THRESHOLD` | mean abs deviation, 64 normalised samples | 0.0100 |
| `rbv5.ASPECT_DEVIATION_THRESHOLD` | single ABSOLUTE delta of an h/w ratio | 0.0434 |
| `vqr2b.PROFILE_DEVIATION_THRESHOLD` | mean abs deviation, 64 normalised samples | **0.0** |
| `visual_quality_gate.THRESHOLDS["silhouette_max_aspect_deviation"]` | RELATIVE aspect deviation | not measured |

Any future session that finds two of these sharing a value must treat that
as a suspected conflation and prove otherwise before ruling on either.

### U1. RBV-5 aspect threshold = **0.13**, status `OWNER_CALIBRATED`

Three times the measured floor of 0.0434 — the same ratio §T1 chose for the
profile mean, applied deliberately and separately rather than inherited.

**Why 3×, and why that is a policy choice not a measurement.** The floor is
what `canonical_self_comparison()` measures when the subject IS the
canonical sample: 0.0434 of pure round-trip noise. A threshold at or below
it makes the gate report the rasteriser, not the design — the exact defect
§T1 fixed on the profile axis and the reason this axis was correctly left
FAILing rather than tuned. 3× puts the binding line clear of the noise while
staying tight enough that a real proportion error is caught. No measurement
determines the multiplier; the owner does. Hence `OWNER_CALIBRATED`, never
`MEASURED`.

**Binding conditions:**

(a) the constant's provenance string must state, in the file, that it binds
an ABSOLUTE delta of a height/width RATIO, and that it is NOT the profile
mean and NOT `silhouette_max_aspect_deviation`;

(b) the §T1 guard pattern applies here too and must be INVERTED the same
way: a test asserts the binding threshold sits ABOVE the measured aspect
floor, so nobody can quietly re-tighten it under the noise;

(c) the measured floor 0.0434 stays recorded on every verdict as a
diagnostic. A diagnostic that starts deciding verdicts is a bar being
moved and needs its own ruling;

(d) this calibrates the M3-canonical basis only. The real-bottle basis
stays honestly UNMEASURED until the RBV-1 P1 pack lands; 0.13 does not
travel to it without a floor measured on that basis.

### U2. R2b profile threshold = **0.03**, status `OWNER_CALIBRATED`

The executor's proposed number, given authority. It is unchanged in value
and completely changed in meaning.

**Why the reasoning is different from §T1's.** RBV-5's floor is 0.0100
because it compares a vector fit against a raster — two representations,
so some divergence is instrumental. R2b rasterises, masks and measures the
SAME file, and the test proves the round trip reproduces EXACTLY: floor
0.0. There is no noise to clear. So 0.03 is not "3× a floor"; it is a pure
design-tolerance statement — **a reconstruction may drift up to ~3% mean
deviation from its selected concept across the 64-sample profile before it
stops being that concept.** Every nonzero deviation R2b reports is
attributable to the artwork.

**Binding conditions:**

(a) the provenance must say the floor is 0.0 and that this number therefore
clears NO noise. Copying §T1's "3× the floor" sentence here would be false;

(b) because the floor is 0.0, the §T1 inverted guard does not apply in the
same form. What must be guarded instead is that the floor is still 0.0:
if the self-comparison ever stops reproducing exactly, the instrument has
changed and this ruling's premise is void. Assert it;

(c) 0.03 is calibrated against a self-comparison, which by construction has
never seen a real emitted `.ai`. The FIRST real reconstruction-vs-concept
comparison is an owner-review item: if honest work fails at 0.03, that is a
finding about the tolerance, and it comes back here — it is never fixed by
widening the number in the file;

(d) the resolution refusals stand and are not softened by this ruling. An
under-resolved raster is UNMEASURED and blocking, never a pass. The real
ES3083 lid refusing at 42px against a 64-sample floor is the instrument
working correctly.

### U3. The audit-honesty defect is FIXED in sprint 4 and cleared INDEPENDENTLY

The refuters found that an ABSENT `provider_request_id` field and an EMPTY
one produce byte-identical findings, so the refusal asserts
`provider_request_id=''` about a row that never carried the field. Its
author left it unfixed under §T2b rather than clear its own code. That was
correct and is upheld.

(a) sprint 4 fixes it as a first-class numbered work item: the two cases
must produce DISTINGUISHABLE findings, with a negative control proving they
diverge;

(b) an independent pass — an agent that neither wrote nor judged the code —
verifies **the property claimed, not the outcome observed.** This wording
is deliberate. The sharpest thing sprint 3 found was a register entry
reading "verified empirically, not asserted" whose author had verified that
the row refuses (the outcome) rather than that the line never runs (the
property claimed), while claiming the opposite. Every clearance from here
names which of the two it checked;

(c) if the independent pass cannot be run independently, the defect stays
recorded and failing. §T2b's no-self-clearing rule holds without exception.

### U4. On the record: why no-self-clearing is load-bearing

§T2's independent pass refuted all three executor-judged keys, six votes to
zero, and the executor confirmed the counterexample against its own claim:
the "unreachable default" was mechanically false — the missing-field loop
appends to a list, it does not refuse, and the only `raise` is 22 lines
later. Three keys the author judged competent were not competent. That is
not a procedural nicety vindicated; it is the rule catching exactly what it
was written to catch, on its first real use. It is not to be relaxed for
schedule reasons at any point in this programme.

`SIGNED: BBrose (PROJECT_OWNER, via Cowork question session)  DATE: 2026-08-17`

## §V — POST-SPRINT-4: LEDGER INTEGRITY, THE §R1 CARRY, DANGLING EDGES, AND THE INSTRUMENT (2026-08-17)

Sprint 4 landed §U1–§U3 in five commits and left `ire.design_graph_v2`
honestly IN_PROGRESS at 45% — a CONTRACT with 22 tests and nothing in
production calling it. Four rulings below. **Owner-answered; do not re-ask.**

### Two things sprint 4 did right that are now precedent

**A ruling is the number, not the arithmetic used to reach it.** §U1 said
0.13, described as "three times the measured floor of 0.0434". Exactly three
times is 0.1302, so a guard asserting `ratio >= 3.0` failed the owner's own
ruling at 2.9954. The executor bound the guard to what §U1(b) actually
requires — that the threshold sits ABOVE the measured floor — rather than
moving 0.13 to satisfy a test it had just written. That was correct.
Changing an owner's number to pass your own test is widening a threshold to
make your work pass, whatever the pretext. **Where a ruling states a value
and a rationale, the VALUE binds and the rationale is provenance.**

**A scoped clearance does not grow itself.** §U3 cleared
`provider_request_id`. The same independent pass found four more defects of
the same class in the same function, and the executor recorded them and
refused to fix them, because chaining self-directed fixes onto a scoped
clearance is how a scope becomes a blanket. Also correct, and the reason
§V1 exists rather than a commit.

### V1. §U3 is EXTENDED to all four residual `validate_ledger_row` defects, terms unchanged

Verified in `apps/pipeline/services/rbv4_claude_review.py`:

1. **`image_transmitted` — no value-level check at all.** It is in
   `LEDGER_REQUIRED_FIELDS` so it must be PRESENT, and nothing then tests
   what it holds: `'UNKNOWN'`, `0`, `False`, `'yes'` all pass on a row
   claiming a real call. **Fix this one FIRST.** It is the only one of the
   four where a bad row is ACCEPTED rather than merely mis-described, and it
   is therefore the only one that can let a falsified call into the budget.
2. **`input_tokens`, 3. `output_tokens`, 4. `cost_usd`** — each reads
   through `entry.get(field)`, so an absent field collapses into a
   present-null and the finding fabricates `=None`, a value the row never
   held. Same defect §U3 fixed for `provider_request_id`, three more times.

**Why one ruling for the class.** This is §S1's shape again: a ruling opened
on a target that turned out to be bigger than the ruling. §S1 extended §R4
to the m7 emitter on unchanged terms rather than pretending the measured set
matched the original scope, and that was right. Same here.

**Terms, unchanged from §U3:** an independent pass — an agent that neither
wrote nor judged the code — clears each fix, verifying **the property
claimed, not the outcome observed**, and stating which of the two it
checked. No self-clearing (§T2b, §U4). If the pass cannot be run
independently, the defects stay recorded and failing.

### V2. The 6 unspent §R1 calls carry forward — CONDITIONALLY

They are extended beyond build sprint 2 and become spendable **only once
V1's fixes have landed and cleared an independent pass.** Not before.

**Why conditional and not automatic.** The mechanism that enforces the
budget is `validate_ledger_row`. That is the code we just found accepts
`image_transmitted: 0` on a row claiming a real call. A budget policed by a
check that will accept a falsified row is not a budget; it is a number in a
file. **Enforcement precedes authorization.** The original §R1 terms
otherwise stand in full: every call ledgered, no rollover, `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`
rather than a silent fixture degrade, the offline path still required, and
execution authorizes no approval of anything.

Until V1 clears, the correct answer to "may I spend a call" remains no, and
it is not a judgement call.

### V3. Dangling tracker dependencies: GUARD FIRST, then repoint

Seven edges point at nodes that do not exist — six at `pc.owner_acceptance`
(`cp.creation_ux`, `gift_set.all`, `marketing.all`, `social.all`,
`booth.all`, `display_stand.all`) and one at `pc.structural_geometry`, which
is the sole dependency of `ire.design_graph_v2`, the node being built right
now. A dependency that cannot resolve cannot gate, so these read as
constraints and enforce nothing.

(a) **The guard lands first**: a test that FAILS on any dependency naming a
node not in the tracker. Then the seven are repointed or removed so it
passes. Order matters — the guard is what prevents the eighth, and "nothing
prevented the next one" has been this programme's actual failure mode often
enough to be a pattern. It is the same move as the conflation detector that
landed in sprint 4: convert a caught mistake into a structural assertion
rather than into care.

(b) Repointing is a judgement about intent, not a deletion sweep. Where the
intended target is evident, point at it; where it is not, remove the edge
and record what was removed and why. Do not invent a node to satisfy an
edge.

(c) `ire.design_graph_v2` may proceed while this is fixed. Its dependency
was never gating anything, which is precisely the finding.

### V4. Poppler MAY be installed — and the floor is re-measured before it measures anything

`pdftoppm` may be installed so R2b can resolve sources `sips` cannot. But
installing it CHANGES THE INSTRUMENT, and §U2's calibration rests on a
measured round-trip floor of exactly 0.0 obtained from the current one.

(a) the §U2 premise guard is re-run on the new rasteriser **before any
comparison produces a verdict**;

(b) **if the floor is no longer 0.0, §U2 is void by its own terms** — it
says so explicitly — and R2b's threshold returns here for recalibration
against the new floor. It does not get quietly re-derived in the file;

(c) every verdict records which rasteriser produced it and what that
rasteriser's measured floor is. A result that cannot name its instrument is
not a measurement;

(d) `pdf_to_png`'s inert `dpi` argument is a recorded instrument limit. If
poppler makes the argument real, that is a behaviour change to the
measurement path and it is disclosed in the close report, not absorbed.

The principle: **the instrument is measured before it measures anything.**

`SIGNED: BBrose (PROJECT_OWNER, via Cowork question session)  DATE: 2026-08-17`

## §W — POST-SPRINT-7: THE FOUR RULINGS THE GATE WAS WAITING ON (2026-08-18)

Sprints 5, 6 and 7 landed without an owner round-trip, exactly as §Q intends.
Sprint 7 closed with every gate-read contract wired to a producer and **no
build work queued** — the remaining blockers are rulings, not code. This
section is those rulings. **Owner-answered; do not re-ask.**

### The precedent sprint 7 earned

**A test you wrote proves your code does what you meant. It cannot tell you
that you meant the wrong thing.** Twice in one sprint a producer passed its
own tests and was then refused by the real emitted document — once measuring
a 1.5 pt caption on a schematic thumbnail as if it were container type, once
asserting in a docstring AND a test name that a `TextRun` carries no clip
path when `Group` and `Image` both do and the emitter puts a real one on
`BACK_DIRECT_PRINT`. Both were caught by the artefact, not the suite.
**Run a producer against the real emitted artefact before believing it, and
when the artefact disagrees, find out why BEFORE touching the expectation.**
Related and also now binding: **a work-item label that names nothing real is
a stale claim.** Carry work-item names in a file and check them against
`git log` before citing one.

### W1. A FULL-SCALE BACK PANEL SHALL BE EMITTED

The back panel currently exists only inside the presentation sheet's 92×46 mm
schematic strip: body copy at `2.0 * k` pt with `k` floored at 0.5 — so the
ingredient list renders at **1.0 pt**, truncated to **70 characters**,
headings to 40. Nothing in this repo measures it. `container_production_method`
does not see it either, because it only inspects `product-name*` runs.

**This is a product gap, not a measurement gap, and that is why it is being
built rather than excused.** A client-approvable deliverable cannot represent
its regulatory panel as a 1 pt truncated diagram. The panel that carries the
ingredient list, the directions and the regulatory copy is the one a printer
and a regulator will read first.

(a) emit a **full-scale back panel at true dimensions with untruncated copy**
— a real surface, not a strip glyph. The strip stays as it is; it is a map
and it is fine as a map;

(b) once it exists, the typography axis measures it like any other surface.
Until it exists the axis stays UNMEASURED and blocking on that surface — the
current "excluded the strip, and here is how many runs that was" record is
correct and stays;

(c) **do not measure the strip harder.** Measuring a diagram of a panel more
precisely produces a more precise answer to a question nobody asked. The
sprint-7 1.5 pt finding is the reference case;

(d) the truncation limits (70 / 40 characters) are a strip constraint and
must not follow the copy onto the full-scale panel. If real copy does not fit
the real panel, that is a finding and it comes back here — it is not solved
by truncating.

### W2. THE PRINT-METHOD TABLE GOVERNS MINIMUM TEXT SIZE, ON ALL RUNS

Four constants disagreed: 5.0 pt (`visual_quality_gate.THRESHOLDS["typography_min_text_pt"]`,
currently deciding the container), 5.5 pt (`compose_vector_art._MIN_TEXT_PT`),
4.5 pt (`production.py` / `production_readiness.py`), and the
`container_production_method` capability table (EMBOSS/DEBOSS 8.0;
HOT_STAMP/CAP_HOT_STAMP 6.0; SCREEN/PAD/CAP_PRINT/SHRINK_SLEEVE 5.0;
ADHESIVE/WRAP_LABEL 4.0; BOTTOM_INKJET_CODE 2.0) — applied only to
`product-name*` runs.

**The table is right and the flat number is wrong, and the repo already knew
it.** Minimum legible size is a physical property of how the type is put onto
the substrate. You cannot emboss at 5 pt, and forbidding a 2.0 pt bottom
inkjet code that is standard practice is a false FAIL.

(a) the capability table governs, extended from `product-name*` runs to **all
runs**, matched by the print method recorded for the surface the run sits on;

(b) where the print method is **unrecorded**, the flat 5.0 pt applies as a
**fallback**, and the record must say it is a fallback. A fallback reported as
a measurement is the defect class this programme keeps catching;

(c) the other constants keep their own domains — 5.5 pt for vector artwork,
4.5 pt for dielines — and each must state the domain it governs, in the file,
the way §U required of the silhouette tolerances. **A constant that does not
name its domain is a conflation waiting to happen**;

(d) this is a policy choice, not a measurement. Status `OWNER_CALIBRATED`.

### W3. OVERLAP: TYPE-OVER-TYPE BLOCKS; TYPE-OVER-ARTWORK DOES NOT

One ruling, covering `blocking_overlaps` on the composition axis and
`overlapping_text` on the typography axis. They were the same question asked
about two axes.

(a) **two text runs whose geometry intersects BLOCK**, at any opacity. Two
names on top of each other is never intentional;

(b) **type set over a rule, motif, medallion or colour field does NOT block.**
That is the composition working as drawn, and the A2 rosette and the FB3093
lids depend on it;

(c) **any element crossing the artboard edge blocks**, separately and
already measured as `elements_outside_artboard`;

(d) refusing to supply `0` for these fields was correct and is upheld. Now
that the rule exists, measure them; do not default them. If a case does not
fit (a)–(c) cleanly, it is UNMEASURED and blocking, and it comes back here.

**Not chosen, and why it matters:** the legibility-based variant — blocking
only when an overlap materially impairs reading — is the better rule and is
not available, because no instrument in this repo can measure "impairs". If
one is ever built, W3 is amendable through this sheet.

### W4. THE GATE-A DIVIDER AND THE CONTAINER FRONT RULE ARE DIFFERENT OBJECTS

`ai8_color.DIVIDER_WIDTH_PT` = 0.362384 pt (0.128 mm), read out of an accepted
proof's content stream and verified at Gate A. `compose_container.py:175`
`rule-front-single` = 0.25 mm (0.709 pt). Ratio 1.9556. **They are two
elements, not one, and both numbers stand.**

**Why not reconcile them.** The Gate-A figure came from an ACCEPTED PROOF — a
colour-sheet hairline, in a context that was measured and passed. The front
rule sits above a product name on a container, a different surface with a
different print method. 0.128 mm is at the fine edge of what offset holds
reliably. Moving production artwork onto a number borrowed from another
context, on an assumption that the two are the same object, would be a change
with no evidence behind it. No accepted proof gets reopened on a guess either.

(a) record the two as distinct elements, each naming its context;

(b) **the container front rule owes its own recorded weight rationale.**
"Different objects" is a ruling about identity, not a blessing of 0.25 mm as
a considered value. It is currently an unexplained number and must stop being
one;

(c) if a later proof of the CONTAINER measures its front rule, that
measurement supersedes (b) and this ruling is amendable here.

### W5. PLACEHOLDER TEXT — derived from standing rulings, not a new one

The executor left `placeholder_text_present` unmeasured because a boolean
failing on any placeholder would contradict §B1/§B2. Correct. The rule
follows from those rulings without needing a new policy:

(a) **permitted** placeholders are exactly the ones already ruled: the
back-label EAN (§B1) and the distributor identity (§B2). Both are
clearly-marked and do not gate artwork;

(b) **any other placeholder text drawn on a container FAILS the axis**, and
the finding names the run and the text;

(c) the two disagreeing regexes (`print_data._PLACEHOLDER_RE` matches "N/A",
`production_readiness._PLACEHOLDER_RE` does not) were both written for spec
FIELD VALUES, not for type drawn on a container. **Do not reuse either.** The
container needs its own rule keyed to the permitted list in (a) — a short
allow-list, not a better regex;

(d) adding a placeholder to the permitted list is an owner ruling through
this sheet. An executor may not extend it.

`SIGNED: BBrose (PROJECT_OWNER, via Cowork question session)  DATE: 2026-08-18`

## §X — POST-SPRINT-8: THE RULING THAT WAS NOT IN THE REPOSITORY, AND THE PANEL THAT DOES NOT FIT (2026-08-19)

Sprint 8 discharged all five §W items in nine commits and then reported that
**§W itself had never been committed.** Seven committed source files and five
commit messages named a section the repository did not contain. The executor
found it, refused to fix it — "committing the owner's uncommitted ruling is
the owner's act, not mine" — and queued it. That refusal was correct and is
now precedent. This section answers it, and answers the overflow finding that
§W1(d) was written to produce.

**Owner-answered; do not re-ask.**

### The precedent sprint 8 earned

**An authority is only an authority once it is in the repository.** §W's own
preamble made it binding that *a label naming nothing real is a stale claim*,
and the ruling document was the one place that test was not applied. The
failure was not the executor's: it was the owner channel's. Three things
follow, and they bind the channel that writes these sections, not the session
that builds:

(i) **a citation is a claim about the repository, not about the working tree.**
Before a source file, a docstring or a commit message names a §-section, that
section must be resolvable by `git show HEAD:OWNER_BLOCKER_CLEARANCE.md`;

(ii) **an uncommitted file is lost-able and it is lost silently.** The
sprint-8 mandate was delivered the same way — as an uncommitted edit to
`NEXT_SESSION_LAUNCHER.md` — and survived only because the executor chose to
preserve it verbatim in an appendix rather than overwrite it. Nothing was
lost. It was lost-able;

(iii) **the second half of a probe's silence is the dangerous half.** Sprint 8
also recorded a standalone probe that reported `FIT_UNMEASURED` for a
310-character INCI list because it had no Django bootstrap, so every text
extent was unmeasurable. The code was correct, the record honest, and the
conclusion would have been wrong. §V4's rule — *the instrument is measured
before it measures anything* — extends to probes written to check an
instrument.

### X1. COMMIT §W AS IT STANDS — AUTHORIZED

The working-tree change to `OWNER_BLOCKER_CLEARANCE.md` at the close of
sprint 8 was **159 insertions and 0 deletions**. It adds the §W block and
touches nothing else. It cannot revert WI-A, cannot re-open §W5, and cannot
alter §A–§V.

(a) **§W1–§W5 are final text, not a draft.** They were written as complete
owner rulings, checked against the code they govern before they were written,

and are **not** covered by this authorization. §O/§P govern the `.ai` drift

never commits `OWNER_BLOCKER_CLEARANCE.md` on its own initiative. It reports

### X2. THE BACK PANEL BLOCKS, AND THE COPY IS WHAT CHANGES

§W1(d) fired exactly as intended and produced a real number: the confirmed

WARNINGS, MANUFACTURER and NET CONTENT absent entirely. Today's copy fits

**The block stands. `CONTAINER_BACK_PANEL_COPY_EXCEEDS_PANEL` is correct
behaviour and is not to be softened.** The resolution is that the copy is
written to fit the panel, not that the panel is made to fit the copy:

(a) **no new surface is invented.** ES3083's confirmed zone set is `z_front`,

(d) **the honest risk is recorded here rather than discovered later:** it may

it passes today, it blocks the day the content is real, and that is the
correct pair of behaviours. **Nobody is to make it pass on real copy by any
means other than shorter real copy.**

## §Y — POST-SPRINT-9: WHO MAY LOOSEN A FLOOR, AND WHAT A TEST THAT READS A FILE IS WORTH (2026-08-19)

Sprint 9 discharged X1 at `dcc518c`, WI-F at `f6aaffb` and closed at `7958056`.
Mutation M3 — popping `minimum_text_size_pt` off each built method — was
survived by **all 161 pre-existing tests** and killed only by the eight new
ones, with the headline that a surface pinned at a 12.0 pt floor emitted 8.0 pt
type and reported `below_size_floor: False`. A four-point-under violation
reported as a pass. That is what X3(b) was written to produce and it produced
it.

**Owner-answered; do not re-ask.**

### The precedent sprint 9 earned

**Coverage by execution is not coverage.** A committed docstring in
`test_container_text_floor.py` says nothing exercises `reconstruct_container`.
It was wrong, and the way it was wrong is the lesson: `ContainerFlowTests`
drives that function indirectly through
`aria.resume_after_container_profile` in at least three tests. The function was
**unasserted, not unreached** — and those are materially different facts that a
line-coverage number cannot tell apart. M3 survived precisely there: executed
on every run, asserted by nobody. **Never say "no test reaches X" when what you
mean is "no test asserts anything about X", and never accept execution as
evidence of coverage.**

Second, and smaller: **a rule you wrote down is not a rule you have applied.**
Sprint 8's queue block named the uncommitted-file exposure as *"lost-able, and
it would have been lost silently"*, and sprint 9 then destroyed an uncommitted
launcher by rewriting it without a backup. Naming an exposure does not remove
one. The structural fix is in Y4.

### Y1. A ZONE MAY TIGHTEN A FLOOR. IT MAY NOT LOOSEN ONE.

`apps/ire/container_production_method.py:182` currently reads
`z.get("min_text_size_pt") or defaults.get("min_text_pt")`. A zone-level value
beats the §W2 capability table, nothing records that it did, and the record
still stamps `constraints_source: INFERRED_NONAUTHORITATIVE_TYPE_DEFAULT` —
so the provenance field is false in exactly the case that matters.

**§W2 bound the capability table because the table describes what the PRESS can
hold.** A zone is a region of a design. It can legitimately be stricter than
the press. It cannot be more permissive than the press, because that is a claim
about manufacturing capability, and the record's own `authority_state` on every
one of these methods is `INFERRED_NONAUTHORITATIVE` or
`USER_REQUESTED_UNVERIFIED`. Neither has standing to make it. Therefore:

(a) **the effective floor is the LARGER of the zone value and the table value**
when both are present. A zone value above the table tightens and is honoured.
A zone value below the table is **rejected as the floor** — the table value
stands;

(b) **a rejected zone value is not discarded silently.** It is recorded, with
both numbers and the reason, so the disagreement is visible. §W2's rule that a
fallback must be *reported* as a fallback applies with equal force to an
override that was refused;

(c) **`or` becomes `is not None` on all three numeric floors** —
`minimum_line_weight_mm`, `minimum_text_size_pt` and
`registration_tolerance_mm`. The two sibling fields on the same record
(`permitted_color_count`, `maximum_coverage`) already do this correctly, so the
file is internally inconsistent and the inconsistency sits exactly on the
fields where `0.0` is both meaningful and dangerous. **A zone floor of 0.0
currently falls through to the default and nothing says so.** Whether 0.0 is
then honoured is settled by (a): a 0.0 minimum is below any table value, so it
is refused and recorded — it never silently clears every run;

(d) **`constraints_source` must stop lying.** When any value on the record did
not come from the type default, that field says so and names which. A
provenance field that is a constant is not provenance. Likewise `floor_source`
must distinguish table / zone-tightened / fallback — not merely table vs
fallback;

(e) this is a **statistic-scoped ruling** in the sense of §U's preamble. It
binds the minimum-text-size floor and, because (c) touches them, the line-weight
and registration floors as to the `is not None` defect only. It does **not**
authorize a general zone-beats-table or table-beats-zone policy anywhere else
in the repo. Anything outside these three fields is a separate ruling.

### Y2. THE SOURCE-STRING GUARDS STAY, AND THEY DECLARE WHAT THEY ARE

The two tests in `test_container_text_floor.py` that assert a literal appears
in a file survived M3 intact. That is not a defect in them — that is what a
source-string guard does, and they do catch the one thing they are for:
somebody deleting the call site outright. Cheap, and genuinely load-bearing.

**The defect is that their names claim more than they check.**
`test_the_gate_no_longer_carries_a_second_copy_of_the_number` reads as a
behavioural assertion, so a survivor report containing it reads wrong.

(a) **keep both.** Retiring them buys nothing and loses a real check;

(b) **every source-string guard in this repo carries a name and a docstring
that say it is a source-string guard** — that it asserts the presence or
absence of a literal in a file and asserts nothing about behaviour;

(c) **a source-string guard may never be cited as evidence that a BEHAVIOUR is
covered**, in a close report, a ledger row, a tracker validation count or a
mutation-survivor analysis. If a mutation survives and the only tests touching
that code are source-string guards, the correct statement is "no behavioural
coverage", not "covered";

(d) this rule is general. It is not scoped to these two tests.

### Y3. FINDING 5 IS TRIAGED BEFORE IT IS TOUCHED

`reconstruct_container`'s fail-closed `if image is None` branch may be dead:
`PackagingOutput.approved_image` is a non-null `ForeignKey`
(`apps/pipeline/models.py:429`), so no persisted output can reach it.

**Do not delete it and do not write a test for it until you know which it is.**
Sprint 8's second mutation survivor is the governing precedent: a test for an
impossible input is a test that will pass forever and prove nothing, and the
right answer there was to delete the guard. But that precedent cuts both ways
and the question is factual:

(a) establish whether `reconstruct_container` is **ever** called with an
unsaved or partially-constructed `PackagingOutput`, or with any object that is
not a `PackagingOutput` at all. Read the call sites; do not infer from the
model;

(b) if the branch is provably unreachable, **delete it** and record the proof
— the call-site enumeration, not the model constraint alone;

(c) if it is reachable, it gets a behavioural test and stays;

(d) `IntegrityError` while trying to reach a branch is evidence about the
database, not about the code path. It is a hint, not the answer.

### Y4. SPRINT 10 — RULINGS FIRST, THEN THE FRONT TYPE

Three work items, in this order. **Nothing from §X2 is built. The hairline
finding waits for sprint 11.**

**WI-0 (first, before any code): commit `NEXT_SESSION_LAUNCHER.md` at sprint
START.** The sprint-9 loss is structural, not a lapse of care, and the fix is
structural: the launcher is committed as the first act of every sprint, so the
handoff document is never the thing standing between an uncommitted edit and a
rewrite. This is a **standing rule from here on**, and it applies to

**WI-G — implement Y1 and Y2.** The zone floor rule with its recording, the

and `floor_source` honesty fix, and the source-string guard labelling. Y1(a)
needs a negative control: a zone value BELOW the table must be shown refused,

**WI-H — Y3's triage, and the false docstring.** Fix the
`test_container_text_floor.py` docstring to say **unasserted, not unreached**,
and name `ContainerFlowTests` as the indirect driver. Then Y3.

**WI-I — wire the container's own front type to a surface.** `front-brand` at
2.58 pt and `front-support` at 3.4 pt sit outside any
`Decoration` / `motif-` / `Surface-` group, so §W2's per-surface floor has
never reached them. WI-F's tests pin the hero-surface path, which is what makes
this safe to change and observable when you do. **Determine first whether it is
a wiring fix or a scope question, and say which before you start.** If it turns

(a) **the red count is 5 failed / 3 skipped / 16 keys / 69 occurrences / 4

(b) **`pc.vqr3_artwork_composition` stays at 0.** V3 §10 admits no

(c) **no chained fixes** (§V precedent 2). Findings get recorded, not fixed.

### Y5. THE SPRINT-9 LAUNCHER RESTORATION IS BYTE-VERIFIED — the label may be upgraded

The appendix in `NEXT_SESSION_LAUNCHER.md` labelled **"RESTORED FROM THIS

        owner original (77 lines)

Two notes, both to the credit of the close report. First, the bound was

## §Z — POST-SPRINT-10: THE UNIT, AND THE DETERMINATION THAT POINTED THE WRONG WAY (2026-08-19)

Sprint 10 was four work items and **two of them ended in findings that
contradicted the brief that ordered them.** That is the sprint working, not
failing. WI-H was sent to consider deleting a branch and proved it reachable —
after a first probe said "never executed", which was wrong in the direction
that would have deleted live code. WI-I was sent to wire front type to a
surface and found the type already wired, then found something much larger
underneath it.

**WI-I's finding is the most valuable thing this arc has produced. Its
conclusion is also backwards, and this section reverses it.**

**Owner-answered; do not re-ask.**

### The precedent sprint 10 earned, stated against sprint 10 itself

**§W's rule was: run the producer against the real emitted artefact, and when
the artefact disagrees, find out why BEFORE touching the expectation.** WI-I's
determination did the opposite in the one place it counted. It reasoned about
what the number *means* — "2.115 mm, which is 6.00 pt printed" — instead of
what the emitter *does* with it. The emitter does this, and there is no third
reading:

```
apps/ire/emitters/pdf_ai.py:184   c.setFont(face, node.size_pt)      # no * mm
apps/ire/emitters/pdf_ai.py:66    def X(x_mm): return x_mm * mm      # converted
apps/ire/emitters/pdf_ai.py:360   c.setLineWidth(stroke.width_mm * mm)  # converted
```

The only `c.scale` in the file is inside the barcode branch. `_draw_text`
applies none. So `size_pt` reaches the PDF as literal points while every
geometric quantity beside it is multiplied by 2.8346.

**The emitted artefact really does carry 2.58 pt type. The axis was right the
whole time.** Had the determination been acted on — §W2's domain narrowed, or
the floor loosened, on the strength of "type that physically passes" — this
system would have shipped genuinely illegible 2.6 pt type on a container front
with a green typography axis. That is the precise failure this programme
exists to prevent, and it arrived dressed as a careful measurement.

**Two claims that cannot both be true is a finding about your instrument, and
so is one claim that contradicts an artefact.** The close report already
learned the first half from WI-H's probe. This is the second half.

**None of that diminishes the work.** Stopping and queueing instead of building
is what surfaced this at all — a wiring fix would have buried it — and the
scale-dependence table and the 30-run census are correct, are kept, and are
what made the diagnosis possible.

### Z1. THE UNIT CONVENTION IS LAW, AND THE COMPOSER IS THE DEFECT

(a) **A field suffixed `_mm` is millimetres and the emitter converts it. A
field suffixed `_pt` is points and the emitter does not.** The emitter honours
this exactly and its docstring states it. `size_pt` is points. **The emitter is
correct and is not to be changed** — in particular, `setFont(face,
node.size_pt * mm)` is forbidden. It would make the field name a lie and
silently reinterpret every literal in the repo, turning the 9.0, 3.4 and 3.0 in
`_front_typography` and the 4.0 / `8 * _k` in `compose_container` into 25.5,
9.6, 8.5 and larger;

(b) **`_front_typography` violates the convention and is the defect.** It
derives `size_pt` from `zh`, which is `float(zone["height"]) * s` — a scaled
millimetre length. **No `size_pt` anywhere in this repo may be derived from a
millimetre quantity.** A type size is chosen as type;

(c) **the proof is inside the same function and it is decisive.**
`front-support` is `max(3.4, zh * 0.034)`; at every scale in use the literal
wins, so it reads 3.4 and is scale-INVARIANT. `front-brand` is `zh * 0.05`
with no literal floor at all, so it reads 2.5803 at hero and is
scale-DEPENDENT. **`front-brand` is the only run in that function with no
literal floor, and it is exactly the one recorded below floor.** Two runs, one
function, one document, two different behaviours — the units are not merely
wrong, they are not consistent with each other;

(d) **the scale-dependence finding stands and is a second, independent
defect.** One physical zone drawn at hero 1.22 and flat ~1.55 produced 2.5803
and 3.2686 for the same physical type. A measurement that changes when the
drawing is enlarged is not measuring the product. Fixing (b) fixes this too,
because a chosen point size carries no `s`;

(e) **§W2's domain is NOT narrowed, no floor is lowered, and the axis is not
touched.** The instrument was right. §T's oldest rule applies without
qualification: when a metric fails, you fix the thing being measured.

### Z2. THE FRONT IS CORRECTED TO INTENT, THEN COMES BACK FOR EYES

(a) **give `front-brand` an explicit point size at approximately 6.0 pt** —
the value the millimetre arithmetic was reaching for (2.115 mm ÷ 0.35278 =
5.995 pt) — chosen as a type size, not derived;

(b) **remove every `zh`-derived `size_pt` in `_front_typography`.** Where a
literal floor already dominates, the literal becomes the size outright; the
`max(..., zh * f)` form goes. It is currently doing nothing except waiting to
become wrong at a different scale;

(c) **the changed front is an owner-eyes item.** Append it to
`OWNER_REVIEW_QUEUE.md` with the before/after sizes so the new proportion of
the wordmark against the product-name block and the front rule can be judged.
**Correctness first, aesthetics second — but the aesthetics do come back here,
and the fix is not "accepted" until they have;**

(d) **this is not a redesign.** Do not re-proportion the whole front hierarchy
in the same change. A design pass bundled into a unit fix is unverifiable, and
§V's second precedent forbids the scope growing itself;

(e) **re-run the below-floor census afterwards and report the new count
against 30.** If the number does not fall by the runs you changed, and only by
those, that is a finding.

### Z3. THE FIFTEEN BACK-PANEL RUNS ARE A REAL FAIL AND STAY BLOCKING

The 15 `back-panel-*` runs sit at 5.0 pt against a 6.0 pt floor. They are
untouched by Z1 — 5.0 is a literal, not a `zh` derivation — so this is a
genuine §W2 finding about real printed regulatory copy.

(a) **5.0 pt is §W2(b)'s disclosed FALLBACK**, taken because the composer holds
no production-method record for `BODY_BACK`. **A floor from an actual
capability table outranks a fallback.** That is the whole reason §W2 made the
table the authority, and Y1 has already settled that direction of travel: the
larger floor governs, and a lower number does not get to win by being the
default;

(b) **the copy is set at 6.0 pt or larger and the runs stop failing that way**,
not by re-examining the 6.0;

(c) **then re-measure the panel against §X2 and expect the overflow to get
worse.** It will: taller type on a fixed 19.0 × 39.30 mm column can only
reduce the characters that fit. **That is the honest outcome and it is not a
reason to reconsider (b).** §X2 already ruled that the copy is what changes;

(d) if the resulting overflow is the thing that finally proves mandatory copy
cannot fit the panel, **that is §X2(d) firing and it returns to this sheet with
the numbers.** Do not pre-solve it, and do not let it argue backwards into a
smaller floor.

### Z4. SPRINT 11

**WI-J — Z1 and Z2.** The composer fix, the census re-run, the queue append
with before/after sizes. **A negative control is required:** a `size_pt`
derived from a millimetre quantity must be shown to be catchable, so that
Z1(b) is a guard and not an intention.

**WI-K — Z3.** The back-panel copy at 6.0 pt or larger, then the §X2
re-measurement with the new overflow stated in mm and characters.

**WI-L — the hairline zero-height defect**, deferred from §Y4.
`geometry_report._path_bbox` never consults stroke width. Replace it with a
fix, not a wider tolerance — the same defect is shared with
`elements_outside_artboard` where it could change an answer.

(a) **§Y2 is IN FORCE BUT NOT DISCHARGED and must not be reported as applied.**
58 pre-existing source-string guards in `accounts` / `dielines` / `pipeline`
remain a counted backlog. The committed census is the authority on that number
— not an ad-hoc script — and the close report was right to say so, right to
keep the 61 → 94 → 62 → 64 history, and right that three of those four were
numbers it could have reported instead;

(b) **the ledger's five sprint-10 hashes are not five things built.** WI-I's
hash is a committed determination. The warning in that file stays and is not to
be tidied away;

(c) red count unchanged: 5 failed / 3 skipped / 16 keys / 69 occurrences / 4
files. `pc.vqr3_artwork_composition` stays at 0. No chained fixes; findings are
recorded, not fixed.

## §AA — POST-SPRINT-11

**PRECEDENT, and it is the whole of this section's reason to exist: a
constraint the pipeline never reaches is a constraint nobody has tested.**

WI-K wired `BODY_BACK`'s capability table to the composer correctly, proved it
node-for-node against the pre-fix module, and then measured the one thing that
matters most about it: **on today's live output the change does nothing.**
`propose_zones` gives this bottle `screen_printing` on both faces, `BODY_BACK`
resolves to `SCREEN_PRINT`, and `SCREEN_PRINT`'s `min_text_pt` is 5.0 — the
same number as §W2(b)'s fallback. The whole 6.0 pt census, the fifteen failing
runs, the NET CONTENT drop, all of it comes from a **hand-written `HOT_STAMP`
fixture in `test_back_panel.py`**. Saying so, in the same document as the
result, is the reason this sprint's work can be trusted. A report that stopped
at "the back panel now carries its own floor" would have been true and would
have left the owner believing a production surface had changed.

The rule that follows: **when a fix's effect on production output is zero,
that sentence goes in the close report next to the fix, not in a footnote.**
And a fixture-supplied constraint is named as a fixture every time its numbers
are quoted.

Sprint 11 also produced the cleanest instance yet of the programme working on
itself. §Y2 — a rule this executor wrote one sprint ago — caught this
executor's own new test file carrying two undeclared source-string guards, in
0.7 seconds, on all three of its in-force assertions. The red count went 5 → 8
and the cause was the author's. **It was reported as the author's, in the
sprint title, before it was fixed.** Registering the two guards would have been
wrong twice over — the register only shrinks, and `apps/ire` is recorded as
fully converted — so they were renamed and declared instead. That is a rule
being *applied*, not a rule being *stated*, and §Y4's "if you cannot say the
number, you have not applied the rule" is now discharged in the direction that
costs the author something.

### AA1. THE BACK PANEL — THE COPY IS COMPRESSED, ON-PACK, AND THE BAN STANDS

§X2(d) has fired with real numbers and this is it returning. **The answer is
the one §X2 named: the copy changes.** No carton, no leaflet, no wrap, no new
zone, no second surface. That ban is not lifted and it is not weakened by the
overflow being large.

(a) **Sprint 12 writes compressed on-pack copy.** INCI to the legal minimum
that a 30 ml cosmetic dropper must carry; DIRECTIONS shortened; anything that
is not legally required to sit on the container comes off it. The target is
that the panel **fits at its own resolved floor** with every mandatory
declaration present — `NET CONTENT` above all, since that is the section the
6.0 pt case drops;

(b) **the panel keeps blocking until it genuinely fits.** No shrink-to-fit, no
character truncation, no floor drop, no section priority order that lets a
mandatory section fall below a cut line — every one of those is already
forbidden by §X2 and none of them becomes permissible because a real attempt
was made. `CONTAINER_BACK_PANEL_COPY_EXCEEDS_PANEL` is correct and stays;

(c) **"legal minimum" is a claim that needs a source.** Do not compress by
taste. Each cut is recorded with the reason it is permissible — an INCI name
that has a shorter permitted form, a sentence that is marketing rather than
required, a section that regulation allows off-pack. **Where you cannot source
the permission, do not make the cut**; record the section as `SOURCE_REQUIRED`
and leave it in. A shorter panel bought by deleting something mandatory is the
same defect as a lower floor, wearing different clothes;

(d) **the five characters stay open and stay stated.** §X2's headline 613 is
not reproducible from anything committed; the reconstruction lands at 608 and
reproduces every other structural number §X2 gives. **Refusing to invent copy
until the number matched was correct.** WARNINGS and MANUFACTURER were not
supplied with this ruling and are not to be written from imagination — they are
owner-supplied strings and they are still owed. Until they exist, the
reconstruction is the authority and it says so in its own docstring;

(e) **report the fit at BOTH floors.** 5.0 (what ships today) and 6.0 (what a
hot stamp would impose), in mm and in characters, against the same document.
One number is the live answer and the other is the answer this bottle gets the
day AA3 resolves the other way. Neither is the whole finding on its own.

### AA2. THE FRONT IS RENDERED BEFORE IT IS JUDGED

WI-J's restraint was correct — §Z2(d) kept a design pass out of a unit fix, and
leaving the changed proportion visible rather than compensating for it silently

(a) **Sprint 12 renders the changed front at TRUE SCALE, at both panel scales

(d) **do not re-proportion anything in sprint 12.** The render, and only the

### AA3. `BODY_BACK`'s PRINT METHOD IS UNCONFIRMED AND MUST SAY SO

Neither `SCREEN_PRINT` nor `HOT_STAMP` is owner-confirmed for the back of this

## §AB — POST-SPRINT-12 RULINGS (WI-0 … WI-S)

**Anchor the check** — `grep -c '^## §AB'` — for the same reason §AA gave: this
section quotes its own heading and an unanchored count returns more than 1. The
gate that reads this file must not be an instrument that counts its own
instructions.

### AB0 — the precedent, and the law it produces

The sentence sprint 12 is remembered for is WI-O's, and it is taken here as
**praise, not correction**:

> *"**It does not fit, and it cannot be made to fit by writing.** The sections
> that are not the ingredient list already exceed the panel on their own."*

Sixteen lines at 5.0 pt against a document that needs thirty-nine. Break every
rule at once — including the allergen deletion he refused to perform — and the
panel is **still 30.317 mm over**. Give the whole surface to INCI and nothing
else, and **17 of 20 ingredients** fit at 5.0 pt, **11 of 20** at 6.0. That is
not a copywriting result. It is an arithmetic one, and it was obtained by
measuring rather than by trying harder.

Three more of the same kind, all from this sprint: the leading *"was never
tight"* (3.0047 em, not 1.06 — the comment described an intention the code
never executed); the grep *"would have found 17 of 21 and missed the only one
that matters"*; and the front's −1.389 mm overlap, which a negative control at
`dd0d60b^` proved **WI-J did not cause**.

So the law §AB adds, and it binds every future ruling in this file including
mine:

**AB0(a) — an impossibility is a measurement, not an opinion.** Once a
quantity has been measured and the measurement stands, the question is closed
until a *different measurement* reopens it. Effort does not reopen it.
Restating the requirement does not reopen it. "Try again with better copy" is
not a rebuttal to 30.317 mm.

**AB0(b) — a ruling that contradicts a measurement must NAME the measurement it
is betting against, and must be written so the bet can be LOST.** AB1 below is
exactly such a ruling. It is mine, it is against the evidence, and it is
written so that the next measurement can defeat it without anyone having to
overturn an owner decision to say so.

**AB0(c) — a negative control is what separates a defect from a regression.**
WI-M's is the model: the overlap existed before the change that was suspected
of causing it, so the change was exonerated by evidence rather than by
argument. Any future claim that work item X *broke* Y carries the same burden.

### AB1 — the back panel: a SECOND LAYER on the same bottle, and the reduction runs anyway

**This ruling was answered once and revised before it entered the repository,
and the revision is recorded rather than hidden.** The first answer was *reduce
the mandatory set, single surface stands*. It was replaced because the option
set I was given was incomplete, not because the reasoning changed — see AB1(g).
Nothing here was ever committed, so this is a correction made before the fact;
had it been committed, it would have required a new section instead.

**The ruling: the label becomes MULTI-LAYER — a peel-reveal or booklet label on
the same bottle — and the owner-sourced reduction of the mandatory set runs
anyway.** Both. Not one as a fallback for the other.

**AB1(a) — this does not lift §X2's ban; it corrects what the ban was about.**
§X2 banned a **separate physical object**: a carton, a leaflet in a box, an
outer wrap. A peel-reveal label is one label, applied once, to one bottle. It
adds no component to the pack, no second pick in assembly, and no second
artwork carrier. **The carton and the leaflet-in-a-box remain banned.** The
larger container remains rejected — the geometry is settled and re-deriving it
would invalidate every measurement in the repository to solve a problem the
label solves.

**AB1(b) — the manufacturability is UNCONFIRMED and must say so, in exactly the
form WI-N built.** §C2 withdrew supplier outreach permanently, so no one can
confirm that our converter runs a multi-layer label at this size. That is not a
reason to avoid the decision; it is a reason to record the decision at its true
provenance. **`OWNER_DIRECTED` / `UNCONFIRMED`, and the axis stays blocking**
until a real supplier confirms it. A target we have chosen and cannot yet
verify is an honest state; a target we avoid choosing because verification is
unavailable is paralysis.

**AB1(c) — the reduction runs regardless, because a second layer is not a
licence to stop editing.** The smallest lawful mandatory set is the right set
on one layer or two. What changes is that the reduction no longer has to close
a twenty-three line gap on its own, which is the thing WI-O measured as
impossible.

**AB1(d) — the reduction is measured, never assumed.** When my cut list
arrives it is fed through the same instrument that produced the 39/48 figures,
and the answer is a number. If the reduced set still does not fit **the
available layers**, that is the result, it is reported as a result, and **it is
not an invitation to compress what remains.** §AA1's compression ruling is
spent — WI-O spent it, and it bought one line of a twenty-three line gap.

**AB1(e) — the cut list does not exist yet, and that does not block the
sprint.** What can be built without me is the instrument and the *informed*
question: for each mandatory section, its line cost at both floors, and the
subsets that fit a given surface budget. I cannot cut sensibly against a
39-line total; I can cut against a per-section ledger. **Build the ledger. It
is the deliverable, not the cuts** — and **the surface budget is a PARAMETER of
the ledger, not a constant baked into it**, so the same instrument answers the
one-layer and two-layer questions without being rewritten.

**AB1(f) — the layer count is NOT yet a number.** Two is the working
assumption and it is not ruled. The ledger reports what each budget buys; the
count follows from the ledger. **Do not build anything that assumes exactly
two.**

**AB1(g) — why the first answer was replaced, recorded because AB0(b) demands
it.** I ruled *reduce the set* while WI-O's measurement said the
non-ingredient sections alone overflow. I named that bet and wrote it to be
losable, which was correct procedure applied to an option set that was missing
the option the market actually uses. A reduction of a genuinely mandatory set

worth a few lines against a gap of twenty-three. **The bet was losable and I
could see it losing, so I am not spending a sprint proving it.** AB0(a) applies

impossibility is to change the constraint, not to test the measurement again.

**AB1(d) — every removal will carry a source, and unsourceable removals will be
marked, not made.** §AA1's `SOURCE_REQUIRED` discipline survives this ruling
intact. I am reducing what is *claimed to be mandatory*, which is a sourcing
question, not deleting text because it is long.

**AB1(e) — the STRICT-vs-CITED question is DECLINED, as instructed.** The
executor measured the difference at **23 characters and exactly 0.0 mm at both
floors** and wrote *"do not spend a ruling on it."* Ruling declined on the

**AB1(f) — WARNINGS and MANUFACTURER are still mine, and they now have a

### AB4 — sprint 13 scope: WI-0, WI-T, WI-U, WI-V, WI-W, WI-X

## §AC — sprint 13 close: the metric floor binds, the contract stays shut, a section may split, and the cause gets the node

**Anchor.** Written after reading the sprint-13 close report and verifying it
against the repository at `dd3cbd2`. Six commits, `2593528` → `dd3cbd2`,
confirmed by hash. §AB is committed and this file is additive-only, so §AC does
**not** edit §AB — it corrects §AB by naming the defects and their line
numbers. AC5 does that, and **two of the three defects it corrects are mine.**

This section rules four things the executor correctly refused to rule for
himself, discharges one owner question that has now been deferred three times,
and sets sprint 14.

### AC0 — three laws

**AC0(a) — a measurement true of the STRING is not true of the DESIGN.**

WI-V measured 1.06 em twice and got two honest answers. The **metric** floor —
the face's own line box, true of any name set in that face — overlaps by
**0.959 mm**. The **ink** floor — these specific glyphs, rasterised — clears by
**1.073 mm**. The difference is 2.032 mm, which is 0.64 em, which is *exactly
the descender the word `Rose` does not have.*

Both numbers are correct. Only one of them is a property of the design. A
measurement taken on the glyphs currently in the string expires the moment the
string changes; a measurement taken on the line box does not. **When two floors
disagree, the floor that survives a change of content binds. The other is
recorded as an observation and never as a permission.** An ink clearance is a
fact about a word. A design cannot be built on a fact about a word.

**AC0(b) — a count I quote is a measurement, and it must be re-taken after the
thing it counts changes.**

I wrote "217 insertions" for §AB v1, then added roughly fifty-two lines to AB1
in the revision, then shipped the 217 into two files. The measured number is
**269**. This is precisely the defect WI-S found in the executor one sprint
earlier — a count quoted from a draft rather than re-measured after the thing
it counts changed — and this time the executor found it in me. A number carried
forward from a draft is not a measurement; it is a memory of one. **Every count
that appears in a close report, a queue entry, a launcher or a ruling is taken
from the tool at the moment of writing, against the final artefact, not against
the draft that motivated it.** This law binds me exactly as hard as it binds
the executor, and AC7(j) puts a re-measurement step in sprint 14's close.

**AC0(c) — in an additive-only file, a correction is a new section that names
the defect by line number.**

Quietly writing the right text in a later section, while the wrong text is
still readable above it with no pointer between them, is worse than the
original error: it produces two authorities that disagree and gives a reader no
way to tell which one is live. §X says an authority is only an authority once
it is in the repository; AC0(c) adds that a *superseded* authority is only
superseded once the repository says so, at the line where it sits.

### AC1 — leading: THE METRIC FLOOR BINDS. 1.06 em FAILS.

**The ruling: the metric floor is the constraint. At 1.06 em the line boxes
overlap by 0.959 mm. That is a FAIL. The leading rises until the metric floor
clears, and the number it must clear is 1.362 em.**

§AB3 said the verdict returns as §AC. Here it is.

**AC1(a) — why the metric floor and not the ink floor.** AC0(a) is the general
law; here is the specific consequence. The ink clearance of 1.073 mm is real,
and it is a property of the strings `Rose` and `Damascena` — neither of which
has a descender. AB2(f) has already ruled that this name is the fixed point
**for this name**, and that the next SKU will have a different one. The ink
floor therefore passes today and dies on the first product name containing a
`g`, `j`, `p`, `q` or `y`, with nothing in the pipeline to notice. That is not
a constraint. That is a coincidence with a measurement next to it.

**AC1(b) — 1.362 em is a floor, not the setting.** Clearing zero is not a
design. The floor says only which values are legal.

**AC1(c) — the setting is 2.0 em, and this is a bet I am naming so it can be
lost.** WI-V rendered three values at true scale: 1.06 (now dead), 2.0, and
3.0047. Both survivors clear the metric floor. I am picking **2.0 em** for two
reasons, and against one measurement.

*For:* 3.0047 em exists only because a comment was wrong — AB3 correctly
allowed that an accidental provenance carries no aesthetic penalty, but it
carries no aesthetic credit either. And three ems of leading between the two
lines of a two-line lockup, on a zone 42.3 mm tall whose lower 45% is already
empty, pushes the name apart at exactly the point where AB2(c) recorded that
the composition has an unresolved vertical problem. 2.0 em clears the metric
floor by 0.638 em — enough headroom to absorb a descender without re-ruling —
and keeps the two lines legible as one unit.

*Against:* **I have not seen the 2.0 em render at true scale and I am ruling
from arithmetic.** Per AB0(b) I name the measurement I am betting against: WI-V
produced the comparison and no one has judged it. **The bet loses if the 2.0 em
render shows `Rose` and `Damascena` reading as two unrelated lines rather than
one lockup.** WI-Y presents both survivors at true scale in the review queue;
if 2.0 loses, 3.0047 is the fallback and it needs no new ruling to take.

**AC1(d) — the guard measures metrics, and the negative control proves it.**
A guard that passes 1.06 em because the current glyphs happen not to touch is
the ink floor wearing the metric floor's name. **The control: the same guard,
at the same leading, on a synthetic product name containing a descender, must
return the SAME verdict.** If the verdict changes with the string, the
instrument is measuring ink and the guard is void. §W applies — a test the
executor wrote proves his code does what he meant, and only the control proves
he meant the right thing.

**AC1(e) — the front's hard-coded `product_name` is now load-bearing, and
parameterising it is the named exception to "no chained fixes."** WI-U found
the name hard-coded on the front. AC1(d)'s control is impossible while it is:
you cannot render a descender-bearing name into a string that is not a
variable. This is not opportunistic cleanup nearby a fix — the parameter *is*
the instrument, in the same way WI-T's fix was the instrument. Named as an
exception here so it cannot be cited later as a precedent for tidying.

**AC1(f) — the false comment stays fixed, and 3.0047 em keeps its name.** AB3
required the comment fixed regardless of outcome; it was, and
`NAME_LEADING_EM = 3.0047244094488192` is now a named constant. It stays named
even after 2.0 em is set, as the recorded incumbent. Deleting the number would
delete the evidence that the accident happened.

### AC2 — the zone contract: DO NOT ADD ZONES. BUILD PARAMETRIC.

**The ruling: no zone is added in sprint 14. The `zone_set_hash` is not
re-derived. The `combined_confirmation_hash` is not re-derived. The back-panel
work is built against an ABSTRACT surface list of unbound length.**

confirmed zone set is `z_front` / `z_back` / `z_bottom_code`, and a peel-reveal
or booklet label carries printable faces none of those three names.* §AB1
authorised the multi-layer label; §X2(a) makes adding a zone a CONTRACT change.
So the target is authorised and the surface it needs is not contracted.

**AC2(a) — why not just contract the zones now.** Because I would have to name
them, and naming them fixes the count. AB1(f) says the layer count is not yet a
number and that nothing may be built assuming exactly two. Contracting
`z_inner_front` and `z_inner_back` this sprint would violate AB1(f) *through*
the contract rather than in the code, which is worse, because a contract
carries a hash and a hash carries authority. **A guess with a hash on it is
indistinguishable from a decision.**

**AC2(b) — the abstract form.** The ledger and the construction model take
`(N, B)` — N surfaces, budget B per surface — with **N unbound**. Surfaces are

anywhere in the multi-layer path.** This is deliberate: an invented name in a
comment becomes an invented name in a variable becomes an invented name in an
emitter, and §Y2 already established that source strings drift into looking
like coverage.

intent.** A test asserts the confirmed zone set is **exactly**
`{z_front, z_back, z_bottom_code}` and that **no module emits geometry to any
other zone name.** Its negative control: a deliberately introduced emission to
a fourth name must FAIL the guard. A guard that has never fired on anything is
§AA's case — a constraint the pipeline never reaches is a constraint nobody has
tested.

**AC2(d) — when the contract does open, it opens once and with a number.** The
sequence is: AC3's splitting rule → WI-2A's re-enumeration → a minimum surface
count → an owner ruling in §AD fixing the count → *then* the zone contract,
once, with all hashes re-derived together. Not incrementally. Not
provisionally. **A contract amended twice is a contract that was guessed once.**

### AC3 — a section MAY split across a fold, under four conditions

**The ruling: sections may split.** WI-W's enumeration is decisive and I am not
going to argue with it: INGREDIENTS costs **20 lines at 5.0 pt and 26 at 6.0**,
against a panel holding **16 gapped / 18 ungapped at 5.0 pt and 13 / 15 at
6.0**. It does not fit alone, and therefore appears in **none** of the 30
fitting subsets at 5.0 pt or the 22 at 6.0, out of 63 enumerated exhaustively.
Atomic sections would make INGREDIENTS unplaceable on *any* surface at any
layer count, which turns a layout problem into a false impossibility. A booklet
label that cannot continue a list across a fold is not a booklet.

The four conditions exist because "splitting is allowed" without them is a
licence for the packer to hide overflow:

**AC3(a) — a split occurs only at a line boundary the ledger already models.**
Never mid-word, never mid-token, never at a position the line-counter cannot
name. If the ledger cannot point at the break, the break did not happen in the
model, and a break that is not in the model is not measured.

**AC3(b) — a continuation COSTS A LINE, and the budget is charged for it.**
The receiving surface carries a continuation marker (`INGREDIENTS (cont.)` or
whatever the copy rules settle on), and that marker is debited from that
surface's budget in the ledger. **If a split is free, the arithmetic lies** —
you can manufacture capacity by splitting, and the minimum surface count
becomes a number the model invented rather than measured.

**AC3(c) — surface reading order is DECLARED before the split is computed.**
A split section is only legible if the reader knows which face follows which.
The order is an input to the packer, not an output of it. Declared first, so
the split can be judged against it rather than justified by it.

**AC3(d) — a split is permitted only where it is NECESSARY, never for
balance.** A section that fits entirely on one surface is placed on one
surface. Opportunistic splitting for visual evenness is a layout preference,
and permitting it would let the packer split things to make a tight fit look
comfortable — which is exactly how an overflow becomes invisible. If a
balance-motivated split is ever wanted, it comes back as an owner question.

**AC3(e) — what this unblocks, and what it does not.** With splitting enabled,
39 lines against 16 gapped per surface has a computable minimum. **WI-2A
computes it. WI-2A does not rule it.** The number returns as an owner question
in §AD, because AB1(f) reserved the layer count to me and AC3 does not
transfer it — AC3 supplies the missing rule that makes the number *computable*,
which is a different thing from supplying the number.
