## §AU — OWNER-RULED — the three rows that stop VQR-3, ruled; and the discovery that one of them was two rows wearing one number

**Date issued: 2026-08-21 · Ruled by: BBrose (PROJECT_OWNER, via Cowork
question session) · Consumed by: `NEXT_SESSION_LAUNCHER.md`,
`OWNER_INPUT_MANIFEST.md`**

**Trigger.** WI-3K closed with **zero nodes moved**, claimed that as a §AS2(2)
defect rather than arguing around it, and did the one thing that made the
tranche worth more than a moved percentage: it **measured** which manifest row
actually stops `pc.vqr3_artwork_composition` instead of inheriting the answer.
§AS2(5) had guessed **A1**, the five calibrated photographs. Measured, A1 blocks
`pc.vqr2b_reconstruction_measurement`, and that node is **VALIDATED, 100/100**;
every VQR-3 axis reads the *emitted document*, not a photograph. The rows that
stop it are **C8, C2 and A10** — two of them raised or created by that
measurement, and one of them (A10) a cross-reference that had sat inert in §E
since §E was written because it named no node and no urgency.

Three questions were put and three answered. All three were the recommended
option, which is worth saying plainly rather than treating as agreement: the
recommendation was mine, so the reasoning below has to stand on its own and be
losable on its own, and each ruling carries a named condition under which it is
wrong.

---

### AU0 — the laws this section establishes

**AU0(a) — A reserved row that bundles a STRUCTURE with a CONTENT is two rows,
and the structure is almost always rulable today.**

C8 was recorded as one BLOCKING row: *"the ordered tiers of type on the
container front."* It is two things wearing one number. **How many tiers there
are, and what kind each one is**, is a taste question answerable in a sentence
and reserved under §AE2(c). **The words inside those tiers** are copy, reserved
under §AE2(b) or §AE2(c) depending on what they say, and no sentence from me
makes them safe to invent.

Bundled, the row blocks everything. Split, it blocks one string. Every element
of the front — the tier count, the vertical rhythm, the relative sizes, the
rule, the fitting, the geometry record, the tests, the failure modes — becomes
buildable, and what remains owed shrinks from *a design* to *a line of text*.

Generalisation, and this applies to the whole manifest rather than to C8:
**before a row is filed as BLOCKING, it should be checked for a structure the
owner can rule now.** The manifest currently contains at least three more rows
of this shape. Splitting them is worth a tranche on its own.

**AU0(b) — an owner ruling on a design question is an authority, and it is NOT
a measurement. Recording it as one would be §AK in the opposite direction.**

§AK caught a fabricated quantity claiming authority it did not have. AU2 below
is the inverse risk: a real authority overclaiming its own kind. `0.30 mm` is
ruled, not measured. Its `authority` field must read `OWNER_RULED` and must say
so in words. **§W4(c) survives this section completely intact** — a later proof
that actually MEASURES a printed container front rule supersedes AU2 without
needing to argue with it, and §AE3(d) applies: the ruling is re-derived when the
measurement lands, never grandfathered.

The distinction is not pedantry. A number recorded as measured is not
re-examined; a number recorded as ruled is. Getting this wrong costs the
programme the thing it is built to protect.

**AU0(c) — a standard that nothing can violate is not a standard.**

The permissive C2 set — 0.5× cap height, an 8 mm floor, any ground clearing 3:1
— was rejected for a reason that is not aesthetic. `brand_gov.minimum_component_library`
would then validate against rules that no real placement could fail, and a
component library that cannot go red is a document, not a gate. This is §AA in
brand clothing: **a rule nobody has seen refuse anything is not evidence that
anything is correct.** The conservative set was chosen partly *because* it is
tight enough that the existing emitted logo might fail it — and if it does, that
failure is the most valuable output of the next tranche, not a problem with the
ruling.

**AU0(d) — the row that stops a node is a MEASUREMENT, and the manifest is more
trustworthy now than it was, because a guess inside it was refuted rather than
inherited.**

§AS2(5) guessed A1 in good faith and named it in a committed ruling. WI-3K
measured it and found it false. The correct response to that is not
embarrassment — it is to note that **the manifest is a document full of claims
about causation, most of which have never been measured**, and that each one
should be treated as a prediction until the node it names is actually
approached. A1 is still BLOCKING and still the highest-leverage physical row in
the file; what it is not is the thing standing in front of VQR-3.

---

### AU1 — C8 RULED: one supporting tier, and a rule. The SHAPE is ruled here. The STRING is not, and is not invented.

**The ruling.** The container front, top to bottom, is: the **product name**;
below it a single **fine horizontal rule**; below that **exactly one supporting
line of type**. The decoration element sits above or behind, as it already
does. Nothing else prints on the front.

**The contract, in the form the code consumes:**

```
hierarchy_lines = [
    {"text": <one string, OWNER-OWED>, "rel": <one number, EXECUTOR-RULED>,
     "kind": "descriptor"},
]
```

**`len(hierarchy_lines) == 1` is a CONTRACT number**, in the sense §AD1(d)
established for the four surfaces. A second tier is not a layout tweak; it is a
different front, it changes the rule's job from separating two things to
separating three, and it requires this section to be superseded rather than
extended.

**`rel` is the executor's.** It is dimensionless and it is a typographic
relationship, not a claim about the product. §Z1(b) still binds absolutely: it
may scale a chosen size, and it may never be derived from a zone height or any
other millimetre quantity. The existing floor stays a floor.

**`text` is the owner's and stays owed.** It is filed as a new manifest row
**C9**. It is not §AE2(b) regulated copy — it makes no claim, carries no
warning, declares no quantity — but it is §AE2(c) brand identity, and a front-of-pack
descriptor invented by the executor is taste fabrication on owner-facing output.
See AU5, which is the part of this section with teeth.

**What was rejected, and why.**

*Name only, deleting COPY and DIVIDER.* This was the tempting option: it would
have shrunk the node from five elements to three and let the executor build it
today with no further input at all. It was rejected because **a node that
validates because it got smaller has not been built.** V3 §10 allows no partial
credit precisely so that scope cannot be traded for a green. If the front is
ever reduced to the name alone, that must be a design decision recorded as one,
taken when nothing is waiting on it — not a decision taken because it was the
cheapest way past a gate. The temptation to take it is exactly the reason not
to.

*Descriptor plus volume.* Rejected as self-defeating: a net quantity on the
front is `NET CONTENT`, which is inside `RESERVED_HEADINGS` in
`tools/reserved_copy.py`, which is §AE2(b), which is manifest row **B5**, which
is already BLOCKING. It would have replaced one blocker with two.

*Descriptor plus range name.* Rejected as premature. There is no range. Ruling a
slot for one would put an empty structural commitment on the production path.

**Discharges** the shape half of C8. The string half becomes C9.

---

### AU2 — A10 RULED: the container front rule is **0.30 mm**, on OWNER authority, and the record must say that in those words

**The ruling.** `container_line_weight.ELEMENTS["container_front_rule"]["width_mm"]`
becomes **0.30**. Its `authority` becomes, verbatim in substance:

```
OWNER_RULED — §AU2. A ruled design value, not a measurement.
No manufacturer and no proof has measured this stroke.
Superseded on arrival of any §W4(c) proof that measures a printed
container front rule.
```

`emitted` flips to `True` **only when the branch is genuinely reached** — not as
part of the same edit, and not on the strength of this ruling. `emitted` is a
statement about what production draws, and it is false until production draws
it. Flipping it early would be a §AK-shaped lie in a field designed to catch
exactly that.

**Why 0.30 rather than keeping 0.25.** 0.25 mm was never chosen; it was present.
On a direct-printed front, where ink meets material with no label substrate, a
0.25 mm hairline is at the edge of where dot gain and ink spread stop being
theoretical. 0.30 mm is the smallest weight I am willing to put on owner-facing
output while it has no measurement behind it. **This is a judgement about print
risk, not a measurement of print behaviour**, and if it reads as over-cautious
when a real proof comes back, that is the correct direction to be wrong in.

**The third condition on the divider, which the A10 row did not name.** Reading
`compose_container.py` rather than the manifest: inside `if direct_print and
hierarchy:` the rule is drawn only `if language is not None` — it additionally
requires a **SUPPORTED motif language**. So the divider has *three* gates, not
two: the branch must be reached (C8), the weight must have authority (this
section), and the concept must carry a supported language. **The manifest was
incomplete on its own subject.** That third gate is now a manifest note, and the
executor must confirm which concepts satisfy it before claiming the divider is
drawable — per AD0(a), that is a measurement to take, not a condition to assume
is met.

**What was rejected.** *Commission a measured proof first.* It is what §W4(c)
literally asks for and it remains the right long-run answer. It was rejected as
the immediate route because it adds a physical-world row to section A, and
section A rows have a demonstrated latency measured in weeks. The divider would
stay undrawn the whole time, for a number that is a 0.05 mm judgement call.
Ruling it now with an honest authority field, and superseding it when the proof
lands, gets the geometry built and loses nothing — because §W4(c) was already
written to supersede exactly this.

---

### AU3 — C2 RULED: the conservative brand usage set

**The ruling, in the form a validator consumes:**

```
clear_space   : 1.0 × the logo's own cap height, on all four sides
minimum_size  : 12.0 mm reproduced width in print
                60 px reproduced width on screen
backgrounds   : permitted — brand light ground, pure white
                permitted — the reversed lockup on brand dark, and ONLY
                            the reversed lockup
                forbidden — everything else, including photographic
                            grounds and any tinted field not named above
```

**Clear space is expressed in the logo's OWN cap height, deliberately.** A
clear-space rule in millimetres is a rule about one reproduction size; a rule in
cap heights holds at every size, which is the only way it survives contact with a
35 mm container front and a web header in the same document. It is also directly
machine-checkable against geometry the repo already emits.

**On the 12 mm floor and the front it has to fit on.** This is the number most
likely to be wrong, and it is wrong in a specific, checkable way — see AU6(c).
The front in the live profile is **35.00 mm** wide. A 12 mm logo with 1× cap
height clear space each side has to coexist with the name, the rule, the
descriptor and the decoration element. **I have not measured whether it fits.**
That measurement is the executor's first move on this row, and if it does not
fit, the correct output is *"the ruled minimum does not fit the ruled front"* as
a finding — not a quietly reduced floor. **Never move a bar to make a
measurement pass** applies to bars I set five minutes ago.

**What is NOT blocked, and was never blocked.** The logo already emits, and its
axis already PASSES on measured geometry: `container_logo_metrics/1.0` is
produced from the real emitted document, `rendered_extent_pt` clears the 8.0 pt
floor, and every placement reports `aspect_deviation == 0.0` and `clipped is
False`. **C2 was never the reason the logo was unmeasured; it was the reason it
was unjudged.** Those are different failures and the record should not blur
them.

**What was rejected.** *The generous set* (2× cap height, 15 mm) — plausibly
correct for the mark and plausibly impossible on a 35 mm front; choosing it
would have made AU6(c)'s risk near-certain rather than merely open. *The
permissive set* — rejected under AU0(c). *Defer* — rejected because it leaves
the executor with strictly less to do and defers a decision that gets no easier
with time.

---

### AU4 — what this actually unblocks, stated as a prediction so it can be wrong

Per AD0(a), everything in this list is a **prediction until the executor
measures it**, and the tranche that acts on this section must report the measured
version rather than restating the predicted one.

| element of `pc.vqr3_artwork_composition` | before | predicted after |
|---|---|---|
| NAME | drawn | drawn, unchanged |
| DECORATION | drawn | drawn, unchanged |
| LOGO | drawn, unjudged | drawn **and judged** against AU3 |
| DIVIDER | **never drawn** | drawn, at 0.30 mm, subject to the third gate in AU2 |
| COPY | **never drawn** | drawn as a marked provisional, per AU5 |

**The node is not predicted to VALIDATE**, and any report that claims it did
should be read with suspicion. V3 §10 allows no partial credit, and one of the
five elements will be carrying a placeholder string until C9 lands. What is
predicted is that **all five are reached for the first time**, which is a
different and honest claim.

**§AS2(2) note.** If the tranche acting on this section closes with no node
percentage moved, that is still a reportable defect and is still reported first.
This section makes movement *possible*; it does not license claiming it.

---

### AU5 — the guard that does not exist, and why the front descriptor may not be fed until it does

This is the load-bearing clause of the section.

`tools/reserved_copy.py` is real and works — §AK's finding that `⟪PROVISIONAL⟫`
appeared in zero `.py` files is **false at HEAD**, discharged by WI-3H, and the
token now lives in `tools/reserved_copy.py:54` bound alongside the production
spelling `CONTENT_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED`. That is the repair working.

**But its scope excludes exactly this string.** From its own docstring: *"the
PRODUCT heading is deliberately outside it — the product name comes from the
record on the production path and is brand (§AE2(c)), a different reservation
with a different remedy."* `RESERVED_HEADINGS` covers INGREDIENTS, WARNINGS,
MANUFACTURER, DIRECTIONS, DESCRIPTION, CLAIMS and NET CONTENT. **A front
descriptor tier is none of those.** So if the executor feeds a placeholder
descriptor into `hierarchy_lines` today, **no instrument in the repository will
refuse it**, and the "different remedy" the docstring promises for §AE2(c) has
never been built.

That is the §AA shape precisely: a protection that exists in prose and not in
code, described as being in use, in a file whose entire subject is that exact
mistake having been made once before.

**Therefore, the ordering is fixed and is not the executor's to reorder:**

1. **The remedy for §AE2(c) brand strings is built first** — whether by
   extending `reserved_copy.py`'s scope, or by a sibling checker, is the
   executor's call under §AE1 and should be ruled in its own EXECUTOR-RULED
   section with a named bet.
2. **It is watched failing on a real violation before it is relied on** — §AA
   is not satisfied by a guard that has only ever passed. Feed it an unmarked
   descriptor, see it refuse, then remove the violation.
3. **Only then** may `hierarchy_lines` be supplied on the production path, with
   `text` carrying the literal `⟪PROVISIONAL⟫` token and `provisional: true`
   per §AE3.
4. **No emission carrying a provisional descriptor reaches print, a proof, or
   any owner-facing artefact.** Fail-closed, and the closure is observed firing
   before it is trusted.

**If step 1 turns out to be large**, the honest outcome is that the front stays
unreached this tranche and the size of the remedy is the finding. That is a
better tranche than a drawn front with an unguarded fake string on it.

---

### AU6 — the named bets. Each of these three rulings can lose, and this is how.

**AU6(a) — AU1 loses if one supporting line cannot carry what the front has to
say.** The bet is that the product name plus a single descriptor is a complete
front. If, when the real string is written, it will not fit on one line at a
size that reads — or if it turns out the front must carry a second idea — then
`len(hierarchy_lines) == 1` was ruled too early and this section is superseded,
not stretched. **Losing condition: the owner writes C9 and it does not fit one
tier.**

**AU6(b) — AU2 loses to any real measurement.** By design. The bet is narrower
than it looks: it is not that 0.30 mm is right, it is that **0.30 mm is a safer
place to sit than 0.25 mm while neither has a proof.** Losing condition: a
§W4(c) proof measures a printed container front rule at a weight that makes 0.30
the worse of the two guesses — in which case AU2 was over-cautious and the
correct lesson is about the direction of caution, not about the number.

**AU6(c) — AU3 loses on arithmetic, and this is the bet most likely to be
lost.** The bet is that a 12.0 mm minimum reproduced width, plus 1× cap-height
clear space on all four sides, fits on a 35.00 mm front alongside the name, the
rule, the descriptor and the decoration. **I did not measure this before ruling
it.** Losing condition: the executor measures the front and the ruled minimum
does not fit. Required response: report it as *"AU3's floor is too high for the
front it has to live on"* and queue the correction — **do not reduce the floor
to make the fit pass.**

**AU6(d) — AU0(a) loses if splitting rows turns out to produce more churn than
progress.** The bet is that structure/content splits shrink the owed set. If the
next three splits each produce a ruled structure that is immediately superseded
when the content arrives, the split was premature and the rows should have stayed
bundled. Losing condition: **two** ruled structures superseded by their own
content within one tranche.

**(a)** `len(hierarchy_lines) == 1` is a contract number. Changing it supersedes

**(b)** `container_front_rule.width_mm == 0.30` with `authority` beginning
`OWNER_RULED`. A rewrite of that field to anything resembling a measurement is a
§AK-class defect.

**(c)** `container_front_rule.emitted` stays `False` until production actually
draws it, and flips in the commit that makes it true, not the commit that makes

proof, or any owner-facing artefact.

**(f)** AU3's floors are not adjusted to make a fit measurement pass. If they do
not fit, the finding is that they do not fit.

**(g)** Nothing in this section advances `owner_acceptance` for any node, and

superseding inputs arrive (§AE3(d)): C9 for AU1, a §W4(c) proof for AU2, a real
printed logo reproduction for AU3.

**(i)** This section is OWNER-RULED and is therefore not bound by §AS3's
prohibition on opening a new `## §Ax` section before a node moves. That

## §AV — EXECUTOR-RULED — the §AE2(c) remedy is two instruments, not one, and the runtime half has no wire to run on

**THE NODE THIS UNBLOCKS: `pc.vqr3_artwork_composition`.** WI-3K moved zero
nodes, so §AS3 forbids opening this section unless §AS2(4) applies. It applies,
and here is the specific chain rather than an assertion of it: AU5 fixes the
order — the §AE2(c) guard is built *first*, and `hierarchy_lines` may not be
supplied until it has been watched refusing. `hierarchy_lines` is AU1's C8
shape. C8 is one of the three rows WI-3K measured as the rows that stop
`pc.vqr3_artwork_composition`. So this section is not ahead of anything; it is
the first buildable item on the only path to that node.

### AV0 — the negative result first

I went looking for a way to satisfy AU5(1) by extending `reserved_copy.py`,
because that was the cheaper of the two options the owner named and I expected
to take it. **It cannot be extended to cover this.** That is a finding against
my own preference and it is stated first per AD0(c).

### AV1 — before any of that: the readiness report has been dropping content codes for 25 days

This was found while tracing where a provisional brand string would have to
surface. It is not what I was looking for.

`apps/pipeline/targets/container/__init__.py:810` says of the
`CONTENT_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` markers:

> *"The markers surface in the readiness report and block production
> authority."*

and `:1387-1388` repeats it:

> *"unverified back copy blocks PRODUCTION authority (a Gate-2 concern, visible
> in the readiness report …)"*

**Both sentences are false at HEAD, and I measured it rather than read it.**
The writer at `:1389-1390` does persist `readiness["content"]`. The reader,
`apps/ire/container_production_readiness.py:29-31`, iterates a fixed tuple:

```
_SECTIONS = ("font", "material", "material_attribution", "production_method",
             "production_metrics", "quantitative_fidelity", "separations",
             "wrap_alignment")
```

`"content"` is not in it. Measured differentially, with `_output_intent`
neutralised and every other input held constant:

| spec | `blocking_codes` |
|---|---|
| no content codes | `RECONSTRUCTION_ABSENT`, 3 × `PRINT_DATA_INCOMPLETE` |
| **three unverified reserved sections** (ingredients, warnings, manufacturer) | **byte-identical to the row above** |
| CONTROL — one code under `font` | the same list **plus `FONT_LICENCE_MISSING`** |

The control is what makes this a measurement and not a guess: the aggregation
path demonstrably works, and one `font` code changes the verdict. Three
`CONTENT_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` codes change nothing. Unverified INGREDIENTS
copy — the §AE2(b) core — does not block production authority, in the one
report whose comments say it does.

**Dated.** Reader `de27a61` created `_SECTIONS` on 2026-07-24. Writer `2a92be8`
added `readiness["content"]` on 2026-07-27, three days later, without extending
it. **Live for 25 days.** The test fixture at
`apps/pipeline/tests/test_2b3d_readiness.py:22-26` re-types the reader's eight
names as `_CLEAN_SECTIONS`, so the test data embodies the same omission and
nothing could have noticed. This is §AA in its most ordinary form: a protection
described in a comment, believed by everyone downstream, never once observed
firing.

**RULED: the repair is not the missing string.** Adding `"content"` to
`_SECTIONS` fixes today and rebuilds the hole tomorrow, because the next
category added by a writer three days later fails exactly the same way and
fails silently. `_SECTIONS` becomes the DECLARED set, and any key present in
the persisted spec but absent from the declaration emits
`UNDECLARED_READINESS_SECTION: <name>` as a blocking code. A category nobody
declared halts the report rather than being dropped from it. This mirrors
`reserved_copy.py`'s own `UNKNOWN_ROLE` discipline, in which "a seventh
spelling of `text` halts this scan" — the house already owns this pattern and
this is not a new invention.

**Cost, measured before ruling and not after:** `"content"` was temporarily
added to `_SECTIONS` and the six affected test files run — **107 passed, 0
failed, 18.24s** — then reverted, with `git diff --stat` confirming the revert.
The repair costs zero test failures. I am not claiming that number covers the
declared-set version, which is a larger change; it bounds the *disconnection*
repair only.

### AV2 — `reserved_copy.py` cannot be extended to cover brand strings, and the reason is the thing that makes it good

AU5(1) leaves "extend its scope, or a sibling checker" to me under §AE1. It
resolves to **sibling**, on measured grounds.

`_pairs` gates every path on `RESERVED_HEADINGS` membership
(`reserved_copy.py:345-350`). Its first act is to look for a heading-role key
whose resolved value is a reserved heading, and:

```
if not headings:
    return out, unknown          # line 349-350
```

AU1's descriptor shape is `{"text": …, "rel": …, "kind": "descriptor"}`. It has
no heading-role key at all. Measured against the live function, with controls:

| input | result |
|---|---|
| AU1 descriptor, **unmarked** — a real §AE2(c) violation | `pairs=[] unknown=[]` |
| AU1 descriptor carrying `⟪PROVISIONAL⟫` | `pairs=[] unknown=[]` |
| CONTROL — `{"heading": "INGREDIENTS", "text": …}` | **seen**, one pair |
| CONTROL — `{"heading": "WARNINGS", "blurb": …}` | **`UNKNOWN_ROLE` fires** |

`'kind' in HEADING_ROLE_KEYS` → False. `'descriptor' in RESERVED_HEADINGS` →
False. `'rel' in TEXT_ROLE_KEYS` → False.

The two controls matter more than the two findings. The third row proves the
scanner is sensitive. **The fourth proves that even the safety net does not
cover this**: `UNKNOWN_ROLE` lives *below* the line-349 return, so it catches
only a dict that names a reserved heading and then misspells its text key. A
dict naming no reserved heading is not an unknown role — it is not a subject at
all, and the scanner is right about that.

**And that return is load-bearing.** The comment at `:305-314` records that an
earlier content-paired version produced *"139 findings of which about a dozen
were copy"* and that a guard with a hundred false findings *"is a guard that
gets silenced."* The `RESERVED_HEADINGS` gate is precisely what bought the
selectivity. Widening it to admit brand tiers would spend that.

**RULED: a sibling, `tools/brand_strings.py`.** Adding `"descriptor"` to
`RESERVED_HEADINGS` is a category error and not merely a preference: that
frozenset *is* the §AE2(b) regulated-copy vocabulary, and putting an §AE2(c)
brand tier inside it would make the file's own SCOPE declaration false — the
declaration AU5 quotes as the reason this remedy is owed. A guard that lies
about its own scope to cover one more case is the AD0(b) failure with the
polarity reversed. The sibling shares the `_resolve` / `_py_files` /
`_module_constants` machinery by import; it does not fork it.

### AV3 — the half AU5 does not name: a static scanner cannot satisfy AU8(e)

AU5's four steps read as one instrument. They are two, and this is the part
worth the section.

Steps 1–3 are **static**: does a placeholder string appear, unmarked, in
source? An AST scan answers that, and `reserved_copy.py` is the proof that it
answers it well.

**AU8(e) is not a question about source.** *"No emission carrying a
`⟪PROVISIONAL⟫` descriptor reaches print, a proof, or any owner-facing
artefact."* An emission is a runtime object. The descriptor reaching it may
have come from a database row, a fixture, or an owner-supplied C9 string that
does not exist yet — **none of which are in any `.py` file.** A static scanner
is structurally incapable of refusing it. If the static half alone were built
and called the AU5 remedy, the result would be a guard that passes cleanly
while a provisional string goes to print: §AA again, freshly built, in the
tranche whose subject is §AA.

**RULED: the runtime half is a readiness code**, `BRAND_STRING_PROVISIONAL:<kind>`,
emitted where the descriptor is realised and aggregated through the readiness
mechanism — **which is why AV1 is a prerequisite and not a digression.** The
runtime half of the §AE2(c) remedy is a blocking code carried by exactly the
aggregation path that has been silently dropping a whole category for 25 days.
Built in the other order, the guard would be wired to a wire that goes nowhere,
and it would report green.

### AV4 — the named bets

**(a) That the sibling stays a sibling.** If `brand_strings.py` and
`reserved_copy.py` converge to near-identical bodies differing only by
vocabulary, the split was wrong and one parameterised scanner with two declared
vocabularies was the right shape. **Losing condition: more than 60% of the
sibling's non-import lines are substantively shared with `reserved_copy.py`
when it is done.** I will measure this and report it whichever way it falls.

**(b) That `UNDECLARED_READINESS_SECTION` blocks and never merely warns.** The
bet is that no legitimate non-blocking readiness category exists. **Losing
condition: more than two categories end up needing to be declared non-blocking**
— at which point the right shape was a per-category severity field and the flat
declared set was too crude. §AU8(f) applies to this by analogy and I bind
myself to it: if a real category needs to pass, I declare it and say so; I do
not quietly move it out of the set to make a run go green.

**(c) That the runtime code has a place to be emitted from.** I have measured
the reader and the writer, but I have *not* yet found the site where a
`hierarchy_lines` descriptor becomes an emission. **If that site does not exist
yet, the runtime half cannot be built this tranche, and per AU5's closing
clause the honest outcome is that the front stays unreached and the size of the
remedy is the finding.** I am recording this bet before building rather than
discovering it afterwards and presenting it as a plan.

### AV5 — what this section does not claim

It does not claim `pc.vqr3_artwork_composition` will move. It does not adopt
§AU4's prediction table; every number here is one I measured. It does not touch
`owner_acceptance`. It does not claim any guard has been seen firing — **no
guard has been built yet**, and AU5(2) requires the refusal be watched before
anything is relied on. The `_pairs` probe above is a measurement of an existing
scanner's blind spot, not a guard firing.

## §AW — EXECUTOR-RULED — the closure belonged at the emitter, and AU3's clear space fails on a side the ruling never looked at

**THE NODE THIS UNBLOCKS: `pc.vqr3_artwork_composition`.** AV6 moved zero nodes,
so §AS2(3) forbids opening this section unless §AS2(4) applies. It applies, and
the chain is specific rather than asserted. The C2 row names what it blocks:
*"`brand_gov.minimum_component_library` (as before) **and the LOGO element of
`pc.vqr3_artwork_composition`**"*. §AU's order of work item 2 says measure C2's
floor and *"then build the validator"*. The validator is the instrument that
makes the LOGO element **judged** rather than merely measured — the distinction
the C2 row itself draws. This section is the ruling that validator needs in
front of it under §AE0(b). It is not ahead of anything; it is the thing being
built.

### AW0 — THE PREVIOUS TRANCHE'S HEADLINE CLAIM WAS REFUTED BY ITS OWN AUDIT

AV6's headline said the three closures covered the paths to an artefact. The
§AE6 audit of `e893791` found a fourth, and it was right. Quoted verbatim, its
first REFUTED item:

> **1. A fourth path exists, is production, and is the same shape.**
> `apps/dielines/services/export_service.py:258-263` composes
> `compose_vector_art_graph(..., product_name=params.metadata.product_name,
> subtitle=params.metadata.product_type)` — byte-for-byte the same call and the
> same data source that gate 3 (`native_handoff.py:95-100`) guards — then writes
> an editable `.ai` at line 280 and a PNG proof at line 299. The `elif` branch
> does the same at lines 337/347. `grep -rn brand_string apps/dielines/` → **zero
> hits**. Its outputs land on the *same owner-facing fields gate 1 protects*:
> `apps/pipeline/agents/aria.py:1542` (`output.design_preview`) and `:1549`
> (`output.design_preview_ai`); also
> `apps/pipeline/management/commands/correct_dieline_output.py:175/180`. The
> message hedges ("NOT that there is no fourth path… found the same way"), but
> `grep -rn "emit_pdf_ai(" apps/` returns only four non-test call sites and **two
> of them are this file** — the same grep that found gate 3 landed on it. The
> headline "A document carrying provisional brand copy can no longer produce an
> editable .ai, a PNG proof" is true only of the three paths chosen.

**Confirmed by my own reading, not accepted on the audit's word.** The composition
at 258-263 and the emission at 280, the second pair at 330/337, and
`grep -rn brand_string apps/dielines/` returning nothing, are all as described.
(The audit says the `elif` composes at 327; measured, it is 330. Its emission
and rasterization line numbers, 337 and 347, are exact.)

**One correction to the audit, in its favour.** It says four non-test call sites
of `emit_pdf_ai`. I measure **five**: `targets/container/__init__.py:1382`,
`ire/vq1_render.py:256`, `ire/handoff/container_adapter.py:448`,
`export_service.py:280` and `export_service.py:337`. The undercount does not
weaken the finding, it strengthens it — there was one more unguarded emitter
than the refutation claimed.

**The reason this happened is the shape of the remedy, not the diligence of the
search.** Three gates were written as three copies at three call sites. AV6's own
defect 1 was that the *third* copy shipped without its import, because a copy
carries no obligation to be complete. A fourth call site was then added to the
world by nobody — it was always there — and no copy was placed on it. §AK3 says
two spellings of one idea belong bound in one place. Four copies of one closure
is the same error with a larger number.

### AW1 — RULED: THE §AE2(c) CLOSURE MOVES TO THE EMITTER, AND THE CALL-SITE COPIES STAY

The closure is placed in `apps/ire/emitters/pdf_ai.py::emit_pdf_ai`, which every
editable-`.ai` emission in the repository passes through. A document whose brand
strings are not clean does not become a file.

**The three existing gates are NOT removed.** They fail earlier, with better
messages, and they refuse the *package* rather than one file. A chokepoint that
makes earlier gates redundant would be an argument for deleting them; this one
makes them redundant only for the narrow question "does a file get written",
which is not the only question any of them asks. Keeping both is not belt and
braces, it is two different assertions that happen to agree on one case.

**Blast radius, measured before ruling rather than after.** `brand_string_report`
returns `clean = not runs` and `provisional_runs` decides on `MARKER in text`
alone — the literal `⟪PROVISIONAL⟫`. A document with no marker is clean. Thirteen
test files call `emit_pdf_ai`; none of them composes a marked string today, so the
gate is inert for every existing caller. **A guard that is inert everywhere is
also a guard nobody has seen fire (§AA), which is why it is watched refusing a
real emission before this section is relied on.**

**THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN ENGINEERED AWAY (§Y2(c)).** `emit_pdf_ai` is the
chokepoint for documents. It is not the chokepoint for *artefacts*.
`apps/dielines/exporters/design_preview.py` contains two functions that draw a
product name straight onto a ReportLab canvas with no Document in between —
`export_design_components_ai:239` (drawing at 399-406) and
`export_design_preview_ai:427`. `brand_string_report` cannot read either, because

### AW2 — §AU ORDER 2, MEASURED. THE FRONT IS NOT 35.00 mm, AND THE FLOOR IS NOT THE PROBLEM

AU3 ruled `minimum_size: 12.0 mm` and named AU6(c) as the bet most likely to be
lost: *"a 12.0 mm minimum reproduced width, plus 1× cap-height clear space on all
four sides, fits on a 35.00 mm front alongside the name, the rule, the descriptor
and the decoration."* Measured off the emitted document, per AD0(a).

**(a) The scale is 1:1, so the numbers are comparable at all.** `_sheet_layout`
sets `con_box = (…, W, H)` and `_fit` therefore returns `s = 1.0`. The hero
container is at true product scale, so one sheet millimetre is one container
millimetre and `placed_mm` may be compared to a print floor without conversion.
This was measured, not inferred from the docstring that claims it.

**(b) The front is 28.80 mm, not 35.00 mm.**

```
backbone.label_zone            x=5.600  y=53.020  w=28.800  h=38.500   mm
propose_zones z_front (live)   w=28.0 mm
ruling states                  35.00 mm
difference                     -6.20 mm  (-17.7%)
```

**Where 35.00 comes from, reproduced rather than guessed at.**
`surface_geometry` reads `body_width_mm` with a **fallback of 50.0**, and
`propose_zones` covers the front at 0.7. `build_inferred_profile("bottle")` with
no estimates gives `BODY_FRONT.w = 50.0` and `z_front.width = 35.0` — exactly the
ruled figure. The live `ContainerProfile` default is `width_mm = 40.0`, giving
28.0, and the composed `label_zone` is 28.8. **35.00 mm is the width of a front
derived from an unmeasured fallback**, not a measurement of the live profile. The
ruling's own sentence — "The front in the live profile is 35.00 mm wide" — is the
one thing in AU3 that reads as a measurement and is not one.

This makes the front **narrower** than the bet assumed, which tightens AU6(c)
rather than loosening it. It is reported that way round deliberately: a
correction that happens to help the ruling would be worth less.

**(c) Cap height is not placed height, and the difference is 16.7%.** The mark is
`media/brand/logo.png`, 1439×300 px — an all-caps wordmark, a rose counter in the
O, and a superscript ® at top right. Measured per column at alpha > 128:

```
flat capitals (B, B, R), x[0,700)   ink y[34,290]   = 257 px   <- CAP HEIGHT
round O overshoot,       x[767,944) ink y[24,295]
superscript ®,           x[1357,   ) ink y[0, 261]  <- reaches the canvas top
whole canvas                        y[0, 299]      = 300 px
CAP_RATIO = 257/300 = 0.856667      ASPECT h/w = 0.208478
```

The canvas is taller than the cap band at the top because of the ® and at the
bottom because of the round-letter overshoot. **A validator that reads
`placed_mm[3]` as the cap height over-requires clear space by 1/0.856667 − 1 =
16.7%** — a gate too strict for a reason that has nothing to do with the brand.

**(d) The floor fits. Comfortably. AU6(c) is WON on the axis it was bet on.**

```
a logo reproduced at exactly the 12.0 mm floor:
  placed height                 2.5017 mm
  cap height (x0.856667)        2.1432 mm
  footprint incl. clear space   16.2863 x 6.7880 mm
  the front is                  28.8000 x 38.5000 mm
  horizontal headroom           +12.5137 mm
  vertical headroom             +31.7120 mm
  on the 35.00 mm front assumed +18.7137 mm
```

Even on the front that is 17.7% narrower than ruled, the ruled minimum fits with
more than 12 mm to spare. **§AU8(f) does not get invoked, because there is
nothing to invoke it against.** The floor is not moved, and it did not need to
be.

**(e) AND THE CLEAR SPACE FAILS ANYWAY, ON THE SIDE THE BET DID NOT NAME.** The
emitted logo is placed at 17.28 mm wide, above the floor. Its cap height is
therefore 3.0866 mm, and that is what 1× clear space costs on every side:

```
                      available     required    verdict
left                     5.7600       3.0866     PASS
right                    5.7600       3.0866     PASS
above                    4.3590       3.0866     PASS
below  (see table)          ...          ...     FAIL
minimum_size 12.0 mm    placed 17.280 mm         PASS
```

Below is measured against real font metrics, because `TextRun.y` is the
**baseline** — `emitters/pdf_ai.py::_draw_text` calls `drawCentredString(x, y,
…)` — so a text tier's ink starts above its `y`. The registered faces are
NotoSans / NotoSans-Bold, `OS/2.sCapHeight = 714 / upm 1000`, confirmed against
the `H` glyph's own yMax of 714.

```
logo bottom edge 74.181 mm; nothing may ink above 77.268 mm

element                      ink top      gap     need   verdict
TODAY   product-name-0       75.7549   1.5739   3.0866  FAIL by 1.5127 mm
AFTER   rule-front-single    75.4600   1.2790   3.0866  FAIL by 1.8076 mm
AFTER   product-name-hero    76.8030   2.6221   3.0866  FAIL by 0.4645 mm
```

`TODAY` is the front as emitted at HEAD. `AFTER` is the front once
`hierarchy_lines` is supplied under §AU order 1(c) — composed in memory for this
measurement only, writing nothing, with the descriptor carrying the marked
provisional token so that even the measurement is not an unmarked brand string.

**So AU3's clear-space rule is violated by the artwork the repository emits
today, and gets worse by 0.3 mm when the ruled front rule arrives.** This is the
outcome §AU asked for in as many words — *"It is meant to be tight enough that
the emitted logo might fail it. If it does, that failure is the tranche's best
output"* — and it is a failure of the **layout**, which is §AE1's and mine to
fix, against a **rule**, which is §AE2(c)'s and the owner's to keep. The rule
does not move. Nothing in this section moves it.

**What is NOT claimed here:** not that the layout is corrected — it is not, this
section only measures — and not that 1× cap height is the wrong ratio. A rule
that the current layout fails is the rule doing its job on the first day it
could.

### AW3 — RULED: WHAT "CAP HEIGHT" MEANS TO THE VALIDATOR, AND WHY IT NEEDED RULING

**The words already mean something else in this repository.** `ContainerProfile`
carries `cap_height_mm`, `surface_geometry` reads it, and there it means **the
height of the bottle's closure**. AU3's "cap height" is the typographic distance
from baseline to cap line of the logo's own letterforms. Two ideas, one spelling,
and §AK3's failure mode is a reader binding to the wrong one.

**RULED:** the brand-usage contract never uses the bare term. It emits
`logo_cap_height_mm`, and the closure dimension keeps `cap_height_mm`. The
validator computes:

```
logo_cap_height_mm = placed_height_mm × cap_ratio
cap_ratio          = (flat-capital ink band) / (asset canvas height)
```

**`cap_ratio` is MEASURED PER ASSET, never a constant.** 0.856667 is this file's
number, not the module's. A different logo — one with padding, a descender, a
lowercase wordmark — has a different ratio, and a constant would silently
mis-measure it while looking authoritative. The flat-capital band is found by
excluding the columns that overshoot: round letters at the baseline and any
superscript above the cap line.

**The honest limit (§Y2(c)):** for a mark with *no* flat capitals at all — a
lowercase or purely pictorial logo — there is no cap band to find, and the
contract emits no cap height and the clear-space check reports UNMEASURED rather
than substituting the placed height. An UNMEASURED axis is blocking, which is the
true state; a substituted number would be a claim made from no measurement, which
is the exact defect `container_logo_metrics` was written to avoid.

`RULED BY: executor under §AE1. REVIEWABLE. NOT OWNER-ACCEPTED.`

**AX0(p) — I RAN A391's FIVE STEPS COMPLETE AND MISORDERED, WHICH IS §AV5's
DEFECT INVERTED.** A391 reads *"records, regenerate, rebind, compute, pin"*.
This tranche ran regenerate/rebind/compute/pin over `suite_file_manifest`
first, pinned `protocol_identity` to `a046c26c242831a3` — and only then found
`record_integrity.py` refusing on a `RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH`. The **records**
step, step one, had not been run. Clearing it moved
`record_digest_manifest.json` from `b924d02e…` to `a32b4daa…`, invalidating the
identity pinned minutes earlier and forcing the entire chain a second time.
Final identity: **`b5e84a3b8ecb08b1`**.

How I talked myself out of step one is the entry. I hashed the record manifest
against the corpus, found them equal, and concluded the records step was
already satisfied — and wrote that down, in the pin comment, as *"the narrower
§AV5 case"*. But "is the pin current?" and "does the record set validate?" are
different questions, and the check I ran answers only the first. §AV5's own
entry, four lines above mine in the same file, records the mirror image: it
read `RECORD_INTEGRITY=OK` and concluded the **pin** was current, calling that
verdict *"true and irrelevant — an instrument's verdict borrowed for a question
it was not asked."* I read that sentence, wrote a comment claiming to have
learned from it, and made it backwards in the same edit. Both wrong sentences
are left standing in `test_characterization_protocol.py` with the correction
beneath them.

What it cost: one re-run. §AV5's silent version cost a full tranche. A387 threw
`UnsyncedManifest` naming the order **in its own error message**, before any
commit — which is the first time this repo has been able to put a price on the
difference between a loud guard and a silent one. That is the strongest
argument for A387 anyone has produced, and it is an accident.

### AX2 — THE THRESHOLDS THAT ARE MINE, AND WHY EACH IS NOT TUNED TO ITS SAMPLE

The three bars are **the owner's** (C2, ruled at §AU3) and this section changes
none of them. What §AE1 hands me is what it takes to *read* them.

**AX2(a) — `CAP_BAND_MIN_SHARE = 0.10`.** A cap height cannot be assumed, so it
is measured per asset from the mode of inked-column top edges. The floor decides
when a winning edge is a **cap line** rather than the tallest thing in a crowd.
Measured: the passing asset's edges carry 40.16 % and 29.35 %; the mark with no
cap band carries 4.51 % and 4.01 %. 0.10 sits **2.9× below the lowest pass and
2.2× above the highest fail**, so it is not wedged between two samples — the
property that matters, because a threshold tuned to its samples describes them.
A mode-margin rule was tried first and **rejected on measurement**: it rejects
the approved logo itself, whose baseline mode leads by only 1.82× because the
runner-up is the round letters' overshoot — the exact feature the mode exists
to ignore.

**AX2(b) — ink detection is alpha-if-present, corner-differs otherwise.** Forced
by a real asset: `bbrose_logo_approved.png` carries **no alpha channel**, and an
alpha-only reader called every column inked and returned a cap ratio of
**1.000000** — which would then have demanded clear space equal to the mark's
*full placed height*. A gate made stricter by a bug, wearing a measurement's
face. It now reports UNMEASURED for that asset, which is the true state.

**AX2(c) — UNMEASURED is neither a pass nor a failure.** `all([None])` is True
in Python, so the first aggregation quietly turned "we never measured this" into
"this passed". Both `meets_minimum_size` and `meets_clear_space` now return
`None` when any placement is unmeasured, and an unmeasured axis is blocking.

**AX2(d) — a node that CONTAINS the logo is a GROUND, not a neighbour.** Stated
as containment rather than as a list of node names, so a field that merely
*crowds* the mark is still reported.

**AX2(e) — text is measured from its BASELINE.** `TextRun.y` is the baseline —
`pdf_ai._draw_text` calls `drawCentredString(x, y, …)`. A validator reading `y`
as a top edge under-reports every intrusion from below by a whole cap height,
which is precisely the direction today's real failure comes from. The x-extent
is deliberately treated as ±∞, which over-reports rather than under-reports.

**AX2(f) — the spelling (§AK3).** `cap_height_mm` already means the height of
the bottle's **closure**. This contract never uses the bare term; it emits
`logo_cap_height_mm`, so a reader cannot bind to the wrong one of two ideas
wearing one spelling.

*Corrected 2026-08-21, and the correction is the point.* This paragraph
originally read *"`ContainerProfile.cap_height_mm` already means…"*. There is no
such attribute — measured, `ContainerProfile`
(`apps/pipeline/targets/container/silhouettes.py:32`) carries `archetype`,
`variant`, `height_mm`, `width_mm`, `neck_ratio`, `cap_style`, `label_zone`,
`decoration_zone`, `closure_geometry`, and nothing named `cap_height_mm`. The
real spelling is a **confirm-gate form dict key**, at `views.py:1106,1369`,
`targets/ui.py:250` and `targets/composite.py:153`. The §AK3 collision is
therefore real and the paragraph's conclusion is unchanged — but I wrote the
wrong citation for it, **in the same document in which AX0(m) corrects §AW for
writing that exact wrong citation.** I found it by reading my own section back,
not by being told. Two spellings of one idea is what §AK3 is about; two
statements of one wrong location, four screens apart, is what §AE0(e) is about.

### AX4 — THE NAMED BETS

**AX4(a) — the 0.10 share floor loses to a wordmark with no flat capitals.** A
mark set entirely in lowercase, or in a script face, has no cap line to find and
will report UNMEASURED — correctly, but it means the clear-space axis is
unavailable for a whole class of legitimate marks. Losing condition: a brand
asset the owner approves for which this gate can never return a verdict.

**AX4(b) — the ±∞ x-extent loses if it manufactures a failure.** Treating a
centred run as infinitely wide is conservative by choice, and conservative
instruments generate false positives. Losing condition: a clear-space failure
reported on the left or right side that a real ink measurement would clear.

**AX4(c) — this section's successor closes with the layout corrected and no
record of the front ever having failed.** Inherited from AW5(c) and restated
with the **right number**: gap 1.5737 mm against 3.0861 mm required, on
`product-name-0`, on the document the target emits today. The correction is a
separate tranche and the failing measurement is committed first.

## §AY — OWNER-RULED — the credential was never missing and the clear space was never failing where anyone said it was, and both remedies are orderings rather than fixes

**Trigger.** Two questions arrived at the owner from opposite ends of the
tranche and have one shape in common: in each, an executor stopped short of an
action it could physically perform, because performing it would have crossed
something reserved. §AX declined to unshadow a live API key because unguarded
spend is §AE7(c). §AW and §AX declined to resolve C2's clear-space failure
because the bars are §AE2(c). **Both refusals were correct and both are
rewarded here with a ruling rather than a permission.**

This section rules the ordering of two remedies. It does not rule either
remedy's outcome, and in one case it proves by arithmetic that the outcome
cannot be what the obvious reading assumes.

### AY0 — DEFECTS AND CORRECTIONS, INCLUDING TWO OF THE OWNER'S OWN

**AY0(a) — the claim that no `conftest.py` exists anywhere in the tree is
FALSE, and it was load-bearing.** It was stated as the reason the suite has no
safety net and therefore as the reason a live key means unguarded spend.
Measured at HEAD:

```
bbrose_design_os/conftest.py     tracked, committed at 80978a6, 11 lines
tools/dip0/tests/conftest.py     tracked
tools/dip0b/tests/conftest.py    tracked
tools/dip0c/tests/conftest.py    tracked
```

`bbrose_design_os/conftest.py` is not merely present, it sits at **the pytest
root** — the exact file the proposed guard was going to be created as. Its
existing eleven lines force `CELERY_EAGER`; its own docstring calls itself
*"belt-and-suspenders"* for a guard that authoritatively lives in
`config/settings.py`.

**The substance of the concern survives the correction, and was separately
measured.** A search for `autouse=True`, `socket.socket`, `disable_network`,
`no_network` and `block_network` across all four repository conftests returns
**zero hits**. So the true statement is not *"there is no conftest"* but
*"there are four conftests and none of them blocks an outbound call."* The
first is a claim about a file. The second is a claim about a behaviour, and
only the second is true.

**This is the §AW error in a new costume** — an absence asserted without its
search extent stated — inside a tranche that had already withdrawn a fabricated
defect for exactly that. The standing house rule applies and is restated as law
below.

**And the correction makes the remedy smaller, not larger.** The guard does not
need a new file. It goes into `bbrose_design_os/conftest.py`, which already
loads, is already tracked, and is already at the right level. Creating a second
root conftest — which is what the original framing would have produced — would
have introduced an ambiguity where none needed to exist.

**AY0(b) — the number the owner was shown for the C2 collision was the wrong
one, and the owner is recording that against himself.** The question put to
BBrose before this ruling described *"1.279 mm actual against 3.087 mm
required, short by 1.808 mm."* Those are the `AFTER / rule-front-single` row of
§AW2(e) — **a hypothetical**, reachable only once `hierarchy_lines` is supplied,
which nothing in the repository does. §AX0(a) had already caught this. The
owner's question repeated the superseded figure anyway.

**The live numbers, measured on the document the target emits today:**

```
intruder            product-name-0
gap                 1.5737 mm
required            3.0861 mm
shortfall           1.5124 mm
live front width    28.80 mm   (label_zone, not the 35.00 mm §AU3 assumed)
logo placed at      17.28 mm   (above the 12.0 mm floor, so size passes)
```

**The ruling's substance is unaffected — both numbers fail, and fail the same
bar in the same direction — but the ordering below is written against the live
number and not the future one.** A ruling issued against a hypothetical is a
ruling that cannot be checked.

**AY0(c) — the intruder is a VARIABLE, and every prior statement of this
collision treated it as a constant.** The element sitting inside the mark's
clear space **today** is `product-name-0`. The element that will sit there
**after** `hierarchy_lines` lands is `rule-front-single`. These are different
objects at different coordinates, and a remedy phrased as *"move the rule
down"* — which is how the owner first phrased it — **does not fix the failure
that exists now.** It fixes the one that does not exist yet.

So AY2's ordering is phrased against *the intruder*, whoever it turns out to
be on the day it is run, and **both states must clear**: the front as emitted
today, and the front as emitted once C9 supplies the descriptor. Clearing one
and shipping is not clearing.

**AY0(d) — the law both of the above are instances of.** *An absence is a
measurement and carries a search extent; a quantity is a measurement and
carries the state it was measured in.* A claim that a thing is not there must
say where it was looked for. A number quoted into a ruling must say which
version of the document it came off. **Neither of these is a new rule** — the
first is the standing house rule on absence claims, the second is §AD0(a) —
and both were broken in this tranche by different parties, which is the
argument for restating them where the next reader will hit them.

**AY0(e) — a refusal to act is reported at the volume of an action.** §AX
declined to clear the shadowed key and said so at length, including that it was
declining to *name a cause* between two readings that both fit its evidence.
That was the correct call twice over: once on the spend, once on the causation.
**§AE0(e) is usually read as "report your failures loudly." AY0(e) extends it:
report the things you deliberately did not do, and why, at the same volume.**
An executor that goes quiet at the edge of a reserved category is
indistinguishable from one that did not notice the edge.

---

### AY1 — THE SHADOWED CREDENTIAL. RULED: ACCIDENT. GUARD FIRST, THEN CLEAR.

**The finding, independently re-measured by the owner before ruling on it.**
`bbrose_design_os/.env` carries `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` at **108 characters** and
`OPENAI_API_KEY` at **164 characters**. `config/settings.py:17` calls
`environ.Env.read_env(ENV_FILE)`, whose documented behaviour is that it will
not override a key already present in `os.environ`. The shell exports
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` at **length zero**. An empty string is present. So the
blank wins and the 108-character credential is never read.

**The asymmetry is the proof and it is worth keeping.** `OPENAI_API_KEY` is
absent from the shell entirely, and resolves at 164 from the same file, through
the same loader, in the same process. Same everything except which one the
shell got to first. That is not an inference; it is a controlled comparison
that the repository ran on itself by accident.

**AY1(a) — RULED: the empty export is an ACCIDENT and is NOT PRESERVED.** It
was never designed, never documented, and appears nowhere in any committed
file. A spend control that exists only in the ambient state of one terminal
session is not a control; it is a coincidence that has been holding.
§AU0(c)'s shape applies — **a safeguard nobody wrote down and nobody has seen
refuse anything is not a safeguard** — and here it is worse than inert, because
it has been costing three test results and one credential's worth of capability
while looking like a bug to every audit that has walked past it.

**AY1(b) — the ordering is fixed and is not the executor's to reorder.**

```
1. BUILD  the outbound-call guard into bbrose_design_os/conftest.py.
          An autouse fixture, session- or function-scoped as the executor
          judges, that refuses every outbound network call raised from a
          test. NOT a new file. NOT a second root conftest.
2. WATCH  it refuse a REAL outbound call. Not grepped. Not asserted. RUN,
          with the refusal captured in full in the tranche report.
3. CLEAR  the empty export so .env line 4 resolves at 108.
4. RERUN  the full suite through guarded_commit.sh. No SUITE_CMD override.
```

**Step 2 is the step this ruling exists for.** §AA: a guard nobody has seen
fire is not evidence of anything. A guard built and then trusted on inspection
is precisely the artefact §AA was written about, and building it in the same
tranche that clears the credential means the first thing it protects is the
first thing it has ever been asked to protect. **Step 3 may not precede step 2
even if step 2 proves slow.**

**AY1(c) — if step 1 turns out to be large, the key stays shadowed and the
SIZE OF THE REMEDY IS THE FINDING.** This is §AU5's clause transplanted whole.
A green suite bought with unguarded spend is not a green suite; it is an
invoice with a green suite attached. If blocking outbound calls turns out to
require touching how the code paths under test are constructed, that discovery
is a better output than three tests going from red to green.

**AY1(d) — §AR4(5) is FALSIFIED and the consequence is not optional.** The
three failures were never inherited. They were caused, locally, by a blank in
the shell. §AW's justification for committing outside the extent gate rested on
their being pre-existing. It does not rest on anything now. **`ad3db82`'s
bypass of `guarded_commit.sh` is therefore an UNEXCUSED DEFECT**, is named as
one here, and is not to be repeated on the strength of the same reasoning. The
correct disposition is that once step 4 passes, the override has no remaining
justification in the repository and any future use of it is a fresh defect
requiring its own fresh argument.

**AY1(e) — what the executor may NOT do under this ruling.** It may not modify
any shell rc file. It may not write a credential into any tracked file. It may
not print, log, echo or commit the value of either key, at any length, in any
form, including partially masked. It may report **lengths**, which is what
every measurement in this section is built from and is sufficient for all of
them.

---

### AY2 — C2 REFUSED THE FRONT. THAT IS THE RULE WORKING. RULED: AN ORDERING.

**§AU0(c) predicted this in terms, and the prediction is the reason the
conservative set was chosen.** §AU said the tight set was picked partly
*because* it is tight enough that the emitted logo might fail it, and that *"if
it does, that failure is the most valuable output of the next tranche."* It
failed. **The finding is upheld as the tranche's best output and the bar does
not move.**

**AY2(a) — RULED: the ordering, phrased against the intruder.** The executor
**measures** which step fits. It does not choose which step it prefers.

```
1. MOVE THE INTRUDER.  Whichever element is inside the clear space on the
                       run — product-name-0 today, rule-front-single once
                       hierarchy_lines lands — move it out, if the vertical
                       budget exists. Costs nothing. Logo stays at ruled size.
2. SHRINK THE LOGO.    If step 1 does not fully clear it. Floor is 12.0 mm
                       print / 60 px screen and THAT FLOOR DOES NOT MOVE.
                       See AY2(c): this step alone provably cannot close it.
3. REPORT.             If neither fits, the finding is "the front cannot carry
                       the logo at ruled clear space" and the logo comes OFF
                       THE FRONT. That is a real answer, not a failure.
```

**BARRED, in these words: reducing clear space below 1.0× cap height.** Never
move a bar applies to bars set the same morning. §AU8(f) is available and is
not invoked, because nothing here reduces a floor.

**AY2(b) — both states must clear.** The front as emitted today, and the front
as emitted after C9 supplies the descriptor. §AW5(c) was written against the
future column and §AX0(a) caught it; the reverse mistake — fixing today's
intruder and declaring the row closed while the future one still collides — is
available and is barred by this clause.

**AY2(c) — the arithmetic that makes step 2 insufficient on its own, and this
is the part the owner did not know when ruling the order.** Required clear
space is a linear function of placed width: at 12.0 mm the cap height is
2.1431 mm, at the placed 17.28 mm it is 3.0861 mm.

```
requirement at the current 17.28 mm placement    3.0861 mm
requirement at the 12.0 mm floor                 2.1431 mm
relief available from the REQUIREMENT side       0.9430 mm
measured shortfall                               1.5124 mm
still uncovered after shrinking to the floor     0.5694 mm
```

**Shrinking the mark to its absolute permitted minimum buys 0.9430 mm of a
1.5124 mm shortfall — 62.3 % of it — from the requirement side alone.** The
remaining 0.5694 mm has to come from the geometry: a smaller mark occupies less
vertical space and its edges may move away from the intruder, which would
contribute the rest. **Whether it does is a MEASUREMENT and is not assumed
here.** What is ruled is the consequence: **step 2 may not be attempted as a
standalone remedy on the theory that shrinking is sufficient.** It is not
sufficient from the requirement side, by arithmetic, and anyone reaching for it
first is reaching for the option that cannot work alone.

**AY2(d) — the front is 28.80 mm and every ruling that says 35.00 mm is
describing a container this repository does not compose.** §AU3 assumed 35.00.
§AX1 measured `label_zone` at **28.80**. The horizontal headroom at the floor is
**+12.5138 mm** on the real front, not the +18.7138 mm the 35 mm assumption
produced. **§AU6(c) is LOST either way** — the floor fits with room on both
readings, and the bet named the wrong axis entirely — but the ruled dimension
is now 28.80 mm and any future fit argument uses it.

**AY2(e) — what stays the owner's after this.** The three C2 bars themselves,
unchanged. The choice of *which* element yields, if step 1 turns out to have
two candidates that both fit — that is composition and it is §AE2(c). And the
outcome of step 3, if it is reached: taking the logo off the front is a brand
decision and is referred back, not executed.

---

### AY3 — WHAT THIS SECTION UNBLOCKS, AND WHAT IT POINTEDLY DOES NOT

**Unblocked.** The three shadowed-credential failures, conditionally on AY1's
four steps completing in order. `guarded_commit.sh` as the sole commit path,
permanently, once step 4 passes — this ruling exists partly to retire the
standing excuse rather than to grant one more exception to it. And the C2 row
moves from *"failing with no sanctioned remedy"* to *"failing with a ruled
remedy and a measured constraint on which branch of it can work."*

**NOT unblocked, and named so nobody infers it.** C9, the one front descriptor
line, is still owed by the owner and is still the single string standing
between VQR-3's five elements and a drawn front. **§AU5's ordering is untouched
by this section**: the §AE2(c) guard gets built and gets watched refusing
something before that string is supplied. AY1's guard is a *network* guard and
is a different instrument for a different reservation; building it does not
discharge §AU5 and may not be reported as discharging it.

**No acceptance gate advances.** `owner_acceptance` remains untouchable under
§AE0(a). `pc.vqr3_artwork_composition` is not predicted to VALIDATE by this
section or by any section.

**§AS2(2) still binds.** If the tranche acting on §AY closes with no node
percentage moved, that is a reportable defect and is reported first, before any
of the above is described as progress.

---

### AY4 — THE NAMED BETS

**AY4(a) — the guard is small.** The bet is that an autouse fixture refusing
outbound sockets fits inside the existing eleven-line conftest without
restructuring anything under test. **Loses if** blocking calls requires changing
how the code paths under test are constructed — in which case AY1(c) fires, the
key stays shadowed, and the size is the finding.

**AY4(b) — the empty export is an accident.** **Loses if** BBrose or any record
produces evidence it was deliberate. The owner has ruled it accident on the
balance of a repository-wide search that found it documented nowhere; that is a
ruling and not a measurement, per §AU0(b), and it is recorded as one.

**AY4(c) — step 1 alone clears the collision.** The bet is that there is
vertical budget to move `product-name-0` out of the mark's clear space without
touching the logo. **Loses if** there is not, in which case step 2 runs and
AY2(c) says step 2 needs geometric help to finish the job. **This is the bet
most likely to be lost**, because nothing has measured the vertical budget on a
28.80 mm front, and the last two numbers quoted for this row were both wrong.

**AY4(d) — clearing today's intruder does not surface a third one.** The bet is
that `product-name-0` and `rule-front-single` are the only two elements that
can enter the mark's clear space. **Loses if** a third appears once the first
two are moved — which is the shape §AV6 hit three times in one tranche, each
layer of watching finding a defect the layer before could not see.

---

### AY5 — WHAT §AY DOES NOT DO

It does not name a cause for the empty export beyond ruling it an accident, and
it does not claim to have found who exported it or when. It does not rule C9,
C1, A1, or anything in section B or D. It does not touch A10 or C2's three
bars — both were ruled at §AU2/§AU3 and re-opening a ruled row is not the
executor's and is not being done by the owner either. It does not authorise any
spend; AY1's whole architecture is to make spend structurally unavailable
before a credential becomes available. It does not withdraw §AX, §AW or §AV,
and where AY0 corrects a number in one of them the correction is recorded here
so the original error stays visible in place.

It does not predict that anything validates.
