### §BD(a) — RULING 1: THE DESCRIPTOR GETS ITS OWN SIZE CONSTANT, AT 5.0 pt

> RULING 1 — descriptor size. The descriptor gets ITS OWN size constant, ruled
> at 5.0 pt — the screen/pad-print floor. HERO_SUPPORT_PT stays 3.2 for the
> other tiers; do not touch them. Constant name is the executor's choice; the
> value 5.0 is mine. Rationale I want recorded: the name must lead — 9.0 over
> 5.0 keeps that lead; raising every support tier was a bigger change than the
> defect.

**WHAT WAS ASKED AND WHAT WAS RULED ARE NOT THE SAME SHAPE, AND THAT IS THE
SUBSTANCE HERE.** The queued item asked whether `HERO_SUPPORT_PT` should rise
from 3.2. The ruling declines the question's framing: a new constant is
introduced for one tier, and the tier that prompted the question is the only
tier that moves. **`HERO_SUPPORT_PT` stays 3.2 and the other tiers keep it.**
The net-content tier at 3.2 pt is therefore left below the screen/pad-print
floor by this ruling, knowingly.

**THE NUMBER'S PROVENANCE, STATED SO IT IS NOT LATER MISATTRIBUTED.** The owner
typed *"5.0 pt — the screen/pad-print floor"*. That floor is
`container_production_method._METHOD_DEFAULTS`, where `SCREEN_PRINT`,
`PAD_PRINT`, `CAP_PRINT` and `SHRINK_SLEEVE` each carry `min_text_pt` 5.0 —
bound as governing by **§W2(a)** at :876, whose status is `OWNER_CALIBRATED`.
**It is NOT §W2(b)'s flat 5.0 pt fallback**, which is a different rule that
happens to hold the same number, and which :1437 already warns about
(*"a capability table outranks a fallback"*). Two rules holding one number is
exactly the confusion this file has caught before; the citation above is the
distinction, written down once.

**THE RATIONALE IS RULED CONTENT, NOT COMMENTARY.** The owner asked for it to be
recorded, so it is quoted rather than paraphrased: *"the name must lead — 9.0
over 5.0 keeps that lead; raising every support tier was a bigger change than
the defect."* A later executor proposing to lift `HERO_SUPPORT_PT` for a
different tier must answer that sentence, not merely cite this one's number.

**RESERVED AND DELEGATED, SEPARATELY.** The value 5.0 is owner-reserved. The
constant's identifier is expressly the executor's. Renaming it later is a
refactor; changing it to any other number is a reversal of this ruling and
requires the owner.

### §BD(b) — RULING 2: THE DIRECT-PRINT FRONT WRAPS LONG NAMES

> RULING 2 — the name wraps. The direct-print front wraps long names to two
> lines, as the Decoration branch did. The §AU2 rule position recomputes from
> the wrapped stack — the rule's WEIGHT (0.30/1.0) is ruled and untouchable;
> its position was always derived. A clipped brand name never ships. "Rose
> Nectar Lip Gloss" arriving intact on the emitted front is the acceptance
> evidence.

**THE RULING SEPARATES A RULED QUANTITY FROM A DERIVED ONE, AND THAT SEPARATION
IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART.** §AU2 at :5709 ruled the container front rule at
**0.30 mm** on owner authority. This ruling states that what §AU2 fixed was the
rule's **weight** — 0.30 mm stroke at 1.0 opacity — and that its **position** was
never ruled, only derived from the type stack above it. Consequently a wrap that
changes the stack is permitted to move the rule, and doing so **is not** a
§AU2 amendment. **Any change to 0.30 or to 1.0 remains an §AU2 amendment and
remains owner-reserved.**

**"AS THE DECORATION BRANCH DID" IS PART OF THE RULING.** The owner named an
existing behaviour as the model rather than describing a new one. The record
notes, without ruling on it, that the two branches producing one behaviour from
two independently written implementations is the precise defect class this whole
arc has been about — but **how** that is achieved is an implementation choice
and is not decided here.

**THE ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE IS NAMED BY THE OWNER AND IS FALSIFIABLE.** *"'Rose
Nectar Lip Gloss' arriving intact on the emitted front."* This is measurable
against the emitted document, not against a unit fixture. The observed defect it
answers is on the record at `OWNER_REVIEW_QUEUE.md`: the extracted front carried
`ose Nectar Lip Glos` — clipped at both ends — on the same emission where the
§BB7(a) descriptor `FACIAL SERUM` arrived correctly. **Both facts came from one
measurement**, and this ruling settles the first without disturbing the second.

**"A clipped brand name never ships"** is recorded as the standard, in the
owner's words, and reads on any future front, not only this one.

### §BD(c) — RULING 3: §W2(a) EXTENDS TO ALL INSTRUMENTS, NOT ONLY NAMED ONES

> RULING 3 — §W2(a) extends to ALL instruments. The deny-list discipline
> governs every instrument that measures text on the emitted document, named or
> not. container_production_method._in_artwork is repaired in ITS OWN tranche,
> sequenced immediately after this arc's commits land. New reds from the dark
> check switching on are honest and stand as findings; none are pre-excused.

**THIS RULING CLOSES A DETERMINATION THE FILE DEFERRED AND NEVER CAME BACK TO.**
**§WI-I at :1270-1276** already recorded the exact geometry: front runs *"sit
outside any `Decoration` / `motif-` / `Surface-` group, so §W2's per-surface
floor has never reached them"*, and instructed — *"Determine first whether it is
a wiring fix or a scope question, and say which before you start. If it turns
out to be a scope question, stop and queue it."* **It was determined to be a
scope question, it was queued, and this ruling is the answer to that queue
row.** The deferral is therefore closed by the owner rather than left to lapse.

**WHAT §W2(a) SAID AND WHAT IT NOW SAYS.** §W2(a) at :876 extended the
capability table *"from `product-name*` runs to all runs"*. That wording bound
the SET OF RUNS. It did not bind the SET OF INSTRUMENTS, and a second instrument
was subsequently found selecting its runs by an allow-list of four name
prefixes — reaching a different set of runs than the instrument §W2(a) was
written against, from the same document. **This ruling binds the instruments:
every instrument that measures text on the emitted document is governed,
"named or not."** An instrument written after this date is governed by it
without needing to be added anywhere.

**THE SEQUENCING IS RULED, NOT SUGGESTED.** *"repaired in ITS OWN tranche,
sequenced immediately after this arc's commits land."* The repair does not ride
inside the wiring arc, and it is not deferred indefinitely either.

**THE PRE-COMMITMENT ON THE RESULTS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SENTENCE IN THIS
SUBSECTION.** *"New reds from the dark check switching on are honest and stand
as findings; none are pre-excused."* The count is unknown at the time of ruling
and was not estimated before it. An instrument that has never reached these runs
may report several failures on first contact. **They are findings, they are
kept, and no exemption may be claimed retroactively on the grounds that this
ruling caused them** — causing them is what the ruling is for.

### §BD(d) — MECHANICS THE OWNER SET, TRANSCRIBED WITH THE RULINGS BECAUSE THEY BIND THE ORDER OF WORK

> MECHANICS, same grant as before:
> - Failure 4's == [12.0] → [12.0, 12.0]: once ruling 1 lands, updating it is
>   honest (5.0 clears the real floor) — take it then, not before.
> - Failure 2 (awaiting_container_profile) stands per §BB5(c) — untouched, as
>   you've held it.
> - The 2d8e4e5 count corrections, the §AC siblings, brand_string_runtime.py:9,
>   and the A11 write-up ride per the queue entry.
> - Implement rulings 1 and 2, land the wiring arc green without lowering any
>   bar, then §3 dropper plumbing, then the ruling-3 tranche.

**THE ORDERING CONSTRAINT ON THE FIRST BULLET IS A DISCIPLINE, NOT A
FORMALITY.** Editing a failing expectation before the ruling that justifies it
lands is indistinguishable, in the diff, from editing it because it failed. The
owner's *"take it then, not before"* makes the two distinguishable in the
history. `test_wif_reconstruct_container.py::
TheCapabilityTableGovernsTheTypographyFloorTests::
test_the_floor_adjudicates_and_does_not_merely_record` deliberately repoints the
front zone to a 12.0 pt floor; **the instrument is working correctly and found a
second genuinely-below-floor run.** After §BD(a) lands, the descriptor at 5.0 pt
still sits below that deliberately-inflated 12.0 pt floor, so the second entry
is correct and expected — which is why the update is honest only afterwards.

**"land the wiring arc green without lowering any bar"** is quoted because it is
the constraint under which everything above is to be executed, and it is the one
an executor is most tempted to satisfy by other means.

### §BD(e) — WHAT THIS SECTION DOES **NOT** RULE, LISTED SO SILENCE CANNOT LATER READ AS CLOSURE

§BC(l) established that a row a sitting leaves untouched must still be named, or
a later reader cannot tell it apart from a row that was closed. The same applies
here.

| item | status after §BD |
|---|---|
| **failure 2** — `awaiting_container_profile` vs `awaiting_gate_2` | **UNTOUCHED and still red**, per §BD(d), on the owner's own citation of **§BB5(c)** at :9265. Stated precisely: §BB5(c) rules the `CONTAINER_MOTIF_FAMILY_MISMATCH` **red** stands; this failing state is that red's **downstream consequence** — the flow does not advance to `awaiting_gate_2` because the fidelity check MEASURED_FAILs. The two are not the same object, and §BB5(c)'s standing rule (*"no later tranche may clear this red"*) attaches to the red. **An executor must not make this assertion pass by advancing the state**, which would clear the consequence while leaving the cause |
| **failure 5** — `CONTAINER_MINIMUM_TEXT_SIZE_FAILED` absent from readiness codes | **NOT closed by §BD(c).** §BD(c) rules that the instrument must be repaired; whether the repaired instrument then emits that code on this front is a MEASUREMENT nobody has taken. It is expected. It is not asserted |
| **`HERO_SUPPORT_PT` at 3.2 for `net_content`** | **KNOWINGLY LEFT BELOW the screen/pad-print floor**, per §BD(a)'s *"do not touch them"*. If a later instrument reds on it, that is a finding to bring back, not a licence to raise the constant |
| **the VQR-4 typography axis flip** | **NOT MEASURED and NOT CLAIMED.** The failing assertion stops one line before the axis state is read. §BD(a) is expected to clear it; expectation is not evidence, and the arc's own §AD0(a) prediction is where that gets scored |
| **whether the two branches SHARE wrap code or duplicate it** | **NOT RULED.** §BD(b) names the Decoration branch as the model behaviour. The implementation is the executor's, within §AE |
| **C3, B2, H2** | **UNCHANGED by this section.** C3 stays blocking on licensed font files (§BC(g)); B2 stays blocking and untyped; H2 stays idle-open. Nothing here touches any of them |

## §BE — OWNER-RULED — the two decisions the stop report put and would not propose: the motif red resolves toward green by pinning the pipeline's real behaviour into the record rather than by silencing the checker, and a ruled sequencing yields to a measurement that falsified its premise — with the disclosure-before-ratification order named as the pattern to keep

**RULED BY: BBrose (PROJECT_OWNER) · 2026-08-28 · owner's own typed words**

The stop report at `OWNER_REVIEW_QUEUE.md:10921` priced four routes and proposed
none. These are the rulings on both decisions. Transcribed per §BC: **this
section carries NO implementation.** Each item lands as its own later commit.

### §BE(a) — RULING 1: FAILURE 2 RESOLVES TOWARD GREEN BY RECONCILING THE TEST

> *"failure 2 resolves toward green by RECONCILING THE TEST. I invoke §BB5(c)'s
> own yield clause: my sentence was 'the FAIL stands as a recorded known-red,'
> and I now say what it reaches — the PIPELINE BEHAVIOR stands (the mismatch
> fires, the task parks), and the RECORD asserts that behavior verbatim. Update
> the test to assert `task.status == "awaiting_container_profile"` and the exact
> code list `['CONTAINER_MOTIF_FAMILY_MISMATCH',
> 'SELECTED_CONTAINER_CONCEPT_FIDELITY_FAILED']`. The checker is pinned, not
> silenced: if it ever stops firing, the test goes red. The previous executor's
> four prohibitions narrow to this reading per their own yield clause. AMBER is
> not taken; the register is not touched."*

**WHAT THIS RULING IS, IN THE OWNER'S OWN DISTINCTION.** It separates two things
the stop report ran together: the PIPELINE BEHAVIOUR and the RECORD OF IT. The
behaviour is untouched — the mismatch still fires, the task still parks at
`awaiting_container_profile`, the flow is still halted. What changes is that the
record now ASSERTS that behaviour verbatim instead of asserting a behaviour the
ruling replaced.

**THE YIELD CLAUSE IS INVOKED BY ITS AUTHOR-IN-INTEREST, WHICH IS THE ONLY WAY
IT COULD BE INVOKED.** §BB5(c):9287-9288 reads *"If the owner meant something
narrower, the owner's sentence governs and this clause yields to it."* The four
prohibitions were the previous executor's construction and were labelled as such
at :9279-9281. The owner has now said what his sentence reaches. **The executor
did not narrow them; the owner did.** This is the distinction §BB5(c):9289-9290
exists to protect — *"an executor finding this red and 'fixing' it has defeated
the instrument, not the defect"* — and it is not engaged here, because the
narrowing came from the ruling and not from the executor's convenience.

**THE PINNING IS THE CONSIDERATION.** The ruling does not merely permit the test
to stop failing; it requires the test to assert the exact code list, so the
checker is held in place by a positive assertion. **If the checker ever stops
firing, the test goes red.** That is a stronger instrument than the one being
replaced, which asserted only that the flow completed and would have said
nothing at all about the codes.

**AMBER IS DECLINED ON THE RECORD.** The executor's corrected route (D)
established that AMBER exists, is reachable, and is the owner's to grant. The
owner has read it and not taken it, and the flake register is not touched. That
refusal is transcribed because a lever offered and declined is a fact about the
record; a lever never named is a gap in it.

### §BE(b) — RULING 2: §BD(c)'s SEQUENCING YIELDS TO THE MEASUREMENT

> *"§BD(c)'s sequencing yields to the measurement. The premise ('dark check
> switching on') was falsified: the check was lit at HEAD and the arc is what
> turns it dark. The `_in_artwork` repair RIDES IN THE ARC, ratified. The
> disclosed deviation was the right call; record that the
> disclosure-before-ratification order is the pattern I want kept."*

**A RULED ORDER IS SET ASIDE BY THE MEASUREMENT THAT FALSIFIED ITS PREMISE, NOT
BY THE EXECUTOR'S PREFERENCE.** §BD(c) sequenced the repair into "ITS OWN
tranche, immediately after this arc's commits land," and the clearance
transcription added "THE SEQUENCING IS RULED, NOT SUGGESTED." Its stated cause
was *"the dark check switching on."* Measured on production output: at HEAD the
front sat inside `Decoration` and WAS measured, at 8.0 pt across two runs; the
repair is INERT there (6 runs → 6, the identical set); and the WIRED front is
invisible to the old list (4) and visible to the repaired one (7). The check was
lit, and the arc is what turns it dark. **The repair rides in the arc, ratified.**

### §BE(c) — THE PATTERN THE OWNER WANTS KEPT, RULED AS A STANDING PRACTICE

> *"the disclosure-before-ratification order is the pattern I want kept."*

The executor made the deviation, **named it as a deviation** rather than
explaining it away, disclosed that the decision was taken before the sequencing
was re-read — *"which is the honest order to admit rather than the flattering
one"* — and brought it for ruling. The owner ratified it after the fact. **The
order of those steps is now itself ruled: disclose first, in the deviation's own
name, and let ratification follow.** A deviation disclosed and later ratified is
a governed act; the same deviation ratified silently is an ungoverned one, and
the two are indistinguishable in the diff.

### §BE(d) — THE MECHANICS, AND THE ONE DECISION EXPRESSLY RESERVED

> *"Land the wiring arc green through the real gate, full §AD0(a) prediction set.
> The reconciled test's docstring must carry why it asserts a red-shaped state:
> §BB5(c) + this ruling."*
>
> *"§3 dropper plumbing next — with one instruction: the dropper fixture carries
> a DIFFERENT product's copy (NIGHT REPAIR OIL). Do not overwrite one product's
> copy with another's. If §3 needs a per-product source for the hierarchy rather
> than the ruled FACIAL SERUM literal, that is a measured proposal to bring back,
> not a decision to make. Everything short of that decision, execute."*
>
> *"Batch per §Q; consolidated report at the end."*

**THE RESERVED DECISION IS NAMED SO IT CANNOT BE DRIFTED INTO.** Whether the
front hierarchy gains a PER-PRODUCT source in place of the ruled `FACIAL SERUM`
literal is **owner-reserved**. The executor may measure it, price it, and bring
it back; the executor may not decide it. Everything short of that line is
authorised.

## §BF — OWNER-RULED — §3 CLOSES on the schema question rather than the source question: the two fronts have different lockup grammars BY DESIGN, so the dropper keeps its own and the ruled hierarchy stays plumbed and unfed as its INTENDED END STATE rather than an unfinished one — and the reserved source question is deferred behind a named trigger instead of being answered

**RULED BY: BBrose (PROJECT_OWNER) · 2026-08-28 · owner's own typed words**

The measured proposal at `OWNER_REVIEW_QUEUE.md:11330` priced three wirings and
recommended none. This is the ruling on it. Transcribed per §BC: **this section
carries NO implementation.** It happens to require none — see §BF(c).

### §BF(a) — THE RULING

> *"The dropper's support line is NOT the container's descriptor tier. The two
> fronts have different lockup grammars and that is by design: the dropper's
> RANGE + VARIANT lockup stands as-is (Option 0). FACIAL SERUM stays scoped to
> the serum container front. The hierarchy plumbing stays in place, unused and
> mutation-guarded — it activates only for a product whose record carries a
> descriptor, and sourcing that per-product is a future ruling when a real
> second product forces it, not now. No overwrite, no duplication, no new work.
> §3 is CLOSED."*

### §BF(b) — WHAT WAS RULED IS THE PRIOR QUESTION, WHICH IS WHY §3 CAN CLOSE AT ALL

The reserved question was *where the hierarchy comes from*. The proposal
reported that a prior question sat under it — whether the dropper's support line
is the container's descriptor tier — because the two composers carry different
SHAPES of copy: `ruled_front_hierarchy` yields FULL NAME + CATEGORY, and the
dropper front's two slots hold RANGE + VARIANT.

**The owner ruled the prior question, and that is what closes §3.** The source
question is not answered here; it is DEFERRED, and §BF(e) records the trigger.
A section that closes by answering a different question than the one it opened
with is worth flagging as such, because the reserved question is still open and
must not be read as settled by this closure.

**"Different lockup grammars, and that is by design"** is the substance. It
converts an apparent inconsistency between two composers into a ruled property
of the product line. The dropper is not a container that failed to get its
descriptor; it is a different lockup.

### §BF(c) — THE RULING SELECTS OPTION 0 AND THEREFORE REQUIRES NO CODE

`caaf6c4` landed the plumbing DELIBERATELY UNFED, and Option 0 is exactly the
state it landed in. So *"no new work"* is literally true: the ruled end state is
the shipping state, byte-for-byte. **Nothing implements this ruling because
nothing needs to.**

This is the third time in this arc that the correct response to a measurement
has been to change nothing, and the owner has now named that pattern. It is
recorded here so the next executor does not read an unfed mechanism as an
unfinished one and "complete" it.

### §BF(d) — THE OWNER TOOK THE EXECUTOR'S PREMISE AND REJECTED THE CONSEQUENCE ATTACHED TO IT

This is the part the executor got wrong and it is recorded rather than smoothed
over.

The proposal offered three readings. Reading (i) was: *"the dropper's support
line is NOT the container's descriptor tier, in which case §3's plumbing should
be fed with the name tier only and the duplication in Option B is a separate
copy question."*

The owner ruled the FIRST half of (i) and discarded the second. Feeding the name
tier only IS Option B, which prints "Night Repair Oil" twice — and the executor
had bundled that duplication into reading (i) as an acceptable follow-on cost,
filed as "a separate copy question". **The owner's ruling does not pay that cost
at all**: if the two fronts have different grammars by design, there is no reason
to push the container's name tier through the dropper's name block either. The
premise does not imply the consequence, and the executor coupled them.

The lesson is narrow and worth keeping: **a priced option and the reading that
motivates it are two different objects.** The proposal presented three readings
each welded to one wiring, which made the option set look exhaustive when it was
not — Option 0 was listed as "today, what ships" rather than as a candidate any
reading might select. It was the one the owner chose. A pricing exercise that
frames the status quo as the baseline rather than as an option biases toward
change, and this one did.

### §BF(e) — THE DEFERRAL IS CONDITIONAL, AND THE CONDITION IS NAMED

Two forward-looking clauses bind, and neither is work now:

**(1) The activation condition.** *"It activates only for a product whose record
carries a descriptor."* This is now the ruled semantics of the `hierarchy_lines`
parameter on `compose_dropper_sheet` — not "unwired pending a decision" but
"wired, dormant, and conditioned on a per-product fact that no current product
has". The two mutation-proved guards that fail if a production caller starts
feeding it are therefore **guards on a ruled boundary**, not scaffolding around
an unfinished feature, and they must not be relaxed by a future executor who
reads them as the latter.

**(2) The trigger for the deferred source question.** *"Sourcing that per-product
is a future ruling when a real second product forces it, not now."* The reserved
question returns when a real second product carrying a descriptor exists —
**not** when an executor judges the abstraction ready, and not on the strength of
a fixture. FB3093's dropper is not that product; its copy is this product's own.

**FACIAL SERUM stays scoped to the serum container front.** The literal is not
promoted to a shared source, and the §BD(a) 5.0 pt ruling on the container's
descriptor tier is untouched and continues to govern only that front. The 3.4 pt
`SUPPORT_PT` on the dropper is not in tension with it, because they are not the
same tier — which is the ruling.

### §BF(f) — WHAT REMAINS OPEN AFTER THIS SECTION, SO THE CLOSURE IS NOT READ TOO WIDELY

§3 is closed. These were raised alongside it and are NOT closed by it:

- The per-product descriptor source — deferred behind the trigger above.
- `compose_dropper.py`'s product-copy literal is unregistered in
  `reserved_copy.py`. The proposal called it "part of the priced decision rather
  than separable from it". That is no longer true: with Option 0 ruled, the
  literal is permanent shipping copy, which makes registering it a plain
  carried-forward item rather than a consequence of an open decision. It stays
  queued and untouched.
- The three findings that rode in the same queue entry — the §Y2 classifier's
  blind spot, the brand register's inability to distinguish an unregistered kind
  from a negative test's invalid one, and the transcribing-double defect class —
  are unaffected by this ruling and remain as recorded.

## §BG — OWNER-RULED — the three calls the §6 sitting left open: the blind instrument is repaired FIRST and ALONE so that every later number is read off a fixed gauge, a percentage the executor refused to move unilaterally is ruled a MEASUREMENT CORRECTION rather than a bar move and therefore moves, and the one item that would have needed a gate overridden is refused — and the executor's own claim about what would have caught the drift is scored FALSE here, because it would have caught nothing

**RULED BY: BBrose (PROJECT_OWNER) · 2026-08-28 · owner's own typed words**

The §6 sitting measured the programme, reported true percentages, and put three
decisions to the owner without taking any of them. These are his rulings on
them. Transcribed per §BC: **this section carries no implementation.** Unlike
§BF, it does require some — and none of it is in this commit. §BG(f) says which
commits carry what and why they are separate.

### §BG(a) — THE RULINGS, VERBATIM

> **RULING 1 — P0 approved, first and ALONE.** Repair the palettes blindness
> (program_view + computed_views entry, so the drift-checker visits it and the
> display prints its row) as its own commit. Every other §6 item waits until the
> repaired instrument is the one measuring. After P0 lands green, report the
> corrected rollup and the full priced push proposal — I rule the push order
> then, not now.
>
> **RULING 2 — watch_corpus.validation_percent moves to the MEASURED value,
> 1/118.** This is a measurement correction, not a bar move: the honest number
> is the one the record keeps. Record the rollup shift it causes as the
> correction's known consequence, with this ruling as authority.
>
> **RULING 3 — no override on expanded_component_library.** The
> post-acceptance gate stands in its own words. The §6 push proceeds on the
> other items; the library starts when acceptance unblocks, not before.
>
> **MECHANICS:** score commit G's prediction when the gate lands before starting
> P0. Rulings 1 and 2 may share a commit only if the tracker edit is one
> coherent record change per §AC's own test; otherwise separate. Same grant,
> same stop conditions, measure-first, batch per §Q.

### §BG(b) — RULING 1 RULES A SEQUENCE, NOT A REPAIR, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING

The repair itself is two fields. What the ruling actually decides is **the order
in which a measurement and its instrument may be trusted**: *"Every other §6
item waits until the repaired instrument is the one measuring."*

The §6 proposal had put P0 first on efficiency grounds — it is the cheapest item
and it unblocks reporting. The owner's reason is different and better. Every
other §6 item is scored by a rollup table that was, at the time the proposal was
written, **omitting the programme's second-heaviest domain**. A push order
argued from that table is an argument from a gauge known to be wrong. So P0 is
not first because it is cheap; it is first because nothing measured before it
counts.

The measured shape of what was wrong, so the ruling is legible without the
proposal in hand:

| | |
|---|---|
| `palettes` weight | **0.152542 — 15.25% of the entire programme** |
| rank among `design_os`'s 17 children | **2nd**, behind `pc` (0.169492) |
| `program_view` | absent → no row at `roadmap_status.py:507`, no entry at `:489 --json` |
| `computed_views["palettes"]` | absent → never visited by the drift-checker at `:398` |
| what the instrument said about all this | **`tracker valid`** |

The two sets — *displayed* (roots ∪ `program_view`) and *cached*
(`computed_views` keys) — differ by **∅ in both directions** across all 107
nodes. Sixteen program nodes, seventeen cached views, `design_os` being a root
that needs no flag. `palettes` was the single node missing from **both**, which
is precisely why the omission read as consistency: an instrument that is wrong
in exactly one place, in both of its two registers at once, is internally
coherent and externally blind.

**Why it was missed is visible in the data and is not a mystery.** Every other
child of `design_os` carries `domain` equal to its own id — `brand_gov` →
`"brand_gov"`, `ire` → `"ire"`. `palettes` carries `domain: "target"`. It was
added on a different axis from the domain nodes and never inherited their
reporting wiring.

**No number was ever wrong.** `rollup()` at `:181` walks `parent_id` and nothing
else, so `palettes` has always been inside `design_os`'s arithmetic. What was
missing was the **row** and the **check**, not the sum. The P0 commit asserts
this rather than claiming it: all five percentages on all 107 nodes are compared
before and after and the script fails if any moved.

### §BG(c) — RULING 2 IS RULED A MEASUREMENT CORRECTION, AND THE EXECUTOR'S OWN CLAIM ABOUT ITS CONSEQUENCE IS SCORED **FALSE** HERE

The ruling settles a question the executor had refused to settle. `H020` is
wired from the watch corpus and cites it by name in the code at
`apps/ire/handoff/package.py:185`, so the corpus has one hook wired, not zero.
The §4(e) repair **reported** that, annotated the `0`, and refused to move it,
on the reasoning that a percentage an executor believes is correct is still a
bar move and bar moves in this arc are proposed rather than taken.

The owner's ruling rejects the framing, not the caution: *"This is a measurement
correction, not a bar move: the honest number is the one the record keeps."*
The distinction is now on the record and is worth stating plainly — **moving a
number to what was measured is not the same act as moving a number to what one
would like it to be**, and only the second needs a ruling. §4(e) treated them as
the same act. That was over-cautious rather than wrong, and the ruling corrects
it.

**Now the part that is an executor error, recorded rather than smoothed over.**

The §6 proposal stated that moving `watch_corpus.validation_percent` 0 → 1
*requires* updating the cached `computed_views` for `brand_gov` and `design_os`
**"or `:398` drift fires."** That claim is **false**. Measured at HEAD:

| node | cached | recomputed after the correction | drift | `ROLLUP_TOLERANCE` | fires? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `brand_gov` validation | 70.2 | 70.30000000000001 | **0.100** | 0.51 | **no** |
| `design_os` validation | 63.9 | 63.866968887996485 | **0.033** | 0.51 | **no** |

Neither drift is within an order of magnitude of firing. `design_os`'s cached
value does not even change — it rounds to 63.9 both before and after — so
**exactly one cached number moves in the whole tracker: `brand_gov` 70.2 →
70.3.** The cache is updated because the record should be true, **not** because
a guard compels it. The executor asserted a guard would compel it without
measuring the guard, in the same sitting whose entire subject was records that
decay because nothing checks them.

**And the reason it would not fire is itself a finding.**
`roadmap_status.py:43` reads:

```python
ROLLUP_TOLERANCE = 0.51          # stored caches are rounded to 1 decimal
```

Caches rounded to one decimal admit at most **0.05** of rounding error. The
constant is **10.2× looser than its own stated justification** — it is sized for
integers while its comment describes tenths. The gap is not theoretical: it is
exactly the band a genuine one-point correction to a 10%-weighted child lands
in. A drift-checker whose tolerance is ten times its own rationale can watch
half a percentage point of real error go past and report `tracker valid`.

This is the same *shape* as the finding §4(e) recorded about
`PALETTE_TOLERANCE_DE = 25.0` — "an order of magnitude looser than a brand
tolerance" — and it is the second tolerance in this repository found to be
loose against its own comment. **It is NOT fixed here.** A constant is code,
§AC forbids chaining it onto a record commit, and no ruling authorises it. It is
proposed and it waits.

### §BG(d) — RULING 3 REFUSES AN OVERRIDE THE EXECUTOR HAD ALREADY DECLINED TO ASK FOR, WHICH IS WHY IT IS SHORT

`brand_gov.expanded_component_library` is gated by its own `next_action` to
begin after acceptance, and acceptance is BLOCKED by
`BLOCKING_RECONSTRUCTION_VISUAL_QUALITY_FAILURE` on `pc.acceptance_outcome`.
The §6 proposal listed it as P5 and simultaneously said it must **not** be
pushed, because starting it requires overriding a gate and that is a ruling, not
an executor's call.

The owner did not override it: *"The post-acceptance gate stands in its own
words."*

The clause that binds forward is *"the library starts when acceptance unblocks,
not before"*. This is now a **ruled** precondition rather than an inherited
`next_action` string, which means it may not be reopened by an executor who
judges the dependency soft, and may not be routed around by starting "part of"
the library under another name. The §6 push proceeds on the other items.

### §BG(e) — A SCOPE QUESTION THE EXECUTOR SURFACED INSTEAD OF DECIDING SILENTLY

The §6 proposal's P0 had **two** halves: the tracker edit, and a new check in
`roadmap_status.py` that fails when a direct child of a root has neither
`program_view` nor a `computed_views` entry — the durable fix, so the hole
cannot reopen.

RULING 1's parenthetical names only *"program_view + computed_views entry"*.
The guard is **code**, and §AC forbids code in a record commit.

Rather than resolve that by picking the reading that let more work through, it
is recorded here and resolved the narrow way: **P0 lands tracker-only, and the
guard is re-proposed separately as its own priced item.** If the owner meant the
guard to ride along, it costs one line to say so and nothing has been done that
must be undone. The reverse — landing code inside a commit ruled to be "its own
commit" for a record repair — could not be undone by a sentence.

This matters beyond the instance. A parenthetical in a ruling is a **scope**,
not a summary, and an executor reading it as a summary can widen a ruled
boundary while believing it is being faithful to intent.

### §BG(f) — THE MECHANICS, AND WHY THIS IS THREE COMMITS AND NOT ONE

The owner's mechanics were followed in order.

**Commit G's prediction was scored before P0 was started**, as instructed. It
landed as `4f4d3a2`, **8 of 8 legs true** — `collected=7653` unchanged,
`failures=0`, `7650 passed / 3 skipped`, `TIER_2=GREEN`, `41596` subtests,
`protocol_identity 4ab5331b49fbd923` unmoved, `2 files changed`, `1` ledger
line. That is **fifty-six consecutive legs across seven commits**. The run also
gave `2cc0b13`'s redirect-safety fix its first live exercise:
`.suite_gate_output` came through at **198 bytes intact**, written at 16:12 and
still whole at 16:23 after the tier-2 stage that used to truncate it to 0.

**On whether Rulings 1 and 2 may share a commit** — the owner's test is whether
the tracker edit is *one coherent record change*. It is not. They touch
different nodes in different domains and they are different **kinds** of act:
RULING 1 makes a node visible and moves **no** number; RULING 2 moves a number
and its rollup. Merging them would put the sitting's only percentage movement in
the same diff as a repair that rests on the claim that nothing moved — and the
attribution of that 70.2 → 70.3 to its ruling is the whole point of recording it
as a known consequence. *"First and ALONE"* also reads literally. **Separate.**

**On why this transcription is not in P0 either** — the register's own precedent
is unambiguous: `8e47f6f`, `df73f84`, `85aa631`, `04b9ffb`, `1a65a5a` and
`eaf333c` each landed a transcription touching only this file (sometimes
`OWNER_REVIEW_QUEUE.md`) and the gate ledger. None mixed a transcription with a
tracker edit. And under §BC a ruling is not on the record until it is in this
file, so a P0 commit citing RULING 1 as its authority should not be the commit
that first puts RULING 1 on the record. **Transcription first is not P0 losing
its "first" — P0 is first among the §6 work; this is the bookkeeping that makes
the ruling citable at all.**

The order is therefore: **this section → P0 (RULING 1, tracker-only) → RULING 2
(tracker-only) → the corrected rollup and the full priced push proposal.**

### §BG(g) — WHAT THIS SECTION DOES NOT CLOSE

Raised alongside these rulings, unaffected by them, and **not** to be read as
settled:

The owner's sentence *"The defect was never the decision; it was that its only
authority was the body of commit 2d4b89d"* settles a question §BG left open and

reclassifies it: the record was correct to refuse the decision, because the
decision had never been placed where the record could see it. `2d4b89d` was a
real approval that had been filed in the one location §BC does not read. The

decision announced in a commit body is not half-recorded, it is unrecorded. The
fix is never for an executor to honour it anyway — it is to get it transcribed.

### §BH4(f) — THE EXACT COUNT, COMPUTED AT TRANSCRIPTION TIME

§BH4(b) orders the number computed now, from the records, at the moment of
transcription — so it is fixed here rather than left to drift into the commit
that reports it. The owner's "~101" and "~41" were his arithmetic on a
derivation reported to him under uncertainty. Both are now confirmed exactly,
and the uncertainty that qualified them is resolved.

**IDENTITY-BACKED — 60 renders, auditable from the committed records:**

    raw_sc.json                12 occurrences   12 distinct render_identity
    raw_mvs_sheen.json         12               12
    raw_pvm_sheen.json         12               12
    raw_lobe.json              24               24
                               --               --
                               60               60      zero shared

**DERIVATION-ONLY — 41 renders, carrying no render_identity in any record:**

    raw_glitter.json            0 render_identity   self-declares
                                                    "renders_this_phase": 22
    raw_flake.json              0 render_identity   18 members
                                                    + 1 mirror commissioning
                                                    = 19
                                                    --
                                                    41

**TOTAL 101 RENDERS AGAINST A CEILING OF 80 — over by 21, at 126% of cap.**

**THE MIRROR IS ONE RENDER, NOT 48.** This was the one open question when the
stop was reported, and it decided whether the derived total was ~101 or ~148.
`palette_characterization_protocol.measure_under` is documented *"One
measurement under one sub-rig"*, and its `samples=` argument is written into the
renderer's own config as `cfg["samples"]` — it is the sample count **inside** a
single render, not a count of renders. The flake phase's mirror call therefore
contributes exactly 1. The owner's "~41" was right and is now exact.

**CORROBORATED BY A SECOND, INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENT.** The derivation above reads
the driver's control flow. The scratch tree measures the same quantity by
counting artifacts, and agrees without adjustment:

    var/m6_spreads_frames/flake_ensembles     19 .exr
                                              = 3 families x 6 seeds
                                                + flake_mirror_reference.exr
    var/m6_spreads_frames/glitter_event       22 .exr
                                              = "renders_this_phase": 22

**THE LEDGER'S 66 RECONCILES EXACTLY — WHICH IS THE POINT.** The counter was
never sloppy. It was precise in a unit that was never declared, and three
different units were summed into one integer:

    phase          counted as                    counted   rendered
    ------------   ---------------------------   -------   --------
    sc             6 member-PAIRS                      6         12
    mvs_sheen      6 member-PAIRS                      6         12
    pvm_sheen      6 member-PAIRS                      6         12
    lobe           24 member-MEASUREMENTS (1:1)       24         24
    glitter        6 trios                             6         22
    flake          18 members (mirror uncounted)      18         19
                                                     ---        ---
                                                      66        101

66 against 80 reads as 14 renders of headroom remaining. The true figure was 21
renders past the cap. **The counter did not fail to add up; it added up
perfectly in an undeclared unit, which is why nothing caught it.**

### §BH4(g) — THE DOCSTRING EVIDENCE §BH4(b) REQUIRES

`apps/pipeline/services/palette_m6_spreads_driver.py`, `run_lobe_ensemble_phase`
docstring:

> *"24 member-measurements counted (harder than the texture phases' per-pair
> unit — the ceiling cannot be snuck past)."*

The hazard was **seen, named, and reasoned about** — at one phase. The author
understood that the per-pair unit was the looser one, deliberately chose the
stricter unit at `lobe`, and wrote down why. The defect is not ignorance. It is
that a hazard identified at one site was corrected only at that site, while the
five other phases kept the loose unit and two of them invented further units
still. The strictest phase in the campaign is the one that proves the problem
was understood.

### §BH4(h) — THE CLASS IS NEW AND MUST BE REGISTERED

§BH4(b) says *"file this under the unit-mismatch defect class (or register the
class if it does not exist)."* **It does not exist** — searched across `*.py`,
`*.json` and `*.md` from the git root, grep's own exit status read directly
rather than through a pipe: no hits. The clause fires; the class gets registered.

    UNIT_MISMATCH — a counter that is internally honest in a unit nobody
    declared, measured against a ceiling denominated in a different unit.
    Every individual increment is defensible. The sum is meaningless. No
    arithmetic check can catch it, because the arithmetic is correct; only
    naming the unit catches it.

It is a sibling of the two classes already on the record, and the family
resemblance is exact: `TWO_ROOTS_MEASUREMENT` returns a clean confident false
result because the *aperture* was wrong, `UNIT_MISMATCH` returns a clean
confident false result because the *unit* was wrong. **Both defeat the reviewer
by being internally consistent.** A wrong path errors; a wrong unit balances.

### §BH4(i) — A SECOND DEFECT, ALREADY-CLASSED, FOUND WHILE COUNTING

Stated because it materially cheapens §BH4(d) and the owner should price the
build knowing it.

`render_identity` is **not missing from glitter and flake. It is computed for
every one of the 101 renders and then discarded by two of the six phases.**
`measure_under` builds it at `palette_characterization_protocol.py:386` —
`sha256(label + lighting_contract_identity)[:16]` — for every render without
exception, flake and glitter included, since both reach the renderer through
that one function. The texture phases keep it: `driver.py:223`,
`"render_identity": d.get("render_identity")`. The flake and glitter row-builders
assemble their rows from `member`, `seed`, `axes`, `subject_peak` and let it go.

That is `CAPTURE_WITHOUT_RETENTION`, a class already on the record. §BH4(d)'s
*"render_identity emitted by every phase"* is therefore **retention, not
instrumentation** — the value already exists at the point where the row is
built.

**And the 41 are corroborated only by scratch that is designed to be deleted.**
`var/` is git-ignored (`.gitignore:66`), holds zero tracked files, and is marked
`NOT_A_RECORD (A403)` in the driver itself. The four identity-backed phases have
**no** frames left on disk — already cleaned — and are fully auditable anyway,
because their identities are in the records. Flake and glitter are the exact
inverse: artifacts present, identities absent. **The moment `var/` is cleaned,
the honest count of those 41 renders stops being recoverable by any means.** The
owner's "countable only by derivation, not audit" is exactly right, and it has a
clock on it.

### §BH4(l) — THIS TRANSCRIPTION'S FIRST COMMIT CLAIMED IT AND DID NOT CARRY IT

Recorded here rather than quietly re-committed, because the §BC register is the
authority record for §BH4 and a reader tracing this ruling to its commit must
not be sent to a commit that does not contain it.

**What happened.** Commit `8ed9068` was made as commit O of this arc. Its
message describes this transcription in detail. Its content is **one line of the
gate's own ledger and nothing else** — 1 file changed, 1 insertion. The 255
lines above it were written to disk and never staged, so `git commit` captured
an index that did not include them.

**Why nothing caught it — and this is the part worth keeping.** The gate ran and
returned `TIER_2=GREEN collected=7653 failures=0`, and that verdict was
*correct*: the suite runs against the **working tree**, where the 255 lines were
present the whole time. The commit then captured the **index**, where they were
not. **The gate measures one object and the commit records a different one, and
nothing in the sanctioned path checks that the two agree.** A green gate is
evidence about the tree. It is not, and has never been, evidence about what the
commit contains.

`tools/guarded_commit.sh` is not at fault and says so in its own comment at
line 318: *"staging is the caller's act and this script only ever ran `git
commit` on an index it did not build."* The contract was documented, and this
executor did not honour it.

**The near miss.** Commit K (`cebe16d`) transcribed §BH1–§BH3 into this same
git-root file and carried 208 insertions correctly, so the arc's history is
intact and no earlier ruling is missing from the record. The four commits
before this one were each verified to contain their stated content. **This
failure is a one-off caller error, not a hole in the arc** — but it was
invisible to every instrument in the path, and it would have stayed invisible if
the diffstat had not been read line by line against a prediction.

**What it cost and what it did not.** No ruling was lost — the owner's words
were on disk throughout and are committed by the commit that carries this note.
Nothing was overwritten, nothing was re-run, and no measurement changed.

**Not minted as a defect class here.** The failure has the shape of one, and the
name it would take is obvious enough to write down —
`GATE_AND_COMMIT_MEASURE_DIFFERENT_OBJECTS`. It is deliberately **proposed, not
minted**: §BH4(b) authorised minting `UNIT_MISMATCH` and authorised nothing
else, minting is a deliberate act under §AC, and a class invented by an executor
to describe its own mistake, inside the commit repairing that mistake, is
exactly the kind of unilateral scope creep this arc's discipline exists to
prevent. **It is raised for the owner's disposition.**

The mechanical guard it implies is one line and is likewise proposed only:
before committing, assert that the caller's intended paths are actually staged —
`git diff --cached --name-only` compared against the act's declared write set.

## §BH6 — LINE 34 GOVERNS P1'S IDENTITY, THE STALE `counts` BLOCK IS A FINDING AND NOT A CORRECTION, AND THREE SELF-CAUGHT DEFECTS GO ON THE RECORD INCLUDING THE ONE ABOUT AN EXPLANATION ACCEPTED BECAUSE IT FIT

**§AC IS OBSERVED: THIS SECTION IS THE RULING AND CARRIES NO IMPLEMENTATION.**

### §BH6(a) — P1 IDENTITY: LINE 34 GOVERNS

> **§BH6(a) — P1 IDENTITY: LINE 34 GOVERNS.** The launcher's literal value
> (fd10bee04a2f9cbe) was a description of past state, not a pin. P1's first

**What this settles.** The work order's literal value and the authority the work
order cited for it disagreed, and the owner resolves it in favour of the
authority: P1's first act is required to name a pin computed at execution time,
whatever any prose says the value is.

**AND THE VALUE IS WORSE THAN STALE — IT IS THE WRONG KIND OF NUMBER.** A first
draft of this subsection read that `fd10bee04a2f9cbe` *"is not wrong about
anything — it is a true description of the identity as of the moment the
launcher was written — it is simply not a pin."* **That was measured false with
this commit's own gate already running**, which is commit P's precedent applied
a second time, and the sentence is quoted here rather than deleted because a
register that silently swallows its own drafts is worth less than one that
shows them. `fd10bee04a2f9cbe` **was never a protocol identity at all.** It is
the *record digest* of `spreads_campaign_declaration.json`, and the two live in
different namespaces that happen to share a 16-hex sha256-prefix shape:

| commit | pinned `protocol_identity` | that record's stored digest |
|---|---|---|
| `2859732` | `4fe211b5837c1645` | `fd10bee04a2f9cbe` |
| `04d5b44` (P) | `b9272465dbe49f31` | `fd10bee04a2f9cbe` |
| `4f3d01b` (Q) | `78c09eeb76cac775` | `87893c1264fd232f` |

At commit P — the window where §BH4(e)'s prose says the bridge
`c1434e1efdb98a62 → fd10bee04a2f9cbe` was *governing* — the protocol identity
was `b9272465dbe49f31`. The pin is the computed identity and it is asserted
green, so this is not an interpretation. **A record digest was written down and
cited as a protocol identity across at least three sites** — this file at
:12983 and :13139, and `spreads_campaign_declaration.json:54`'s
`"superseded_identity"` field. The launcher inherited it and the executor
repeated it.

**The ruling is unaffected, which is the point.** §BH6(a) says name the value
computed at execution time. That instruction is correct whether the launcher's
number was stale, mislabelled, or invented — which is precisely why a rule that
points at a measurement outranks one that points at a value. Nothing in the
correction above touches the owner's words; the blockquote stands exactly as
typed, and his sentence governs.

**Not corrected here, and why.** The three mislabelling sites are left exactly
as written. Two are in ruled sections of this file and one is in a
manifest-tracked record owing the A391 chain; §BH6(b) has just ruled that the
analogous stale number stays put and that a correction needs a fresh ruling of
its own. This subsection records the finding. It does not act on it, and it
does not authorise acting on it.

**The operative consequence, stated so it cannot be read loosely.** P1's first
act does **not** name `fd10bee04a2f9cbe`, and it does **not** name
`78c09eeb76cac775` either. Because §BH5(a)'s mint lands *first* in the ruled
sequence, and because `DEFECT_CLASS_REGISTER` is bound into `protocol_identity()`,

measures at the instant that record is written, after commit S.** It is not
known at the time of this transcription and is deliberately not guessed here.

**Why this was escalated rather than decided.** Naming an identity in a first-act
record is durable and load-bearing; a wrong one is a `DANGLING_AUTHORITY_REFERENCE`
that later readers resolve to bytes that never ran. The divergence was also

**Four things are ruled here, and they are separable.** (1) The block **stays as

### §BH6(c) — THE THREE SELF-CAUGHT DEFECTS, INCLUDING THE UNFLATTERING ONE

> **§BH6(c) — YOUR THREE SELF-CAUGHT DEFECTS.** Record them as reported —

> because it fit the arithmetic, not because it was checked. That sentence

**All three were found by reproducing rather than inheriting, and two of them

**1. A misattributed commit.** The pre-compaction note recorded that the `counts`
lines last changed at `537beeb` (2026-08-10). **False.** They last changed at

because it was carried forward as a settled fact instead of re-measured.

**2. An explanation accepted because it fit.** The declared sum of 31 against 32
table rows had been explained as a principled exclusion of row idx19, a
"permanent record row". Measured: row 32 was appended at `a674e8e` (2026-08-10)
as `BAKED clearance` with status `REPAIRED_RECOMPUTED_ESTABLISHED` — its present

`NOT_ESTABLISHED_FIRED_SUBSTITUTION` status both came later. **There was no
exclusion.** The sentence the owner has ruled stays verbatim:

> **My explanation fit the arithmetic (31 = 32 − 1) and was accepted because it
> fit, not because it was checked.**

The gap is not a principled carve-out. It is the first and smallest instance of
the same staleness, dating from 2026-08-10 rather than 2026-08-15.

**3. A comparator with two silent faults.** The first recheck script (a) collapsed

occurrence inside this arc.

**Why this subsection exists at all.** The owner's reason is recorded in his
words: *"it is the kind of record this register exists to hold."* A register
that only holds defects found in other people's work measures the wrong thing.

### §BH6(d) — THE MEASUREMENTS THIS RULING RESTS ON, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT LATER READ AS RESTING ON RECOLLECTION

**Identity chain (§BH6(a)).** `spreads_campaign_declaration.json:54` carries
`"superseded_identity": "fd10bee04a2f9cbe"`. `test_characterization_protocol.py:561`
records the re-pin at commit Q as `b9272465dbe49f31 -> 78c09eeb76cac775`, mover
being the declaration's own ten inserted lines closing campaign spend; `:575`
asserts `78c09eeb76cac775` and is green in both tier-1 and tier-2.

A first draft of this paragraph continued *"`b9272465dbe49f31` sits between
`fd10bee04a2f9cbe` and the current value, so the declaration's own prose
describing a three-link chain undercounts."* **That is false and is corrected
under §BH6(a) above:** `fd10bee04a2f9cbe` is not a link in the identity chain
and never was, so nothing sits between it and anything. It is the declaration's
own record digest. The measured identity chain across this window is
`4fe211b5837c1645` → `b9272465dbe49f31` → `78c09eeb76cac775`, taken from the
pins, which are asserted green; the declaration's prose is not amended here and
neither is §BH4(e)'s.

**The two namespaces, so this is not repeated a third time.** A protocol
identity is returned by `protocol_identity()` and pinned in
`test_characterization_protocol.py`. A record digest is a field in
`record_digest_manifest.json` and is checked by `record_integrity.py`, which
reports mismatches in the ledger as `RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH`. **Both are 16-hex
sha256 prefixes and neither carries its namespace in its own text**, so a bare
hash quoted in prose cannot be checked against the thing it claims to be. That
is what made this survive: every site that repeated it was quoting a real
number that really existed, just from the wrong register. `record_digest_manifest.json`
at HEAD confirms it — none of `c1434e1efdb98a62`, `fd10bee04a2f9cbe`,
`b9272465dbe49f31` or `78c09eeb76cac775` is a current record digest or prefix,
and no `.py` file is manifest-tracked at all.

**`counts` staleness (§BH6(b)).** The block has changed **exactly once, ever** —
at `d4e8338`, 2026-08-08 — and is byte-identical across all **23** commits that
have touched the file since, including all seven 2026-08-15 adjudication commits
(`51f4381`, `19a3299`, `08fefa2`, `5fd5e98`, `4cf4b79`, `8d32119`, `4815f68`).
Thirteen rows carry a `superseded_2026_08_15` block; **nine** changed status —

`NOT_ESTABLISHED_PENDING_SPREAD` → `ADEQUACY_PRECONDITION_UNMET_DIRECT`, three
`UNMET_BY_CONSERVATIVE_PROXY` → `ADEQUACY_PRECONDITION_UNMET_DIRECT` in place.
Declared against measured: `ESTABLISHED` 10 vs 15 (14 exact plus one long-form
variant), `NOT_ESTABLISHED_PENDING_SPREAD` 11 vs 5,
`ADEQUACY_PRECONDITION_UNMET` 3 vs the renamed `…_DIRECT` at 4.

**Blast radius (§BH6(b), part of the finding's text).** The file has exactly
**three** code readers and **none of them reads `counts`**:
`test_palette_statistics.py:520` takes `A143_forward_identities_2026_08_11`;
`palette_m6_exit_gate.py:161` takes `pair_level_status_downstream_consultation_point`;
`palette_m6_spreads_adjudication.py:54` takes the rows. A search for readers of
the `counts` key returned nothing. No verdict, no gate, and no node number was
ever computed from the stale block.

**Cost of a correction, measured, so the queued item is not later underestimated.**
The file is manifest-tracked: `record_digest_manifest.json` classifies it
`REVISABLE` at digest `75977a56286c0ea6`, 36786 bytes. Editing it moves that
digest and owes the A391 five-step chain.

## §BH7 — P1 NAMES THE DECLARATION IDENTITY (READING A), THE §BH6(a) PARENTHETICAL AND COMMIT T'S FALSE SENTENCE ARE BOTH SUPERSEDED RATHER THAN DELETED, AND THE FIFTH SELF-CAUGHT DEFECT IS THE FIRST ONE THAT WAS A WRONG CORRECTION

**PROVENANCE.** Typed by the owner in this session, in full, as a preamble plus
three lettered rulings — §BH7(a), §BH7(b), §BH7(c) — closing with the standing
caveat *"If I meant something narrower, my sentence governs."* NOT option-picked:
no menu was offered and none was taken. This ruling answers a report-before-acting
that this executor filed after commit S landed. It answers **against** the
executor on nothing and **with** the executor on the identity reading, but it does
so by superseding a clause of §BH6(a) that the executor had itself transcribed —
so the register now records a ruling correcting a ruling, which is the shape §AZ0(u)
exists for.

**LETTER COLLISION — SEARCHED, NOT ASSUMED, AND EMPTY, WITH A NEGATIVE CONTROL.**
The search is recorded, not merely its result, because a search whose key shape is
wrong returns a clean and confident false negative (`TWO_ROOTS_MEASUREMENT`, minted
at commit S).

  * `^## §BH7` as a heading in this register — **0 hits**.
  * bare `BH7` anywhere in this register — **0 hits**.
  * `§BH7` across tracked `.md`/`.py`/`.json`/`.sh`/`.txt` — **0 hits**.
  * bare `BH7` across those same types — **0 hits**.
  * **NEGATIVE CONTROL:** the identical query for `§BH6` returns **31 hits**, so
    the query demonstrably has power and the zero above is a measurement rather
    than a broken pipe.

A first, wider search — bare `BH7` across *all* tracked paths — reported **460
matching files** and had to be discarded. Every hit was inside a binary or
ASCII85-encoded artefact (`.png`, `.exr`, and a PDF whose ASCII85 payload defeats
`git grep -I`'s binary detection, returning 41MB of noise). That is a second live
firing of the same class in the same sitting: the root was right and the KEY SHAPE
was wrong. It is recorded here rather than tidied away.

**§AC IS OBSERVED, WITH ONE SCOPE READING NAMED AT §BH7(f).** §BH7 is one ruling
and lands in one commit. That commit is **U**, and §BH7(c) explicitly scopes U to
carry this transcription *together with* the acts it authorises. That is a
departure from the practice used for §BH5 and §BH6, where the transcription rode
alone ahead of implementation; it is the owner's own scoping sentence and is
followed, and it is named at §BH7(f) so it can be reversed by splitting.

### §BH7(a) — P1 FIRST-ACT IDENTITY: READING A

> **§BH7(a) — P1 first-act identity: A.** The value P1's first act names is the
> DECLARATION identity, 87893c1264fd232f at current HEAD — computed at execution
> time via the canonical declaration_identity() path, exactly as §BH6(a)'s
> sentence already ruled. Line 34 governs. The §BH6(a) parenthetical
> ("post-§BH5(a)-mint value") is hereby superseded per §AZ0(u), reason: it named
> the wrong register. It was inferred from a mislabelled report, and your mint
> measurement proves the two namespaces are independent — the mint moved
> protocol_identity() only. The parenthetical was descriptive and inert; my
> sentence governed then and governs now. Do not delete the parenthetical from
> the register; mark it superseded with this reason. B (dfc98caf984055e3) is a
> protocol identity and must never appear where a declaration identity is
> required — I note your finding that begin_traced_queue would silently accept
> it. That silent-acceptance hole is a FINDING, recorded; any guard for it is a
> separate proposed build, not part of commit U.

**THE SUPERSESSION, RECORDED WITH THE SUPERSEDED TEXT QUOTED VERBATIM.** Per
§AZ0(u) and the owner's explicit *"do not delete"*, the clause is preserved here
in full rather than removed from §BH6(a):

> SUPERSEDED CLAUSE, §BH6(a), quoted verbatim: *"which means the
> post-§BH5(a)-mint value, whatever it measures to when the act runs"*
>
> SUPERSEDED BY: §BH7(a).
> REASON, in the owner's words: **"it named the wrong register."**

The clause's surviving half — *"whatever it measures to when the act runs"* — is
NOT superseded and is the operative instruction. Only the identification of
*which* value moves is withdrawn.

**WHY THE PARENTHETICAL WAS INERT, MEASURED AND NOT ARGUED.** The §BH5(a) mint at
commit `5bb6f74` moved exactly one of the two registers:

| quantity | before commit S | after commit S | moved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `protocol_identity()` | `78c09eeb76cac775` | `dfc98caf984055e3` | **yes** |
| `declaration_identity()` | `87893c1264fd232f` | `87893c1264fd232f` | **no** |

A mint that does not move a value cannot make that value a "post-mint value" in
any sense that distinguishes it from the pre-mint value. The parenthetical was
therefore descriptive of a change that did not occur, exactly as the owner ruled.

**THE TWO NAMESPACES, STATED SO THE CONFUSION CANNOT RECUR BY READING.**

  * `protocol_identity()` — computed over the protocol payload, which binds
    `DEFECT_CLASS_REGISTER` and `EXTENT_DIGESTS`. Pinned in
    `test_characterization_protocol.py`. Moves when the protocol source moves.
  * `declaration_identity()` — `sha256` of the **committed bytes of
    `spreads_campaign_declaration.json`**, first 16 hex, read through
    `git show HEAD:<path>`. Simultaneously that record's entry in
    `record_digest_manifest.json`. Moves when that one record moves.

Both are 16-hex sha256 prefixes. **Neither carries its namespace in its own
text.** That is the whole mechanism of the defect, and it is why the field is
named `declaration_identity` and not `identity`.

**THE SILENT-ACCEPTANCE FINDING, RECORDED AND NOT FIXED.**
`palette_queue_control.begin_traced_queue(queue_name, trace_path, ledger,
declaration_identity)` takes the identity as a **parameter**. It never computes
it. Its only check is falsiness:

> `if not declaration_identity: raise QueueControlError(...)`

A protocol identity is a non-empty 16-hex string and therefore passes. Had this
executor acted on reading B, `dfc98caf984055e3` would have been stamped into a
`declaration_identity` field and **no guard anywhere would have fired**. The
bridge that six executed first acts depend on would have been silently broken.
Per the owner: this is a FINDING, recorded; **any guard for it is a separate
proposed build and is NOT part of commit U.** It is not begun here.

**THE FIFTH SELF-CAUGHT DEFECT, STANDING ON §BH7(b) ALONE.** §BH6(c) is a ruling

> **The first four were wrong facts. The fifth was a wrong CORRECTION.** It took

**WHAT ACTUALLY CAUGHT IT.** Not review, and not the gate. It was caught only

do so — at which point line 46 stated in plain text that the declaration identity
and the record digest are the same string by construction. **A finding that is

**WHAT PREVENTED THE DAMAGE.** §BH6(f) reading 3 left the three flagged sites
untouched, on the restraint precedent the owner set at §BH6(b): findings, not
corrections, absent a fresh ruling. That restraint was adopted for an unrelated
reason and it is the only thing that stopped three correct records from being
overwritten with a false one. **Restraint held under a wrong premise and still
produced the right outcome** — which is the strongest argument in this register
for the finding/correction split.

### §BH8(a) — GATE EXTENT: THE FULL MEASURED 671, NOT 361

### §BH8(e) — WHAT §AZ0(u) ACTUALLY SAYS, MEASURED, BECAUSE THIS RULING CITES IT

**This is recorded because the ruling turns on the citation, not to correct the
owner's intent, which is unambiguous and is executed exactly as typed.**

§AZ0(u) is commonly cited in this project as a rule that corrections must be
*appended*. **Measured, it is not that.** §AZ0(u) runs `:8123-8219` and is an
incident report headed *"I WAS ONE COMMAND AWAY FROM REBUILDING AN INSTRUMENT
THAT ALREADY EXISTS"*. This register **already corrected that misreading twice**,

appending at all."*

Its operative remedy clause, at `:8210-8215`, draws a different distinction
entirely, and it is the one that governs here:

> PLACE.** Two were mine … and are **struck** with the measurement. Three were the
> owner's §AU text … those are **annotated, not rewritten**, because a record of
> what was ruled is not mine to edit.

**So §AZ0(u)'s real distinction is EXECUTOR text versus OWNER text** — struck for
the executor's, **annotated and NOT REWRITTEN for the owner's** — and its common
principle, per `:9680`, is that **the false version stays readable**.

**THIS IS WHY "228" IS NOT EDITED AT §BH5(c).** The figure is the owner's own
typed text — he says so himself, *"is my number"* — and §AZ0(u)'s clause for
owner text forbids rewriting it. Editing `:13271` to read `671` would delete the
superseded figure from the register and destroy exactly the readability §AZ0(u)
exists to preserve. The supersession is therefore recorded at §BH8(d) above,
quoting the false figure verbatim with the owner's reason, and `:13270-13272`
stays byte-identical. **Zero deletions in this commit is the structural proof.**

**A REFINEMENT OF COMMIT U'S OWN CLAIM, MEASURED AND CORRECTED HERE.** Commit U
wrote at `:14013-14014` that *"there is no in-place `[SUPERSEDED]` marker
convention anywhere in this file."* Re-measured: as written that is **true** —
the literal marker occurs zero times, the sole hit at `:14014` being U's own

reading taken here — it is §AZ0(u)'s executor half, behaving exactly as
prescribed, and it strengthens the owner-text conclusion rather than weakening it.

OWNER_BLOCKER_CLEARANCE.md, before acting)"* — so no line of §BH5(c) is touched.

## §BH10 — THE EVIDENCE SET IS THE BUILDERS AND NOT THE CONSUMERS, THE PICKAXE IS RATIFIED IN PLACE OF A LEG THAT CANNOT BE REPRODUCED, AND §BH8(b)'s INSTRUMENT PHRASE IS SUPERSEDED BY QUOTING IT HERE

**PROVENANCE.** Typed by the owner in this session, in full, headed *"OWNER RULING
§BH10"*, as a preamble plus three lettered rulings — §BH10(a), §BH10(b), §BH10(c)
— closing with the standing caveat *"If I meant something narrower, my sentence
governs."* NOT option-picked: no menu was offered and none was taken. This ruling
answers a **stop-and-report filed under §BH8(b)'s own stop condition**, which
reported that the two instruments disagreed in both directions and that the
original instrument pair could not be reproduced. **Both are now settled.**

**LETTER COLLISION — SEARCHED, NOT ASSUMED, AND EMPTY, WITH A NEGATIVE CONTROL.**

  * `^## §BH10` as a heading in this register — **0 hits**.
  * bare `BH10` anywhere in this register — **0 hits**.
  * `§BH10` across tracked `.md`/`.py`/`.json`/`.sh`/`.txt` — **0 files**.
  * bare `BH10` across those same types — **0 files**.
  * **NEGATIVE CONTROL:** the identical queries for `§BH9` return **1 file**, **1
    heading** and **17 in-register hits**, so the queries have power and the zeros
    above are measurements rather than a broken pipe.

### §BH10(a) — THE EVIDENCE SET

> the evidence set is A: modules-edited, EIGHT commits — the seven in both
> instruments plus 4004735. The object evidence_commits names is the work that
> BUILT font governance: commits editing the four font modules and their tests.
> 4004735 is 171 lines into the module itself and enters; the four B-only commits
> are other axes consuming font authority incidentally and do NOT enter — they are
> consumers, not builders. Enter the eight exactly as derived, re-derived by the
> writer at commit time per the house pattern; refuse to write if the set has
> moved. The exclusion of palette_review_fonts.py on substance is ratified.

### §BH10(b) — INSTRUMENTS

> instruments: the pickaxe substitution is RATIFIED. The pair for this set is
> file-history walk + pickaxe scoped to '*.py', divergence diagnosed and
> understood. §BH8(b)'s phrase "the two instruments that already agreed once" is
> superseded by this ruling for this set, reason: the message-grep leg is measured
> unreproducible — no single label scheme covers the eight (WI- sweeps 82 and
> still misses 1712ca9). Record that finding; build nothing for it.

### §BH10(c) — SCOPE

> scope: transcribe this ruling, then P2-b proceeds in one commit as already
> scoped: wiring at __init__.py:1217, fixture proving
> CONTAINER_FONT_LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED fires red-to-green, the eight entered in
> font_governance.evidence_commits. §AD0(a) prediction before the gate. The
> seventh and eighth firings of the measurement-shape class are recorded where the
> house records them; no new defect class unless it fails distinctness both
> directions. Then §BH5(c) at 671, alone and last. If I meant something narrower,
> my sentence governs.

### §BH10(d) — THE EIGHT, RE-DERIVED AT TRANSCRIPTION TIME RATHER THAN COPIED ACROSS

**§BH10(a) requires re-derivation at commit time and refusal if the set has
moved.** That obligation binds the P2-b writer, but the same instrument was re-run
here before these hashes were written into the register, because a set transcribed
from memory is a claim and not a measurement — the same reason §BH9(d) re-measured
its pin rather than carrying it across.

Re-run at `HEAD=c380f4a`: union of the file-history walk over the four paths =
**8 commits**, byte-identical to the set derived before the ruling. **THE SET HAS
NOT MOVED.**

| # | commit | subject |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `882db3b` | WI-N (§AA3): the back of the bottle is printed by an assumption |
| 2 | `75452a9` | WI-G/§Y1/§Y2 — a zone may tighten a floor and may not loosen one |
| 3 | `7de2369` | WI-E/§W1 — the back panel exists at print size |
| 4 | `57d4823` | WI-C/§W2 — the print-method table took the floor off the gate |
| 5 | `95d3de2` | WI-B/§W3 — ONE overlap rule, in one module, read by both axes |
| 6 | `4004735` | WI-A/§W5 — the placeholder allow-list is TWO RUNS |
| 7 | `1c47255` | WI-K/VQR-4 — the typography axis PASSED on three flags nobody measured |
| 8 | `1712ca9` | 2B-3A (1/2): container_font_authority/1.0 + font confirmation gate |

The four paths are `apps/ire/container_font_authority.py`,
`apps/ire/container_typography_metrics.py`,
`apps/pipeline/tests/test_container_font_authority.py`, and
`apps/ire/tests/test_container_typography_metrics.py`.
`apps/pipeline/services/palette_review_fonts.py` was a **name-match false
positive**, read in full and excluded on substance — a 20-line PIL helper loading
Helvetica for review-board labels, not governance work. §BH10(a) ratifies the
exclusion.

### §BH10(e) — WHY THE INSTRUMENTS DIVERGED, AND WHY NEITHER WAS BROKEN

The disagreement was **7 in both, 1 only in A, 4 only in B**, and the cause is
structural rather than defective:

  * **`4004735` is A-only** because it edited `container_typography_metrics.py`
    (**171/27**) and its test (**231/7**) while changing **no occurrence of either
    module-name string**. A module seldom names itself in its own body, so the
    pickaxe is structurally blind to pure body edits.
  * **The four B-only commits** — `f6aaffb`, `5512cdc`, `52aaf4c`, `171e428` —
    changed references in *other* files (`handoff/container_adapter.py`,
    `vq2_artwork.py`, `visual_quality_gate.py`,
    `test_wif_reconstruct_container.py`) **without touching the modules at all**.
    The file-history walk is structurally blind to consumer commits.

So the two instruments were measuring **two different objects** — *edited the
modules* versus *changed references to them* — and measurement could not choose
between them, because the ambiguity was in the phrase and not in the tools.
**§BH10(a) resolves it by naming the object: builders, not consumers.**

**THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE WAS ITSELF NEARLY WRONG, AND THE TELL WAS AN IMPOSSIBLE
COINCIDENCE.** The first diagnostic returned **identical file lists for all five
divergent commits**. That could not be true of five different commits. The query
`git log -1 -S <key> <commit>` walks *backward* from the commit and returns the
first matching ancestor — it never asks about the commit itself. Re-asked as an
explicit single-commit range `C~1..C`, every commit returned a distinct answer,
and only then was the diagnosis above possible. **Had the first run been trusted,
this section would have carried a confident and entirely fabricated cause.**

### §BH10(f) — §BH8(b)'s INSTRUMENT PHRASE, SUPERSEDED BY QUOTING IT HERE

§BH10(b) supersedes a phrase in §BH8(b). Per **§BH9(b)** — *"in-place markers: NO.
The register is append-only for my text. Supersessions live where they were ruled,
quoting the superseded passage"* — the supersession is recorded **here, in the
superseding section**, and **§BH8 is left byte-identical**. No marker line is
placed beside it. The superseded phrase, quoted from the register at `:14077-14078`
so it stays readable:

> *"you do, by measurement, using the two independent instruments that already
> agreed once; if they disagree, stop and report."*

**One precision, recorded rather than smoothed over.** §BH10(b) cites this phrase
as *"the two instruments that already agreed once"*; the register at `:14077`
reads *"the two **independent** instruments"*. The renderings differ by one word.
The owner's §BH10(b) is transcribed above exactly as typed, and §BH8(b) is left
byte-identical, so **both readings stay on the record** and neither was quietly
conformed to the other. The difference is immaterial to what is ruled: the leg
retired is the message-grep, whichever way the pair is named.

**The measurement that retires it.** No single message-label scheme covers the
eight: `--grep 'WI-'` sweeps **82** commits and still catches only **7 of 8**,
missing `1712ca9` because that commit is labelled `2B-3A`; `--grep '2B-3A'`
matches **4**. Negative control `--grep 'ZZQ-NOPE'` returns **0**, so the grep has
power and the failure is real rather than a broken pipe. §BH10(b) rules the
pickaxe scoped to `'*.py'` its ratified replacement **for this set**, and orders
the finding recorded and **nothing built for it** — so nothing is built for it.

### §BH10(g) — A COLLISION THIS RULING ITSELF CREATES, MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS CREATED

**§BH10 is the first two-digit section in the BH series, and that silently breaks
every unbounded prefix search for §BH1.** This was measured on the pre-write file,
while the number was still clean.

`§BH1` is **live**: a real ruling (*G1/HYBRID, decision (a)*), transcribed in
commit K (`cebe16d`), cited **12 times** across `:12740-13213`. Pre-write, bare
`BH1` returned **12** and `BH1[0-9]` returned **0**. After this append, bare `BH1`
returns 12 **plus every `BH10` hit in this section** — silently conflating two
different live rulings, at exit 0, with no error.

**The safe form, verified rather than asserted:** `BH1\([^0-9]\|$\)` returned
**12** pre-write, exactly matching the unbounded count, so the bound does not
under-count. **Control:** the same bounded form applied to `BH9` returned **17**
against an unbounded **17** — equal, as it must be where no two-digit successor
exists. The bound is therefore proved safe in both directions before being relied
upon.

**THE OBVIOUS TEST OF THIS WOULD HAVE FAILED, AND THE REASON IS WORTH THE LINE.**
The natural way to check the bound after the append is *"bounded should still
return 12."* It returns **17**, and the bound is nonetheless correct: **this very
section cites `§BH1` five more times** while describing the hazard, and 12 + 5 =
17. A section that documents a collision necessarily mentions the thing it
protects, so any count-frozen claim about it is self-refuting. **The bound was
nearly declared against a test it was guaranteed to fail** — not because the bound
is wrong, but because the test was.

**THE FIRST REPLACEMENT INVARIANT ALSO FAILED, ON THIS FILE, FOR A THIRD REASON.**
The replacement was stated as *unbounded minus bounded equals the `BH10` count*
using `grep -c` — which counts **matching lines, not occurrences**. The sentence
stating the invariant contains *both* a bounded `BH1` and a `BH10`, so that one
line is counted on both sides and the subtraction fails **by exactly the number of
lines mentioning both**. The claim was refuted by the act of writing it down.

**The invariant that does hold is stated in OCCURRENCES, and its terms are named
rather than frozen:**

> occurrences(`BH1[^0-9]`) + occurrences(`BH10`) == occurrences(`BH1`)

Verified on the committed text at transcription time, with `BH10` confirmed the
only two-digit `BH1x` present. **The measured integers are recorded in this
commit's message and its §AD0(a) prediction rather than here** — because any count
written into this file changes the file it counts, which is the trap the two
previous forms fell into. The form is stable under self-reference; the numbers are
not, so they live outside.

**Anyone auditing §BH1 citations from this commit forward must bound the query.**
This is recorded as a **measurement hazard, not a new defect class** — see
§BH10(h).

### §BH10(h) — THE SEVENTH AND EIGHTH FIRINGS, AND THE DISTINCTNESS TEST §BH10(c) ORDERS

§BH10(c) orders the two firings recorded *"where the house records them"* and
forbids a new defect class *"unless it fails distinctness both directions."*

  * **SEVENTH FIRING — zsh does not word-split unquoted parameters.**
    `git log -- $FILES` returned **0** because zsh passes the whole string as a
    single pathspec, **at exit 0**. Demonstrated both ways: `-- $F` → **0**,
    `-- ${=F}` → **7**. This nearly produced a report of catastrophic instrument
    disagreement that would have been entirely an artefact of the shell.
  * **EIGHTH FIRING — `git log -1 -S <key> <commit>` answers a different question
    than it appears to.** It walks backward from the commit rather than asking
    about it, and returned identical file lists for five distinct commits at exit
    0. Corrected to the range form `C~1..C`.

**DISTINCTNESS TEST, RUN AS ORDERED AND FAILED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** The standing
class is *a query whose SHAPE differs from the question asked, returning a clean

§BH12(a) fixes the producer's cap with two phrases that have to agree: *"ceiling

remains `RIGHTS_REVIEW_REQUIRED` against the app's `LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`:
