### §BH13(f) — THE "APP ENUM" §BH13(a) ORDERS THE CAP ENFORCED AGAINST DOES NOT EXIST, AND "ABOVE THE CEILING" HAS NO DEFINITION IN CODE — BOTH MEASURED HERE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED MID-BUILD

§BH13(a) orders the cap test to *"prove the producer cannot emit any state above
the ceiling, by enumeration against the app enum, not by convention."* Three
things must hold for that instruction to be executable. Measured at
`HEAD=b988bd4`, in `apps/ire/container_font_authority`:

  * **THERE IS NO ENUM.** Module-level collections: **none** — zero tuples, lists,
    sets or frozensets, and no `Enum`. The only collection is `__all__`, **15
    entries**, of which **6** are verification states and the other 9 are gate
    codes, callables and `SCHEMA`. **No collection binds exactly the six states.**
    The six are flat module constants, each a plain `str`.
  * **THERE IS NO ORDERING.** No name in the module contains `RANK`, `ORDER`,
    `SEVERITY`, `LEVEL` or `TIER`. What `font_confirmation_gate` performs is a
    **binary partition, 1 against 5** — `VERIFIED_FOR_PRODUCTION` → `[]`, and each
    of the other five → exactly one code. There is no relation under which one
    non-verified state sits above another.

**"Any state above the ceiling" therefore admits two readings that differ by
exactly one state.** Under the gate's own operative partition, the only state
above `LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED` is `VERIFIED_FOR_PRODUCTION`, the sole state that
yields no code. Under the **source declaration order** at lines 27–32 — repeated
in the identical order inside `__all__`, so it is a deliberate order and not an
accident — the states above the ceiling are `VERIFIED_FOR_PRODUCTION` **and**
`APPROVED_FOR_CONCEPT_ONLY`. That declaration order is textual and carries no
runtime meaning, and it is **not monotone** under an "authority granted" reading:
`FONT_FILE_MISSING`, `FONT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` and `UNVERIFIED` are three distinct
failure modes, not three decreasing grants.

**RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED, AND REPORTED BEFORE ACTING.** Choosing between the two
readings decides whether the producer may emit `APPROVED_FOR_CONCEPT_ONLY`, which
is a licence-shaped state. Choosing it silently would be exactly the substitution
§BH12(e) refused to make. A second question rides with it: since no enum exists,
**something must create the enumeration the cap is enforced against**, and whether
that creation belongs inside commit (2) or is a separate concern under §AC is not
settled by §BH13. Both questions go to the owner rather than being answered here.
**Neither blocks this transcription**, which §BH13's own preamble orders *"before
acting."*

§BH13(a) requires the cap *"enforced in code, not convention"* and §BH13(b)

### §BH14(a) — CEILING DEFINED BY SUBSTANCE, NOT LIST POSITION

> ceiling defined by SUBSTANCE, not list position: the producer may emit only
> states that grant nothing — the identity findings and LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED.
> APPROVED_FOR_CONCEPT_ONLY is above the ceiling and forbidden: it is
> approval-shaped, and a machine writing the word APPROVED confers authority this
> cap exists to prevent. This definition governs over any declaration order or
> partition an existing list implies. The enum encodes it explicitly: every state
> carries its side of the ceiling, and the cap test enumerates the forbidden side
> and proves each state unreachable.

### §BH14(b) — THE ENUM IS ITS OWN CODE-ONLY COMMIT, LANDING FIRST

> the enum is its own code-only commit, landing FIRST. Order is now: enum →
> producer → guard. The enum names the app's font states with the ceiling
> partition from (a) built in; the producer's cap then enforces against
> infrastructure that already exists and was separately gated. The seam finding —
> every string survives verbatim into verification, nothing refused — stays
> recorded; the guard commit is where that closes, per §BH12(b)/§BH13(b).

### §BH14(c) — STANDING DISCIPLINE UNCHANGED

> standing discipline unchanged: §AD0(a) before every gate, findings recorded not
> resolved in transcription commits, supersessions by quoting. If I meant
> something narrower, my sentence governs.

### §BH14(d) — OWNER CONFIRMATION, TYPED SECOND, ANSWERING THE QUESTION RAISED AT §BH14(g)

> Confirmed, my typed words: UNVERIFIED sits AT OR BELOW the ceiling — it grants
> nothing and is the module's most-conservative default. The gate's :220 grouping
> answers a different question and stays untouched. §BH14(a) partition stands:
> 2 forbidden / 4 permitted.

### §BH14(e) — BOTH QUESTIONS §BH13(f) LEFT OPEN ARE ANSWERED, AND THE FIRST IS ANSWERED ON A GROUND NEITHER READING OFFERED

§BH13(f) recorded two readings of *"any state above the ceiling"* differing by
exactly one state, and refused to choose between them because the choice decides
whether a licence-shaped state may be machine-written.

**§BH14(a) selects the same MEMBERSHIP as the declaration-order reading and
explicitly rejects its GROUND.** The states above the ceiling are
`VERIFIED_FOR_PRODUCTION` and `APPROVED_FOR_CONCEPT_ONLY` — which is what reading
two produced — but not because they sit first in a list. §BH14(a) says so
directly: *"This definition governs over any declaration order or partition an
existing list implies."* The ground is substance: a state is above the ceiling if
it **grants**.

**The distinction is load-bearing, not stylistic.** Under the declaration-order
reading the partition moves if the six constants at lines 27–32 are ever
reordered — a cosmetic edit would silently re-licence a state. Under the substance
reading it does not move, because reordering constants does not change what a word
confers. Recording the ground rather than only the answer is what makes the enum's
cap test writable at all, since the test must assert a reason, not a position.

**The second question is answered by §BH14(b):** the enum is its own code-only
commit and lands first. **§BH12(c)'s three-commit order therefore becomes four** —
(1) the regular-face naming fix, landed at `b988bd4`; (2) the enum; (3) the
producer; (4) the guard. The letters in §BH12(c) are the owner's and are not
renumbered here; the sequence is restated rather than rewritten.

### §BH14(f) — THE SUBSTANCE PARTITION CUTS ACROSS THE PARTITION THE CODE ALREADY HAS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

The partition §BH14(a) fixes, and §BH14(d) confirms as **2 forbidden / 4
permitted**, over the six states in `apps/ire/container_font_authority`:

  * **ABOVE THE CEILING, forbidden to the producer (2):**
    `VERIFIED_FOR_PRODUCTION`, `APPROVED_FOR_CONCEPT_ONLY`.
  * **AT OR BELOW, granting nothing (4):** `LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`,
    `FONT_FILE_MISSING`, `FONT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH`, `UNVERIFIED`.

§BH13(f) measured the gate's own partition as **binary, 1 against 5** — only
`VERIFIED_FOR_PRODUCTION` yields no code. §BH14(a)'s is **2 against 4**. The two
disagree on exactly one state, and the disagreement is legible in the source:
`font_confirmation_gate`'s final branch reads `else:  # UNVERIFIED / concept-only`
and emits **one** code for **both** `UNVERIFIED` and `APPROVED_FOR_CONCEPT_ONLY`.
§BH14(a) places those two on **opposite sides of the ceiling**, and §BH14(d)
disposes of the tension directly: *"The gate's :220 grouping answers a different
question and stays untouched."*

**The enum therefore cannot be derived from the gate's structure**, and a helper
written inside the producer's commit would have been read off exactly the
structure that disagrees. That is the practical force of §BH14(b) making the enum
its own commit: it is new information about the states, not a refactor of an
existing grouping. Nothing in the gate is changed — the gate emits
*production-readiness codes*, which is a different question from *what a machine
may write*, and both are correct at once.

### §BH14(g) — THE QUESTION AS IT WAS RAISED: IS `UNVERIFIED` ONE OF "THE IDENTITY FINDINGS"? LEFT STANDING, AND ANSWERED AT §BH14(d)

**This section is preserved as it was written, before the answer existed.**
§BH14(a) names the permitted states as *"the identity findings and
LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED."* `FONT_FILE_MISSING` and `FONT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` are
identity findings on their face. **`UNVERIFIED` is not obviously one**, and the
enum must place all six states on a side, so the gap could not be left open in
code.

**The governing clause is the test, not the gloss.** The sentence's operative
words are *"the producer may emit only states that grant nothing"*, and the
em-dash clause names them. `UNVERIFIED` grants nothing; it is the module's most
conservative state. **Measured:** `_face_record` sets `"verification": UNVERIFIED`
as the **base default for every face**, before any confirmation is consulted.
Placing it above the ceiling would make the module's own most conservative default
a forbidden, grant-conferring state, and would put the unconfirmed container — the
only state this container has ever been in — in permanent violation of the cap.

**That reading was reported to the owner rather than acted on, and §BH14(d)
confirms it** — *"UNVERIFIED sits AT OR BELOW the ceiling — it grants nothing and
is the module's most-conservative default"* — on the same two grounds the
measurement supplied. The question is **left standing here rather than deleted**,
because a register that shows only confirmed readings cannot be audited for how
often the executor's reading was wrong. The enum commit will still **state on its
face which side it encodes `UNVERIFIED` on**, citing §BH14(d) rather than this
section.

### §BH14(h) — WHAT IS BUILT IN THIS COMMIT: NOTHING

Transcription only, per §BH14's own preamble, §BC and §AC. No enum, no producer,
no guard, no cap, no test. `container_font_authority` is not touched, and neither

§BH12(b)/§BH13(b). `_bounded_font_authority`'s six-of-eight `None` key projection

### §BH15(a) — THE AUTHORITY LEAK: CEILING EXTENDED, SEAM EDITED HONESTLY

> Your finding at _face_record:177 is accepted: a machine producer that complies

**Why this is lettered here and marked.** The house form quotes owner text under
lettered headings, and every other letter in this arc corresponds to a letter the
owner typed. This paragraph the owner did not letter. Assigning it (d) silently
would manufacture a provenance the owner did not create; leaving it out of the
lettering would bury an operative instruction in prose. It is therefore lettered
**and** the lettering is disclosed, so a later reader can tell the transcriber's
act from the owner's.

### §BH15(e) — THE GROUND OF §BH15(a) WAS MEASURED BY EXECUTION, NOT BY READING, AND THE MEASUREMENTS ARE TRANSCRIBED SO THE RULING'S BASIS SITS IN THE REGISTER

§BH15(a) accepts a finding. The finding was produced by running the code, on one
font file, with `sha256` proved equal on both sides so that nothing about the font
differs between the two lines:

    no confirmation   source='PLACEHOLDER_FALLBACK'  is_fallback=True
        gate=['CONTAINER_FONT_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED','CONTAINER_FONT_FALLBACK_DETECTED']
    MACHINE-produced  source='USER_CONFIRMED'        is_fallback=False
        gate=['CONTAINER_FONT_LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED']

Two gate codes are **deleted** by a confirmation whose `verification` is
`LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED` — squarely at or below the §BH14 ceiling. So the ceiling
held and authority was conferred anyway. That is the whole of the finding, and it
is why §BH15(a) rules on the principle rather than on the field.

**THE MECHANISM, NAMED.** `build_font_authority` collapses two different things
into one argument before `_face_record` ever sees them:

    use_path = (conf.get("path") if conf and conf.get("path") else path)

`_face_record` is then handed `path=use_path` and cannot tell a file the
confirmation supplied from the placeholder the resolver picked. Having no way to
answer the question honestly, it answers it by assumption — `"is_fallback": False`
under `if confirmed:`. **The dishonesty is a consequence of a discarded
distinction, not of a wrong constant**, which is the thing the seam fix has to
repair; changing the literal alone would relocate the defect rather than remove it.

**THE OTHER TWO GROUNDS, ALREADY IN THE REGISTER AND UNCHANGED BY THIS RULING.**
Of 3,966 evidence rows, **0** carry any human decision — `license_decision`,
`ownership_decision`, `quarantine_decision`, `reviewer` and `reviewed_at` are null
throughout and `machine_inference_immutable` is `true` for all 3,966. And all
3,966 `source_path`s sit under `materials/`, **0** under `static/fonts`, so both
container faces join to NO MATCH; exact `postscript_name` matches are **0** and
core `NotoSans` family rows are **0**, so the emptiness is a property of the
corpora and not of the key. §BH15(b) rules on that state of affairs without
disturbing the measurement.

### §BH15(f) — ONE CITATION IN §BH15(a) IS CURRENT AND THE OTHER HAS MOVED ADDRESS; THE MOVED ONE IS RE-ANCHORED BY QUOTING, AND §BH14(d) IS NOT EDITED

§BH15(a) requires two regions to remain byte-untouched by the seam commit and
names them by line number. Measured at `HEAD=fe5c2bd`, those two numbers are not
in the same condition, and the difference is chronological rather than careless:

  * **§BH13(c)'s revived test** `test_confirmed_production_face_can_verify` has
    likewise moved, `:77` → **`:83`**, by the 6 lines commit AF inserted above it
    (a 4-line docstring paragraph and a 2-line import).

Per the standing rule that supersessions are made **by quoting**, §BH14(d) is
**not** edited to say `:281`. Its sentence stands as typed and is re-anchored
here. A future reader who checks line 220 will find an unrelated line; the region
§BH14(d) protects is the `else:  # UNVERIFIED / concept-only` branch, whichever
line currently holds it.

**WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN TREATED AS PEDANTRY.** This arc has twice
been damaged by a citation that pointed at nothing — §W cited by five commits and
seven files before anyone noticed it had never been committed, and §AZ0(u) cited

expiry date, and commit AF was the event that expired this one.

### §BH15(g) — WHAT §BH15(a) LEAVES TO MEASUREMENT, AND ONE TEST THAT LOOKED LIKE A CONFLICT AND IS NOT — RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED

  * **THE EXACT STRING IS OWED A MEASUREMENT, NOT A PREFERENCE.** §BH15(a) gives
    `MACHINE_JOINED` as an example and rules the *"exact string is yours, by
    measurement against the house idiom"*. That measurement belongs to the seam
    commit and is **not** taken here. What is recorded now is only the population
    it must be measured against: `source` today takes exactly two values in code,
    `PLACEHOLDER_FALLBACK` and `USER_CONFIRMED`, both self-describing
    SCREAMING_SNAKE literals, neither prefixed.

  * **A PRE-EXISTING TEST ASSERTS THE TWO VALUES §BH15(a) ORDERS CHANGED, AND
    SURVIVES UNCHANGED — WHICH MAKES IT THE FIX'S NEGATIVE CONTROL.**
    `test_wif_reconstruct_container.py:633-634` asserts
    `all(f["source"] == "USER_CONFIRMED")` and `all(not f["is_fallback"])`. Read
    cold that looks like a direct conflict with §BH15(a). It is not, and the
    reason is visible three lines above the assertions: the confirmation it passes
    carries `"path": self._tmp_font()` — a real file of its own — and the test's
    own comment says it is checking that *"the confirmation genuinely displaced
    the placeholder, rather than riding alongside it"*. A human did confirm that
    face, and the placeholder genuinely was displaced, so **both values are
    truthful there** and §BH15(a) leaves them alone. The test therefore becomes
    the discriminator the seam fix is measured by: it must stay **GREEN**
    untouched while the machine-join path gets a different `source` and keeps
    `is_fallback` honest. A fix that reddens it has over-reached; a fix that
    cannot redden it under a hostile input has under-reached.

  * **"TRUTHFUL" IS DEFINED BY THE DISPLACEMENT, NOT BY THE CONFIRMATION.** Read
    with the bullet above, §BH15(a)'s *"is_fallback stays truthful regardless of
    confirmation state"* resolves to: the face is a fallback when the file in use
    is the resolver's placeholder, and is not when the confirmation supplied its
    own. This is the executor's reading of the owner's sentence and is recorded as
    such; per §BH15(d)'s caveat the owner's sentence governs if it meant narrower.

  * **§BH15(b) FORBIDS THE CONSOLATION ENTRY.** *"No per-face claim is made while
    the joined set is empty — not UNVERIFIED-dressed-as-progress, nothing."* The
    producer therefore emits **no entry at all** for a face that does not join,
    rather than an entry carrying `UNVERIFIED`. The existing seam already yields

    new machinery — which is the point.

  * **QUEUED BY §BH15(b) AND NOT STARTED:** extending the dip0c audit to
    `static/fonts`. Recorded here so the empty join is not later mistaken for an
    unnoticed defect.

### §BH16(a) — THE SEAM DEFAULT IS INVERTED; SILENCE GRANTS NOTHING

> The seam default is inverted. A confirmation carrying no provenance key may

> the same principle as UNVERIFIED: silence grants nothing. is_fallback stays
> truthful under an undeclared confirmation — it does not flip on silence.
> The two live assertions that pin the old contract (including
> test_an_undeclared_confirmation_still_reads_as_human) are inverted in the
> SAME commit — that is their §BH13(c)-style moment, not a bar lowered.
> §BH15(a)'s protected regions — font_confirmation_gate's grouping and
> test_confirmed_production_face_can_verify — stay byte-untouched; verify by
> diff and say so.

### §BH16(b) — COMMIT AH'S TWO SUBSTITUTIONS ARE ACCEPTED ON THE RECORD

> Commit AH's two substitutions are accepted on the record: MACHINE_DERIVED
> over my example MACHINE_JOINED was inside the delegation I gave, chosen by
> measurement; and your supersession of §BH15(e) — origin, not file — stands,

### §BH16(c) — COMMIT ORDER, AND THE STANDING CAVEAT

> Order from here: §BH16 transcription → inversion commit (a) → producer,
> capped and fixture-tested per §BH15(b) → guard commit per §BH13(b)/(c).
> Each with its §AD0(a) prediction declared before the gate.

The caveat is quoted inside (c) because the owner typed it as a standalone

transcriber-assigned anywhere in §BH16.

### §BH16(d) — THE SCOPE OF THE INVERSION IS AMBIGUOUS ON ITS FACE, AND IS SETTLED BY EXECUTION AND BY THE OWNER'S OWN COUNT RATHER THAN BY THE TRANSCRIBER'S PREFERENCE

§BH16(a)'s sentence *"is_fallback stays truthful under an undeclared confirmation
— it does not flip on silence"* carries two readings that are both grammatically
available and that give opposite code:

  * **READING A — is_fallback FOLLOWS.** "It does not flip on silence" = silence
    does not flip it *to False*, i.e. silence may not clear the flag. `is_fallback`
    stays the derived function of `source` that commit AH made it, so an undeclared
    confirmation now yields `is_fallback=True` and restores
    `CONTAINER_FONT_FALLBACK_DETECTED`.
  * **READING B — ONLY `source` MOVES.** "It does not flip on silence" = the flag
    is not swept into the inversion at all; the ruling's verb *"inverted"* is used
    of the `source` default and of the assertions, and this clause withholds
    `is_fallback` from it. An undeclared confirmation keeps `is_fallback=False`.

Both were BUILT and RUN, per §AA's standing rule that a claim of effect is measured
rather than reasoned from the diff. Three confirmations were taken **verbatim from
the live tests** and put through `build_font_authority` + `font_confirmation_gate`
under HEAD's module and under each reading, in one process:

    PROTECTED  test_confirmed_production_face_can_verify   (provenance key: ABSENT)
      HEAD    source=USER_CONFIRMED  is_fallback=False  gate=[]
      READ-A  source=UNDECLARED      is_fallback=True   gate=[]
      READ-B  source=UNDECLARED      is_fallback=False  gate=[]
    WIF        test_a_licence_pending_confirmation_…      (provenance key: ABSENT)
      HEAD    source=USER_CONFIRMED  is_fallback=False  gate=[LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED]
      READ-A  source=UNDECLARED      is_fallback=True   gate=[LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED,
                                                             FALLBACK_DETECTED]
      READ-B  source=UNDECLARED      is_fallback=False  gate=[LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED]
    AH         test_an_undeclared_confirmation_…          (provenance key: ABSENT)
      HEAD    source=USER_CONFIRMED  is_fallback=False  gate=[LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED]
      READ-A  source=UNDECLARED      is_fallback=True   gate=[LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED,
                                                             FALLBACK_DETECTED]
      READ-B  source=UNDECLARED      is_fallback=False  gate=[LICENSE_REVIEW_REQUIRED]

Scored against the eight live assertion lines those three tests actually contain:

    READING A reddens SIX:   cfa:97, wif:633, wif:634, wif:635, cfa:292, cfa:293
                             (green: cfa:98 and wif:636 only)
    READING B reddens TWO:   wif:633 and cfa:292 — and nothing else.

**TWO INDEPENDENT DISCRIMINATORS SELECT READING B, AND NEITHER IS A PREFERENCE.**

  1. **THE OWNER'S OWN COUNT.** §BH16(a) says *"The **two** live assertions that
     pin the old contract"*. Measured across tracked `.py`: the font-authority
     `source` field is asserted equal to `USER_CONFIRMED` in exactly **two** live
     places — `test_container_font_authority.py:292` and
     `test_wif_reconstruct_container.py:633` — and those are precisely the two
     Reading B reddens. Reading A reddens those two **and four more**, so under
     Reading A the owner's count would be wrong by four. (The nearby
     `test_container_font_authority.py:248`, `assert f["source"] != SOURCE_USER_
     CONFIRMED`, is a NEGATIVE assertion and pins nothing; `:222` and `:233` assert
     the ceiling partition, not the seam default. All three stay green either way.)
  2. **THE BYTE-UNTOUCHED ORDER, WHICH READING A CANNOT SATISFY.** §BH16(a) orders
     `test_confirmed_production_face_can_verify` byte-untouched. That test's own
     confirmation — `container_font_authority`'s test file, `:91-93` — carries **no
     `provenance` key**, so §BH16(a) reaches it. Under Reading A its `:97`
     (`assert all(not f["is_fallback"])`) goes **RED**, and a test cannot be both
     byte-untouched and red. Under Reading B it stays **GREEN**. So Reading A makes
     §BH16(a) self-defeating and Reading B makes it self-consistent.

Recorded rather than resolved by taste: the ambiguity was real, and what removed it
was the owner's own number and the owner's own protection order, both measured
against the tree. Per §BH16(c)'s caveat the owner's sentence governs, and on this
measurement the sentence is determinate.

**ONE SURPRISE INSIDE READING A, WORTH THE RECORD BECAUSE IT IS A FACT ABOUT THE
GATE AND NOT ABOUT THE READING.** Under Reading A the protected test's `:97` goes
red but its `:98` (`assert font_confirmation_gate(auth) == []`) stays **GREEN** —
`is_fallback` became True and no `CONTAINER_FONT_FALLBACK_DETECTED` appeared.
`font_confirmation_gate` does `continue` on `VERIFIED_FOR_PRODUCTION` **before**
reaching `if r.get("is_fallback")`, so a face verified for production can never
report the fallback code whatever the flag says. Recorded, not fixed (§X3(c)); it
is reachable only through a state §BH14's ceiling already forbids a machine to write.

### §BH16(e) — WHAT §BH16 SUPERSEDES IN §BH15(g), STATED BY QUOTING AND NOT BY EDITING

Two of §BH15(g)'s bullets are overtaken. Per the standing rule that supersessions
are made **by quoting**, §BH15(g) is **not** edited; both sentences stand as typed
and are re-anchored here.

  * §BH15(g) wrote of `test_wif_reconstruct_container.py:633-634` that *"it must
    stay **GREEN** untouched while the machine-join path gets a different source"*,
    and made it *"the discriminator the seam fix is measured by"*. §BH16(a) now
    ORDERS the `:633` half inverted, because that test's confirmation carries no
    `provenance` key and is therefore exactly the silence §BH16(a) reaches. Its
    `:634`, `:635` and `:636` stay green — measured above, not assumed. So the
    sentence was correct for the commit it governed (AH) and is superseded only for
    the half §BH16(a) names.
  * §BH15(g)'s *"'TRUTHFUL' IS DEFINED BY THE DISPLACEMENT, NOT BY THE
    CONFIRMATION"* was already superseded by commit AH on the ORIGIN axis, and
    §BH16(b) now ratifies that supersession on the record. §BH15(e)'s naming of the
    `use_path` collapse likewise stands as **recorded and deliberately left in
    place**, per §BH16(b)'s own words.

### §BH16(f) — WHAT §BH16(a) LEAVES TO MEASUREMENT, AND THE ONE THING THE RULING FORCES RATHER THAN DELEGATES

  * **THE STRING IS OWED A MEASUREMENT AND IS NOT CHOSEN HERE.** §BH16(a) gives
    `UNDECLARED` as an example, says it *"is only an example"*, and delegates the
    choice *"by measurement against the house idiom, as in §BH15(a)"*. That
    measurement belongs to the inversion commit, exactly as §BH15(g) held the
    `MACHINE_DERIVED` measurement back to the seam commit. Recorded now is only the
    population it must be measured against: `source` today takes exactly four
    values in code — `PLACEHOLDER_FALLBACK`, `USER_CONFIRMED`, `MACHINE_DERIVED`
    and `UNATTRIBUTED` — all SCREAMING_SNAKE, and all four bound to constants
    carrying the load-bearing `SOURCE_` prefix that commit AH's drift guard requires.
  * **THE RULING FORCES A VALUE DISTINCT FROM `UNATTRIBUTED`, AND THAT IS MEASURED,
    NOT ARGUED.** The obvious economy — let silence reuse commit AH's existing
    `SOURCE_UNATTRIBUTED` rather than mint a fifth value — was BUILT AND RUN as a
    third variant. `UNATTRIBUTED` sits AT OR BELOW the ceiling, so the protected
    test's face came back `source=UNATTRIBUTED is_fallback=True` and `:97` went
    **RED**. So silence and unrecognised-declaration cannot be the same value while
    §BH16(a)'s byte-untouched order holds. The STRING is delegated; the
    DISTINCTNESS is not.
  * **THE DISTINCTION IS ALSO SUBSTANTIVE, NOT MERELY LEXICAL.** After the
    inversion the two neighbouring states disagree on the flag: a confirmation
    DECLARING an origin this module does not know is a fallback, while one
    declaring NOTHING is not. That asymmetry is a consequence of §BH16(a) as read
    above and is carried up to the owner at §BH16(g) rather than smoothed away.

### §BH16(g) — TWO RESIDUALS, REPORTED AND NOT RESOLVED

  1. **SILENCE STILL SUPPRESSES THE FALLBACK FINDING FOR A NON-VERIFIED FACE.**
     Under §BH16(a) as measured, a producer that omits `provenance` no longer
     acquires a human-confirmation claim in `source`, but still clears
     `is_fallback` and so still deletes `CONTAINER_FONT_FALLBACK_DETECTED` — the
     WIF row above shows HEAD and READ-B emitting the same single gate code where
     READ-A emits two. §BH15(a)'s principle has two halves, *"may never write a
     human-confirmation claim, and may never suppress a truthful finding"*;
     §BH16(a) closes the first half against silence and, on this reading, leaves
     the second half open to it. This is reported as a measured consequence of the
     sentence, not urged as a correction: §BH16(a) says in terms that `is_fallback`
     *"does not flip on silence"*, and the transcriber does not read past that.
  2. **SILENCE IS NOW TREATED MORE LENIENTLY THAN AN UNRECOGNISED DECLARATION**, per
     §BH16(f)'s third bullet. A producer that declares `SOME_FUTURE_PRODUCER` is a
     fallback; one that declares nothing is not. Both residuals are the same fact
     seen from two sides and are put up together.

### §BH16(h) — WHAT IS BUILT IN THIS COMMIT: NOTHING

Transcription only, per §BH16's own preamble, §BC and §AC. No seam edit, no

### §BH17(d) — §BH15(b)'s PROHIBITION IS SUPERSEDED BY QUOTING, AND ONLY AS TO MEASUREMENT

§BH15(b) is not edited. Per the standing supersession rule it is re-anchored here by
quoting the sentence §BH17(b) overtakes:

> *"Extending the dip0c audit to static/fonts is queued as its own owner-gated item;
> do not start it."*

That sentence named a GATE and the gate is the owner's. §BH17(b) opens it — **and opens
it to exactly one width.** The words *"It opens PROPOSAL-ONLY"*, *"then STOP for my
ruling before any build"* and *"No audit code lands and no artifact rows are produced
under this ruling"* are three independent statements of the same limit, and the third
is the operative one because it is the only one phrased as a prohibition on OUTPUT
rather than on sequence. **So §BH15(b)'s prohibition survives in full against building;
what is superseded is its application to MEASURING.** §BH16(h) recorded the item as
*"the owner-gated extension of the dip0c audit to `static/fonts`, which §BH15(b) forbids
starting"* — that sentence is now true only of the build half, and is superseded here
by quoting rather than by editing §BH16(h).

The reading is the narrow one deliberately, per the standing caveat. A wider reading was
available — that "opens" licenses a scaffold so long as it is not run — and it is not
taken: *"No audit code lands"* is unconditional and does not distinguish executed code
from dormant code.

### §BH17(e) — THE "SMALLS" IN §BH17(c) ENUMERATE THREE WHERE §BH16(h) ENUMERATED FOUR. RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED

§BH16(h) left the queue as four items: *"the `begin_traced_queue` namespace guard, the
`establishment_table` counts correction, the `finding_4` appends still blocked on the
A391 chain, and the owner-gated extension of the dip0c audit to `static/fonts`."*
§BH17(c)'s parenthetical names three, and they are not the same three: it ADDS the
*"vacuous-test item"* and does not name the `finding_4` appends. The fourth §BH16(h)
item is not missing — §BH17(b) promotes it.

Both halves of the divergence are traceable and neither is treated as an error:

  * The **vacuous-test item** is not new vocabulary. It is the owner's own, from
    §BH12(d): *"The vacuous test and A391 batch stay queued unless the naming fix's
    evidence naturally discharges the former."* §BH17(c) restates a live §BH12(d) item
    rather than opening one.
  * The **`finding_4` appends** are absent from the parenthetical and are NOT thereby
    dropped, because the parenthetical is a gloss on a governing clause that already
    covers them: *"Everything else stays where the queue put it."* An enumeration
    introduced by "the smalls" is illustrative; the rule is the sentence it illustrates.

**This is recorded rather than reconciled.** The transcriber does not renumber the
queue to make two lists agree, and does not treat an unnamed item as closed. Under the
standing caveat the owner's sentence governs, and his sentence is *"everything else
stays where the queue put it."*

### §BH17(f) — A MEASURED HAZARD BEARING DIRECTLY ON §BH17(a)'s "THROUGH THE GATE"

The 2026-08-28 queue block records, as ESTABLISHED rather than plausible, that
*"`guarded_commit.sh` stages the ledger line and never commits it when the caller passes

is untouched** — a tool repair does not ride into a docs commit, per §AC.

only skipped letter in the arc and remains unfilled** — §BH18(a) glosses what it would
have carried, which is not the same act as filling it. See §BH18(f).

### §BH18(a) — THE §BH11 CITATION IN §BH17(b) IS SUPERSEDED BY QUOTING

### §BH18(f) — §BH17(b) IS NOT EDITED, AND A GLOSS ON §BH11 IS NOT A FILLING OF §BH11

§BH17(b) keeps its text. The sentence §BH18(a) overtakes is re-anchored here by quoting
it, per the standing supersession rule, and the citation stays visible in the ruling
that carried it:

> *"It opens PROPOSAL-ONLY, per the §BH11 pattern"*

**THE CORRECTION IS THE OWNER'S, NOT THE TRANSCRIBER'S, AND THAT MATTERS.** The executor
reported the dangling citation and refused to resolve it — it did not substitute §BH10's
or §BH12's pattern, and it did not act on a guess. §BH18(a) supplies the meaning from the
only source entitled to supply it. This is §BH13(a)'s class in terms, and §BH18(a) says
so itself.

**AND THE GAP STAYS A GAP.** §BH18(a) says what §BH11 *"was AUTHORIZED to carry"*. It
does not write a §BH11, does not renumber, and does not convert the skipped letter into
an occupied one. A later reader searching for §BH11 still finds a deliberate absence —
now with a note about what it would have held. The register records both facts and
collapses neither into the other.

**THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS NIL, AND THAT IS ALSO WORTH RECORDING.** §BH18(a) states
that the pattern *"governed regardless"*, because §BH17(b) spelled it out in its own
words — *"then STOP for my ruling before any build"*. The proposal was executed under
those words, not under the citation. So no work is redone and nothing is reversed: the
citation was a dangling reference, not a wrong instruction, and the difference is why
the executor reported it instead of stopping on it.

### §BH18(g) — §BH18(c) DECIDES WHAT THE PROPOSAL DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN, AND BOTH CONDITIONS TRACE TO MEASURED FINDINGS

The §BH17(b) proposal closed with three options and the line *"I am not picking one."*
§BH18(c) picks B. The two conditions are not additions to the executor's analysis —
**each is one of the executor's own findings promoted from an observation to a
requirement**, which is a stronger act than agreement:

  * **Condition (1)** is Q3(4) verbatim in substance: `snapshot()` defaults to
    `SOURCE_ROOT` and `run_c4c` asserts on `integrity.materials.unchanged`, so a widened
    corpus with an unwidened snapshot would report `materials_unchanged: true` while
    saying nothing at all about the new root. The proposal called that *"a silent false
    assurance produced by the very machinery that exists to prevent one."* §BH18(c)(1)
    makes it a condition of landing.
  * **Condition (2)** is Q3(3): `assert_output_safe()` protects only `SOURCE_ROOT`, so
    under an ADDITIVE root — which is precisely what Option B is — the four files in
    `bbrose_design_os/static/fonts/` would carry no write protection from the existing
    guard at all. Option B is the option that creates this hole; §BH18(c)(2) requires it
    closed in the same change that opens it.

**THE COSTLIER OPTION WAS NOT CHOSEN AND THE CHEAPEST WAS NOT EITHER.** Option A
(widen `SOURCE_ROOT`) was priced at 31 files / 53 hits and a change in what the constant
MEANS; §BH18(c) refuses it in terms — *"SOURCE_ROOT keeps its meaning."* Option C (do
nothing) was priced honestly against its own yield: after the audit the two container
faces move from `UNVERIFIED` to `LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `is_fallback` stays `True`,
`CONTAINER_FONT_FALLBACK_DETECTED` still fires, and nothing becomes licensed. The owner
saw that yield stated as one renamed gate code and ordered the build anyway. **That is
the owner's call to make and it is recorded as his, not rationalised here.**

### §BH18(h) — "IN THE SAME CHANGE", TWICE, DEFINES THE §AC CONCERN RATHER THAN BREAKING IT

§BH18(c) requires three things in one commit: the additive second root, the widened
integrity snapshot root, and write protection over `static/fonts`. On a careless reading
that is three concerns in one commit and §AC forbids it.

**It is not, and the ruling itself is why.** §BH18(c)(2) says *"no widening lands while
they sit unguarded"* — the guards are not adjacent work that happens to ship alongside
the widening; they are the condition on which the widening is permitted to exist at all.
Splitting them would produce an intermediate commit in which the corpus reaches live
application assets that are unprotected and whose integrity is unreported. **That commit
is the one §BH18(c) exists to forbid.** So the §AC concern here is *the widening with its
guards*, singular, and honouring §AC means keeping them together rather than separating
them.

The reading is recorded because the alternative is available and wrong, and a narrowing
that is not written down is indistinguishable later from a possibility never noticed.

**WHAT STAYS OUT OF THAT COMMIT IS NAMED IN THE SAME SENTENCE.** §BH18(c) closes by
holding two defects OUT: the `run_c4c` fail-closed-at-`:86` behaviour and the
`relpath()` docstring that says *"always `materials/…`"* while the code returns a
REPO_ROOT-relative path. Both were reported as measurements in the proposal; both are
*"recorded, not repaired, per §AC — separate concerns, separate commits if ever."* This
is §X3(c)'s form: a finding is not a work item until it is ruled one, and *"if ever"*
is not a promise that it will be.

### §BH18(i) — §BH18(c)(2) NAMES AN OUTCOME, NOT A MECHANISM, AND THE EXECUTOR SAYS WHICH IT WILL USE BEFORE IT BUILDS

*"Write protection extends over static/fonts"* states what must be true, not how. The
natural mechanism is the existing one — `assert_output_safe()` currently refuses any
write at or under `SOURCE_ROOT`, and extending its refusal set to cover the new root is
a change to that one guard rather than a second guard beside it. **That is what will be
built**, and it is declared here, before the build, so that the choice is visible as a
choice rather than discovered in a diff.

If the existing guard turns out not to be able to carry it — if the refusal set cannot
be widened without changing what `assert_output_safe` means to its 31 existing callers,
which is the same hazard that disqualified Option A — **that is reported before a second
guard is invented**, per the standing rule that an unruled decision is reported rather
than taken.

### §BH18(j) — §BH18(b) ORDERS A SECOND ALREADY-SUPERSEDED RECORD TO LAND AS WRITTEN, WHICH IS NOW A PATTERN AND NOT AN ACCIDENT

The Q1–Q4 proposal asks the owner to choose between three options. §BH18(c) has already
chosen. §BH18(b) nevertheless orders it landed *"As written — including its own record
that it preceded this ruling."*

**This is the second instance in two commits.** At `83c238f` the OWNER_REVIEW_QUEUE.md
block landed asking for a ruling on what follows the guard, one commit after §BH17(b)
had answered exactly that. It was committed unedited for the same reason §BH18(b) now
states as an order: back-editing a dated record so it never appears to have been open
destroys the only evidence that the question was asked before it was answered. What the
executor did once on its own judgement, and flagged for correction, the owner has now
ruled is the required form. **It is a rule now, not a defensible choice**, and the
`preceded this ruling` clause is the owner's, not the transcriber's.

### §BH18(k) — §BH18(d)'s A391 CLAUSE IS AN INSTRUCTION TO THE PREDICTION, NOT ONLY TO THE BUILD

*"any new test file enters the manifest chain knowingly, A391 priced before the gate,
not after"* binds the §AD0(a) prediction for the §BH18(c) commit specifically. The
manifest chain is `tier2_gate.check_manifest()`, which enforces file-set EQUALITY against
`suite_file_manifest.json`; every prediction in this arc so far has been able to write
*"no new file, so the A391 identity chain is not entered."* **The §BH18(c) commit is the
first in the arc for which that sentence may be false**, and §BH18(d) requires the count
and the declaration to be stated in the prediction file BEFORE staging, where they can be
scored, rather than reconciled afterwards against whatever the gate happened to say.

### §BH18(l) — WHAT IS BUILT IN THIS COMMIT: NOTHING

Transcription only, per §BH18's own instruction, §BC and §AC. No audit, no scaffold, no
corpus root, no guard, no proposal text, no queue append, and nothing under `apps/` or

that follow it are not begun here and no part of them is prepared here. C3 is untouched
and stays BLOCKING by construction, which §BH18(d) leaves exactly where §BH17(c) left it.

## §BH19 — THE GATE TAKES A THIRD LEG OVER tools/dip0/tests, THE WIDENED AUDIT IS RUN LIVE IN THE DEFAULT ENVIRONMENT, AND THE JOIN IS RE-MEASURED TO ITS TERMINAL MACHINE STATE

**PROVENANCE.** Typed by the owner in this session, in full, headed *"OWNER RULING
§BH19 — typed by me, this session"*, with the same instruction as §BH17 and §BH18 —
*"Transcribe per §BC (pure append), its own commit per §AC, before acting"* — as five
lettered rulings, §BH19(a) through §BH19(e), followed by the standing caveat *"If I
meant something narrower, my sentence governs."* on its own unlettered line.

**IT RULES ON A REPORTED FINDING, WHICH IS A THIRD CLASS AGAIN.** §BH17 was recorded
here as NOT option-picked. §BH18 was recorded as option-picked. §BH19 is neither, and
the distinction is worth keeping: it **adopts an executor finding as an order**. At
`8fd9541` the executor reported that `tools/dip0/tests` is collected by NEITHER gate
leg, declined to repair it inside a corpus-widening commit under §AC, priced a third
leg, and stopped for a ruling. §BH19(a) orders the leg and — in the same sentence —
keeps the finding standing: *"your finding that 8fd9541 shipped ungated stands on the
record as the reason."* See §BH19(f).

**LETTER COLLISION — SEARCHED, NOT ASSUMED, AND EMPTY, WITH A NEGATIVE CONTROL.**
Measured at `HEAD=8fd9541` across **3,836** tracked `.md`/`.py`/`.json`/`.sh`/`.txt`
files.

  * `^#.*§BH19` as a heading in this register — **0 hits**.
  * `§BH19` anywhere in this register — **0 hits**.
  * `§BH19` across those tracked types at `HEAD` — **0 files**.
  * `§BH19` across those same types on the WORKING TREE — **0 files**.
  * **NEGATIVE CONTROL:** the identical four queries for `§BH18` return **13 headings**,
    **49 in-register hits**, **6 files** and **6 files**, so the queries have power and
    the zeros above are measurements rather than a broken pipe.
  * **THE TREE AND `HEAD` WERE ASKED SEPARATELY**, per the correction §BH17 recorded
    against itself, and they AGREE — 0 and 0 for §BH19, 6 and 6 for the control. The
    tree was clean when this was measured, which is why they agree; the two questions
    were still asked separately rather than one being taken for the other.

**THE POPULATION MOVED BY EXACTLY ONE, AND THE ONE IS NAMED.** 3,835 → 3,836, the first
movement in this arc. `git diff --diff-filter=A --name-only 83c238f HEAD` returns exactly
`tools/dip0/tests/test_corpus_roots.py` — the file §BH18(c) added, and nothing else. The
same query over `4140bd8..9070991` returns `container_font_evidence_join.py`, so the
query has power and the single name above is a measurement.

**THE NUMBERING IS CONSECUTIVE.** §BH18 → §BH19, no gap. **§BH11 remains the only
skipped letter in the arc and remains unfilled.**

### §BH19(a) — THE GATE WIDENS WITH A THIRD LEG OVER tools/dip0/tests, WITH A FLOOR GUARD PROVEN TO FIRE

> The gate widens with a THIRD LEG, its own commit: a separate process from the git root
> targeting tools/dip0/tests — its own process because of the documented

> LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED is reached, that is the arc's terminal machine state: the next

> the 31/53-vs-32/71 population note. Separate concerns, separate commits if ever, per
> §AC.

### §BH19(e) — THE ORDER, AND THE STANDING CAVEAT

> Order: transcription → gate third leg (a) → live run (b) → live join measurement (c) →
> report and queue append. Predictions declared before each gate.
>
> If I meant something narrower, my sentence governs.

### §BH19(f) — THE FIX DOES NOT ERASE THE DEFECT IT FIXES

§BH19(a) could have ordered the third leg and said nothing more. It does not. It ends by
fixing the finding in place — *"your finding that 8fd9541 shipped ungated stands on the
record as the reason"* — so that a later reader who sees a three-leg gate does not
conclude it was always three, and does not have to reconstruct why it grew.

**THIS MATTERS BECAUSE THE FIX IS THE KIND THAT USUALLY SWALLOWS ITS OWN HISTORY.** Once
`tools/dip0/tests` is gated, `8fd9541` sits in the log looking exactly like every other
green commit. The one thing that distinguishes it — that its 135 tests were run by hand
and not by the gate, and that its `TIER_2=GREEN` was not evidence about it — survives
only because it is written down. §BH19(a) writes it down as an owner sentence rather
than leaving it in an executor report, which is a stronger place for it to live.

### §BH19(g) — BOTH FACTUAL ASSERTIONS IN THE OWNER'S TEXT WERE VERIFIED AT TRANSCRIPTION TIME, AND BOTH HOLD

The §BH11 episode established that a citation inside owner text is checked at
transcription time and reported, never quietly assumed. §BH19 makes two checkable
assertions and **both were checked and both are sound**:

  * **`§BH5(c)`** — exists in this register at line 13268, headed *"GATE EXTENT WIDENING
    APPROVED"*, and is cited three times in `bbrose_design_os/tools/tier2_gate.py`
    (`:52`, `:321`, `:352`). The owner's citation and the gate's own source comment agree.
    **Not a dangling citation**; nothing to supersede.
  * **the "132-file frozen tree"** — `docs/design_intelligence/dip0c`, measured **132
    tracked and 132 on disk**, exact.

**THE EXECUTOR'S FIRST PROBE OF THE SECOND ONE WAS WRONG, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT.**
It measured `docs/design_intelligence/dip0a` — the DIP-0**A** tree — found **5** files,
and was one step from recording a divergence against the owner's number. The frozen tree
`run_c4c` protects is `dip0**c**`, resolved from `tools/dip0c/config.py:34` rather than
guessed from the arc's more familiar milestone name. A near-miss of this shape is
recorded because the arc's rule is that a divergence is REPORTED and never resolved —
and a *false* divergence reported with confidence would have been the same failure
wearing the opposite face.

### §BH19(h) — §BH19(b) AND §BH19(d) BOTH SPEAK TO run_c4c:86 AND DO NOT CONFLICT

Read carelessly these look opposed: (d) keeps *"run_c4c's :86 posture"* on the
recorded-not-repaired list, while (b) calls the same stop *"the EXPECTED stop"* and
orders it recorded *"not as a defect"*. They govern different objects.

  * **§BH19(d) governs the CODE.** The posture is not repaired in this arc; if it is ever
    changed that is its own concern and its own commit, per §AC.
  * **§BH19(b) governs the REPORT of the live run.** When the run stops there, it is
    logged as the guard working, not as a newly-discovered fault.

**THE MECHANISM, PINNED AT TRANSCRIPTION TIME SO THE LIVE RUN IS NOT READ BY GUESS.**
`run_c4c.py:79-83` writes the five `var/`-tier artifacts (`face_manifest.json`,
`technical_view.json`, `rights_view.json`, `queues.json`, `styles.json`). `:86` is the
FIRST write aimed at `C.MILESTONE_OUTPUT_ROOT`, which
`tools/dip0c/config.py:40` defines as `os.environ.get("DIP0C_MILESTONE_OUTPUT") or
DOCS_ROOT`. So the var/ writes complete and THEN the committed-tree write is refused —
which is precisely why §BH19(b) can order both that *"the var/-tier artifacts land"* and
that the stop occurs, in one sentence, without contradiction. **The environment override
§BH19(b) forbids setting is therefore `DIP0C_MILESTONE_OUTPUT`, named here so that
"set no environment override" cannot later be honoured in letter and broken in spirit.**

### §BH19(i) — "PROVEN TO FIRE, NOT ASSERTED" IS A BAR THIS ARC HAS ALREADY FAILED ONCE

§BH19(a) does not merely require a floor guard; it requires the report to show the guard
**firing**. That clause is not decorative, and the arc has the scar to prove it: a
`pytest.raises(...)` "red-before" earlier in this programme raised `AttributeError`
because the name did not yet exist, and therefore demonstrated **nothing whatever about
behaviour** while looking exactly like proof.

The same trap is available here in an obvious form. Asserting `DIP0_FLOOR == <n>`, or
that the constant exists, or that the leg collects `<n>` today, satisfies none of
§BH19(a): each of those passes just as happily if the guard is incapable of refusing
anything. **Firing means the collected count is actually driven below the floor and the
gate is observed to REFUSE** — the failure path exercised, not the happy path
re-described. The floor's whole purpose, in `DIP0C_FLOOR`'s own words at
`tier2_gate.py`, is to catch *"an invocation that collects NOTHING and reports zero
failures"* — a clean exit with a wrong count. A guard against that class cannot be
validated by a green run.

### §BH19(j) — THE FLOOR VALUE IS DELEGATED TO THE EXECUTOR, AND THE DELEGATION IS BOUNDED

*"the floor value is yours, by measurement at build time"* hands the executor a number,
not a judgement. Its bounds are set by the discipline it is named after: `DIP0C_FLOOR`
was fixed at its **measured** extent, 671, and the owner's §BH5(c)-era refusal of a
partial widening — *"a widening that leaves 310 passing tests ungated while reporting
the job done"* — forbids quietly choosing a lower, safer number that would let the suite
shrink without complaint. The floor is measured at build time and stated; it is not
negotiated, and it is not rounded down for comfort.

### §BH19(k) — THE THIRD LEG WILL GATE ITS OWN COMMIT

Worth recording before it happens, so it is not later mistaken for a coincidence: the
gate executes `tier2_gate.py` **from the working tree**. The commit that adds the third
leg is therefore the FIRST commit that leg guards — it runs during its own gate. §BH19(a)
says *"from this commit on, a green gate is evidence about tools/dip0 changes"*, and that
is exact rather than approximate: the boundary falls at the (a) commit inclusive, not at
the one after it.

### §BH19(l) — WHAT IS BUILT IN THIS COMMIT: NOTHING

Transcription only, per §BH19's own instruction, §BC and §AC. No third leg, no floor, no
gate edit, no audit run, no join measurement, no queue append, and nothing under `apps/`,
`tools/` or `var/` touched at all. §BH19(e) fixes this commit as the FIRST of a
five-step order, and none of the four that follow is begun here or prepared here. C3 is
untouched and stays BLOCKING, exactly where §BH17(c) and §BH18(d) left it.

## §BH20 — THE STALENESS FINDING IS ACCEPTED AND ITS REPAIR QUEUED, THE C4A REGENERATION IS ORDERED AS AN INTERVENTION ON MEASURED STATE, AND THE JOIN IS THEN MEASURED AGAINST THE FRESH VIEWS

§BH20 answers the §BH19(b) report. That report ran the widened audit live, recorded
the `:86` stop as the guard working, and then found that the C4C views did not
reflect the widening at all: `run_c4b.load_c4a()` re-runs C4a only "if it is not on
disk", the three Jul 14 C4A artifacts existed, and so a FRESH file list was combined
with a STALE face set — `file_count: 3` beside `face_count: 0`. The executor reported
that finding, named the only available remedy as an intervention on measured state,
declined to take it unruled, and stopped. §BH20 rules on it.

It is the SEVENTH ruling to arrive with that identical instruction — *"Transcribe per
§BC (pure append), its own commit per §AC, before acting"* — after §BH13, §BH14, §BH16,
§BH17, §BH18 and §BH19, with §BH15 carrying the same instruction in a widened
parenthetical. That count is measured across the whole register, not read off the
nearest neighbours; the first draft of this paragraph said "fourth … after §BH17, §BH18
and §BH19" and was wrong, for the reason recorded at §BH20(f). §BH20 carries FOUR
lettered rulings plus the standing caveat on its own line.

### §BH20(a) — THE STALENESS FINDING IS ACCEPTED AS RECORDED, AND ITS REPAIR IS QUEUED, NOT PERFORMED

> The staleness finding is accepted as recorded: run_c4b.load_c4a() tests
> existence, not freshness, and the Jul 14 C4A artifacts blocked the widening
> from reaching the face set. The repair — a freshness guard — is QUEUED as
> its own commit through the gate, owner-gated, not performed in this act.

### §BH20(b) — THE REGENERATION IS ORDERED AS AN INTERVENTION ON MEASURED STATE

> The regeneration is ordered as an intervention on measured state: delete
> the three stale C4A outputs (var/ tier, git-ignored), then re-run the
> two-stage chain under default environment — no overrides, no --milestone.
> Declaration first, per your §BH19(b) discipline: expectations written and
> sealed before anything executes, including the :86 FrozenMilestoneWrite
> stop, which is again the guard working, not a defect. After the run: the
> frozen milestone tree hash-identical, dip0a untouched, worktree clean,
> HEAD unmoved. If any tracked file moves, stop and report.

> (§BH12(a)); the audit records evidence paths and never reads a licence

> §BH19 record.

### §BH20(e) — THE ORDER, AND THIS COMMIT'S PLACE IN IT

§BH20 does not letter its order the way §BH19(e) did, but the order is fixed by the
text: (b) says "then re-run", (c) says "THEN §BH19(c) proceeds", and (d) disposes of
the record produced by both. With the transcription instruction in the header, that
makes FOUR steps:

    transcription  ->  (b) delete + re-run + declare  ->  (c) join measurement
                   ->  (d) docs commit to the queue

THIS COMMIT IS THE FIRST OF FOUR. Nothing in (b), (c) or (d) is begun or prepared
here. Note what is NOT in the list: no code commit. §BH20(d) says "No code lands
under this ruling", so unlike §BH19 — whose (a) was a gate edit — this arc's only
commits are this transcription and the (d) docs record.

### §BH20(f) — EVERY FACTUAL ASSERTION IN THE OWNER'S TEXT WAS VERIFIED AT TRANSCRIPTION TIME, AND ALL HOLD

§BH11 established that the owner's citations are checked before transcribing, not
after. There are more of them in §BH20 than in §BH19, and all hold:

1. **`run_c4b.load_c4a()` tests existence, not freshness** — verified in source. Its
   docstring reads "Re-run C4a first if it is not on disk", and the test is
   `if not all(p.exists() for p in need)` over `faces.json`, `files.json`,
   `groups.json`. There is no mtime comparison and no input-hash comparison.
2. **The Jul 14 C4A artifacts blocked the widening** — verified by measurement at
   §BH19(b) time: all three dated Jul 14 16:16, and `grep` for `static/fonts` and
   `NotoSans` in `faces.json` and `files.json` returns 0, against a positive control
   of 1901 `.otf` hits in the face manifest.
3. **"the three stale C4A outputs (var/ tier, git-ignored)"** — exactly three files
   exist in `var/design_intelligence/audits/dip0c/c4a/`, and `git check-ignore -v`
   resolves them to `.gitignore:66  var/`. The count, the tier and the ignore status
   are each measured, not assumed.
4. **The §BH18 Q4 table** — exists at `OWNER_REVIEW_QUEUE.md:11846`, headed "Q4 —
   WHAT THE JOIN WOULD SEE AFTERWARDS, AND WHY THE PRIZE IS SMALL". Each of the four
   rows §BH20(c) cites is present and reads as the owner summarises it:
   `verification` `UNVERIFIED` -> `LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`; `is_fallback` **True**
   -> **True**; `CONTAINER_FONT_FALLBACK_DETECTED` fires -> **still fires**.
5. **`§BH12(a)`** — exists at register line 14579, headed "PRODUCER: OPTION B", and
   its owner text contains the reservation verbatim: "reading the OFL is my act, not
   code's". It also independently confirms §BH20(c)'s frame — "a join over dip0c
   evidence by file_sha256, ceiling LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED". Unlike §BH11 there is
   nothing dangling to supersede.
6. **The four named symbols** — `confirmed_fonts`, `LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`,
   `is_fallback` and `CONTAINER_FONT_FALLBACK_DETECTED` all exist in
   `apps/pipeline/targets/container/__init__.py` and its tests, with a negative
   control on an invented symbol returning empty, so the query discriminates.

**AND ONE OF MY OWN CLAIMS FAILED THAT CHECK, WHICH IS WHY IT IS RUN ON THEM TOO.**
The preamble above first said §BH20 was the FOURTH ruling to carry the transcription
instruction, "after §BH17, §BH18 and §BH19". A line-oriented `grep` for the instruction
returned six lines, of which the §BH18 one was missing because the phrase is WRAPPED
ACROSS A NEWLINE in that block, so `grep` — which matches within a line — could not see
it. Re-running the search newline-tolerantly over the whole file gives §BH13, §BH14,
§BH16, §BH17, §BH18 and §BH19 for the exact form, plus §BH15 in a widened parenthetical:
§BH20 is the SEVENTH, and the corrected sentence is what stands above. This is the SAME
NAIVE-QUERY CLASS as the §BH11 substring miss, the `grep -v dip0c` filter that silently
discarded every line because the path prefix always matched, and the "no cache" grep at
§BH19(b) that searched for the WORD `cache` when the caching was an existence check on a
file. The class recurs; the counter is a control on every count, including the ones in
the transcriber's own prose.

### §BH20(g) — "TWO CONTAINER FACES" AGAINST THREE `static/fonts` FONT FILES IS NOT A DIVERGENCE, AND WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

The live run measured the second root as FOUR files — three `.ttf` and `OFL.txt` —
and FONT rows rising by exactly THREE. §BH20(c) says "the two container faces" and
"confirmed_fonts gains two entries". Two against three is precisely the shape of an
owner-number divergence, so it was checked before transcription rather than reported.

IT IS NOT ONE. The §BH18 Q4 table already carries BOTH numbers in adjacent sentences:
it grepped "the three `static/fonts` hashes" and got 0, 0, 0, and it says "both
container faces would match by `file_sha256`". The corpus gains three font files; the
join keys on two of them. The third, `NotoNaskhArabic-Regular.ttf`, is in the audit
corpus but is not one of the pair the container target names.

This is recorded for the reason §BH19(g) established: this arc's rule is that a
divergence is REPORTED and never resolved, and a FALSE divergence reported with
confidence is that same failure inverted. Which two faces the join actually keys on
is left to be MEASURED at (c), not asserted here.

### §BH20(h) — §BH20(a) AND §BH20(b) DO NOT CONFLICT: ONE GOVERNS THE CODE, THE OTHER THE STATE

Read quickly, (a) and (b) look opposed — (a) refuses to repair the staleness defect
now, (b) orders the stale state cleared immediately. They govern different objects.

**(a) governs the CODE.** `load_c4a()` keeps its existence-only test. The freshness
guard is queued as its own commit through the gate, owner-gated, per §AC. So the
defect survives its own workaround, exactly as §BH19(a) kept 8fd9541's ungated
shipment standing after the third leg landed.

**(b) governs the STATE.** Deleting the three artifacts is not a circumvention of the
guard; it is the ONLY route the existing code offers. Measured at §BH19(b) time: the
whole `c4a`/`c4b`/`c4c` chain has ZERO `add_argument` and no force, rebuild or stale
handling, against a control of four flags in `dip0/run.py`. `load_c4a()`'s own
docstring documents the path being used — it re-runs C4a when the outputs are absent.
The intervention makes the documented branch the one that executes.

### §BH20(i) — THE INTERVENTION IS BOUNDED TO GIT-IGNORED STATE, AND CARRIES AN EXPLICIT TRIPWIRE

§BH20(b) adds a stop condition that §BH19(b) did not have: **"If any tracked file
moves, stop and report."** That is a tripwire, not a summary of the expected result,
and it converts the post-conditions into a live abort rather than a post-hoc
disappointment. The four post-conditions are named: frozen milestone tree
hash-identical, dip0a untouched, worktree clean, HEAD unmoved.

The blast radius is bounded by measurement rather than by intent: `var/` is
git-ignored at `.gitignore:66`, so every file being deleted and every artifact being
rewritten is outside the tracked tree. This is why "worktree clean" is a WEAK signal
here and must not be reported as if it were strong — the worktree would be clean even
if nothing ran at all. The mtimes and the tree hashes are what carry the proof.

### §BH20(j) — §BH20(c) SETS A SCORING DISCIPLINE, NOT A TARGET TO HIT

"Score expectation against measurement; where they diverge, report the divergence,
don't chase it." The Q4 row set is therefore a PREDICTION TO BE SCORED, not a result
to be produced. If `face_manifest` does not gain the faces, or `confirmed_fonts`
gains a number other than two, or `verification` lands somewhere other than
`LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, the ruled act is to report that — not to adjust the run
until the table matches.

"No per-face claim beyond what is measured" binds the report's language too: the two
faces are to be named and their fields measured individually, with nothing inferred
about one from the other, and nothing inferred about either from the package.

### §BH20(k) — THE CEILING IS RESTATED, NOT MOVED, AND (c) CANNOT REACH PAST IT

§BH20(c) reaches `LICENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and stops. That is the terminal MACHINE
state, not an approval, and three independent things hold it there:

* §BH12(a)'s producer ceiling — "machine-writable states only", structurally
  incapable of emitting `VERIFIED_FOR_PRODUCTION` or any `HUMAN_ONLY` state.
* Q4's measured reason that `is_fallback` does not clear: `SOURCES_CLEARING_FALLBACK`
  is `{USER_CONFIRMED, UNDECLARED}`, and a machine cannot acquire `USER_CONFIRMED`
  by the act of confirming — §BH15(a)'s ceiling holds straight through the change.
* §BH20(c)'s own restatement: "the audit records evidence paths and never reads a
  licence into a state", with the OFL reading reserved to the owner by §BH12(a).

So the measured yield of the whole (b)+(c) sequence remains what Q4 already priced:
ONE GATE CODE CHANGES ITS NAME. Nothing becomes licensed. C3 is untouched and stays
BLOCKING, where §BH17(c), §BH18(d) and §BH19 left it.

### §BH20(l) — WHAT IS BUILT IN THIS COMMIT: NOTHING

Transcription only, per §BH20's own instruction, §BC and §AC. No deletion of any C4A
artifact, no audit run, no join measurement, no queue append, no freshness guard, and
nothing under `apps/`, `tools/` or `var/` touched at all. The three stale C4A outputs
are still in place, still dated Jul 14, when this commit lands — §BH20(b) is the NEXT
act, not this one. The 132-file frozen tree does not move.

  Montserrat-ThinItalic), Quicksand[wght] (300–700, default 300 =
  Quicksand-Light), PlayfairDisplay[wght] (400–900, default 400 =
  PlayfairDisplay-Regular), PlayfairDisplay-Italic[wght] (400–900, default
  PlayfairDisplay-Italic). Each carries a STAT table and fvar named instances
  with PostScript names (Montserrat Thin…Black at 100…900, so Montserrat-Regular
  at 400 and Montserrat-Bold at 700; Quicksand Light…Bold at 300…700; Playfair
  Regular…Black at 400…900 as PlayfairDisplayRoman-* / PlayfairDisplayItalic-*),
  so an instance is pinnable by the font's own name — hard stop 2 does not fire
  on measurement. The other 30 are static; the static Montserrat-Regular is one
  of them (its own granted file). Of the five, only Montserrat[wght] sits in a
  ruled chain (heading); the other four are reachable only as a 2A-6E
  confirmed_font at the display role on a non-exempt surface. The Noto trio is
  static.

  READINGS RECORDED FOR THE OWNER TO OVERRULE (the sentence governs):
  (a) (2) pins Montserrat[wght]'s instance per role; it does not re-rule the

**Quoted verbatim — the option the owner's (b) names, by letter: A.**

- **A. brand_gov stays authoritative over library palettes.** A library colour can enter only as a candidate under a brand role and only when within a measured distance (ΔE) of a brand swatch, or as an explicitly ruled addition. Consequence: outputs stay inside the seeded palettes; the library changes tone, never the palette; the 14 literal swatches in `design_language.py` are re-pinned to the record so the duplicates cannot drift.

The owner's (b) sentence is NARROWER than A where they differ and governs: A admits a library colour as a candidate "when within a measured distance (ΔE) of a brand swatch, or as an explicitly ruled addition"; the ruling admits the PRODUCTION library palette as candidates "only where a role has no brand colour". The layer is built to the ruling: a role with a brand_gov colour resolves to it and takes no library candidate; a role without one may take a PRODUCTION-palette candidate; REFERENCE palettes are inspiration only.

### §BH44(a) — THE PLACEMENT TAKEN AND WHAT THE REPAIR MEASURED (executor)

**Placement, and the exception invoked.** Pure append after the §BH44 block, in the SAME append and the SAME commit as that block — which §AC would ordinarily forbid, and which this ruling's own first paragraph authorises: the register gates red, so no commit lands at all until the suite is green, and a transcription that must land before acting cannot land ahead of the repair that makes landing possible. The owner's sentence names this the §BC header exception and his ORDER line puts both transcriptions in the repair commit. Proved against the 20,490-line staged register (`a47415fec69706a5`); the 52 typed lines round-trip byte-identical out of the blockquote (`6130acfbd95a7520`); nothing above either block is touched.

**(1) THE REPAIR, and the proof the ruling demanded.** `tools/dip0c/tests/test_c1.py::test_ghostscript_adapter_blocked` asserted `eps_capability_state == EPS_GHOSTSCRIPT_NOT_INSTALLED` — a fact about the host, not the code — and an owner-ruled `brew install ghostscript` moved the adapter to its other blocked state, `GHOSTSCRIPT_PILOT_PENDING`. It is replaced by `test_ghostscript_adapter_blocked_when_gs_absent` and `..._when_gs_present`, each patching `detect_ghostscript` and each asserting all four invariants through one shared `_assert_blocked_invariants` helper. **The count went up: the dip0c leg measures 671 → 672.** The proof the ruling asked for was run TWO ways rather than one: with this machine as it stands (`/opt/homebrew/bin/gs`, 10.08.0) the file is **28 passed**, and with every PATH directory holding a `gs` binary stripped — `shutil.which("gs")` returning `None` inside the test process, so the absence is real and not merely patched — the file is **28 passed** again. The adapter's behaviour is unchanged; only the test's dependence on the machine is gone.

**(2) THE PROSE, and the conditional the ruling attached to the second file.** `eps_ghostscript.py:3` opened *"Ghostscript is absent in this environment"* and is corrected to state the two capability states and assert nothing about the machine. `artwork_preview.py:269` raised the refusal *"ASCII EPS carries no embedded preview; Ghostscript is absent"*. The ruling says to correct it only if its false statement is the SAME CLASS — a claim that Ghostscript is absent — and it is that claim verbatim, so it is corrected. Measured before touching it: no test anywhere asserts either string, so neither correction moves a test. The refusal now names what is missing from the FILE (*"and this path renders only from an embedded preview"*), which is both true and the actual reason that code path refuses — it reads an embedded TIFF and never shells out to a rasteriser, so Ghostscript's presence was never relevant to it.

**(3) THE DEFECT CLASS.** The lesson is recorded where the ruling put it: `PIN_CLASSES` in `tools/brain/server.py`, the classes `brain.lessons` answers by, which go from twelve to thirteen with `machine`. The comment beside it states why the class had to exist — every other pin class is a fact about the REPOSITORY, and none of them reaches the machine the repository runs on, which is exactly how a census that checked every pin class still missed an install. The lesson itself now lives in this register block, which the brain indexes, so the class has something to retrieve.

**(4) THE FIVE ADDRESSES, and the divergence to be recorded rather than resolved.** The ruling settles what they are: an earlier session found them and recorded no source, and that is the whole of their provenance. So the dispatch record was **TRUE about evidence** — there is no recorded address, `explicit_address: null` is an honest statement about what was established — and **FALSE about the file's contents**, because five `.eml` files carry a `To:` header. §BH44(a)'s work records both halves side by side rather than editing either into agreement with the other, and each of the five is then verified against a live published page and landed as CONFIRMED with page and date, CORRECTED with the old and the new value both shown, or UNRESOLVED with the extent of the search stated.

**What this commit does NOT do.** It resolves no address, fetches no page, writes no pack, and sends nothing. It repairs a test that asserted a fact about this machine, corrects two sentences that asserted the same fact, records the class, and lands the two transcriptions that had to precede the work. §BH44 (a) through (d) begins after it.

### §BH44(b) — THE PLACEMENT TAKEN AND HOW CAPACITY WILL BE MEASURED (executor)

**Placement.** Pure append after the §BH44(a) block, its own commit before any act of the goal — the ordinary §BC placement, the header exception of §BH44(a) having been spent on the red gate it was granted for. Proved against the 20,563-line HEAD `76b23e4` (`e3f054181e281337`); the 20 typed lines round-trip byte-identical out of the blockquote (`ca2280a374f00f6b`); nothing above this block is touched. **State at receipt:** the repair landed at `76b23e4` and scored 6/8, L2 and L7 both missing the same fact — a refused run leaves a ledger line in the worktree, so the next successful run folds two. The ledger now measures **507 in the worktree and 507 at HEAD**, so this commit's fold is one line, measured at both endpoints rather than reasoned about in prose. Suite 8,648 collected, apps 7,835, dip0c 672, failures 0; worktree clean. §BH44 (a) through (d) has not begun: no page fetched, no address resolved, no pack written, nothing sent.

**CAPACITY COSTS NO EXTRA FETCH, and that is why it belongs to (a).** The ruling puts capacity *"from the same published pages you are already reading"*. So it is not a second research pass: the page opened to find a contact channel is read for both facts at once, and both carry the same page URL and the same fetch date. A capacity is recorded only where the company **states** it — the ruling's own verbs are *"states it makes or tools its own containers"* and *"states it stocks or resells"*. An inference from a product range, a domain name, or an industry guess is not a statement, and where a page says neither the value is **UNSTATED**, which is a finding and not a gap.

**THE MAPPING IS BY CLASS, AND IT IS THE ONLY PLACE JUDGEMENT COULD LEAK IN.** *"whether a company of that stated capacity could plausibly hold that evidence at all"* is a question about the CAPACITY, not about the company: the mark for a given `requires` item is the same for every supplier that states the same capacity, and it is derived once per capacity class and applied. That keeps it reportage. What the executor does NOT do, because the ruling forbids it in the same sentence — *"you conclude nothing about whether to write to them"* — is rank the five, recommend one over another, suggest dropping any, or shape the pack around the mapping. All five remain in the pack with their letters unchanged, whatever the mapping says.

**THE FINDING CLAUSE, and why it is written down before the measurement rather than after.** Gate B's five items are *qualified bottle drawing, qualified closure drawing, product codes, tolerances, compatibility evidence*. It is a live possibility that a list of five container **distributors** holds catalogue codes and compatibility notes while the qualified drawings and the tolerances sit with the factories that tool the glass — in which case no addressee can satisfy Gate B and the owner learns it before he sends. The ruling asks for that plainly, names it *"a fact about my supplier list, not about your work"*, and the executor records here, in advance of measuring, that a negative result will be reported as directly as a positive one. **The measurement decides it. Nothing above is a prediction of the outcome**, and the report will state what the pages said rather than what this paragraph anticipated.

**WHAT STAYS OUTSIDE.** *"Adding a supplier is my ruling and stays outside this goal: the five I authorized remain the five."* So the executor does not seek, propose, name or research a sixth company, does not suggest a category of company to add, and does not treat a gap in the mapping as licence to fill it. ### §BH45(e) — THE PLACEMENT TAKEN, (1) AS RULED, AND WHY (2) WAITS ONE MORE SENTENCE (executor)

**Placement.** Pure append after the §BH45 block, its own commit before any act of this ruling. Proved against the 20,684-line HEAD `8283a2b` (`1e296add7347644e`); the 33 typed lines round-trip byte-identical out of the blockquote (`b114346f79ee3252`); nothing above this block is touched. **State at receipt:** §BH45 landed as `f77926f` → `73fdb4e` → `1f4258d` → `8283a2b`, 30/32, its report delivered. The ledger reads **513 in the worktree and 513 at HEAD**, so this commit's fold is one line. Suite 8,648 collected, apps 7,835, dip0c 672, dip0 141, failures 0; worktree clean. The body is `cb5423b8fe27902e` at 2,444 characters in all five drafts, and `supplier_requests_sent` is 0 in every record.

**(1) PROCEEDS AS RULED, and one premise is measured first.** The check at `supplier_dispatch.py:52` is `(?i)pantone|\bcmyk\b|\bspot colour\b|#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}`. Its last alternative already fires on `#CBA87D`, so *"print this in #CBA87D"* is caught by the check as it stands; what the word-match never caught, measured, is a value set without the word — `C0 M20 Y30 K0`, `C=0 M=20 Y=30 K=0` — and a PMS number, `PMS 7527`. The bar goes up there. The narrowed rule flags a numbered Pantone or PMS reference, a CMYK value set, a hex code, and an instructing sentence: an imperative (print, reproduce, match, use, apply, render, coat, finish, anodise, spray, stamp, foil) followed in the same clause by *in / to / as / with* and a colour system, a value, or a plain colour name (gold, rose gold, silver, copper, bronze, black, white, pink, rose…). A question naming Pantone, CMYK and spot colours passes, and so does every sentence of the current body and of the paragraph previewed in the report, both measured before this was written. The key `no_colour_system_assignment` keeps its name in every record, because it now means what it says. New tests pin both sides, and the two existing tests (`test_supplier_dispatch.py:155-158` and `:177-180`) are re-anchored to assert the absence of an assignment. No record is regenerated in (1): on the unchanged body the narrowed check yields the same record byte for byte, measured dry.

**(2) IS HELD FOR ONE MORE SENTENCE, ON A CENSUS FINDING THAT IS MY MISS.** The T45 reading listed `supplier_evidence_request_dispatch.json` and its pack as re-derivable by *"one generator"* and did not run that generator dry. Run dry today on the unchanged body, `dispatch(write=False)` does not reproduce the record on disk. The drafts record has carried `destination` and `destination_owner_approved` since `5ec8a59` (2026-07-31 16:24); the dispatch record was written at `50fd811` (15:39) and never re-derived. So a re-derivation flips `resolved` to true and fills `email_addresses_in_draft` for all five, empties `codes`, and drops `blocking_checks` to `recipient_identity_known` alone, because `validate()` equates identity with a `contact_name` (`:112`) that no draft has. Three tests pin the 2026-07-31 state and go red on the re-derived record — `test_every_request_carries_the_unresolved_code` (`test_supplier_dispatch.py:92`), `test_no_draft_contains_any_address` (`:97`), `test_no_address_was_ever_invented` (`:109`) — and a fourth, `test_bodies_were_not_modified_after_authorization` (`:193`), pins a fact that (2) makes false. Worse than the tests: the generator hardcodes its findings as 2026-07-31 prose — `blocking_reason` *"no destination…"* (`:220`), `bodies_modified_after_authorization: False` (`:228`), `what_would_unblock` (`:230`), `owner_clarification_required: True` (`:238`) and the pack's header *"NOT SENT: no destination is recorded for any of the five"* (`:261`) — so a record re-derived through it would carry the new body hash beside a stated reason that is no longer true. And one latent breach: `validate()` labels an unblocked request `SENT_PENDING_SUPPLIER_RESPONSE` (`:151`) and `dispatch()` counts those as `requests_sent` and `supplier_requests_sent` (`:185`, `:208`, `:212`) — a send recorded by a module that sends nothing. Today `recipient_identity_known` masks it; a `contact_name` on any draft would move the counter off 0, through the hard stop. Its readers carry the same date: `vq_views.py:736` hardcodes the blocking code, `vq1_review.html:56` states *"there is nowhere to send"*, and `production_authority_gate.json:227` gives the same reason. Last, the preflight: `render_package()` re-embeds the checklist, the specification, the drafts, the gates and the receipts (`production_authority_package.py:365-370`) and not `supplier_dispatch` or `supplier_manifest`, which reached it by hand at `50fd811` and `5ec8a59`; the ruling says the preflight moves in the letter's commit, and as the code stands it moves only by hand-editing a generated record.

So (2) as ruled reaches one of three states, and the executor takes none: a record re-derived through a generator whose prose contradicts its data and whose tests go red; a generated record patched by hand; or a record whose hash stays where the ruling says it moves. **The letter waits for one ruling** on a repair that is its own commit between (1) and (2), proposed here with its boundary so that it can be ruled *as proposed and no wider* — **THE DISPATCH RECORD SAYS WHAT IS:** (i) `validate()` labels an unblocked request `READY_NOT_SENT`; `requests_sent` and `supplier_requests_sent` are 0 by construction in this module, which sends nothing, and advance only through `supplier_sent_validation` on returned evidence, as the manifest already states; (ii) `resolve_recipient()` reads the drafts' owner-approved `destination`, and a company with its owner-approved published address is a known recipient, `contact_name` staying optional; (iii) `blocking_reason`, `what_would_unblock`, `owner_clarification_required` and the pack's header derive from the rows, and say so when nothing blocks; (iv) `bodies_modified_after_authorization` is read from the drafts record, which (2) then amends with the ruling, the date, the paragraph and both hashes beside it; (v) `render_package()` re-embeds the dispatch record, the manifest, the sent-validation and the deferral from their files; (vi) `vq_views.py:736` reads the code from the record, and the template's and the gate record's 2026-07-31 sentences are dated as history; (vii) the tests that pin 2026-07-31 are re-anchored to the measured present, and one new test asserts that no status in the record contains SENT. The record and the pack are re-derived on the UNCHANGED body in that commit, so their hashes stay `cb5423b8fe27902e` and (2)'s diff is the body's alone. Extent: `supplier_dispatch.py`, `production_authority_package.py`, `vq_views.py`, `vq1_review.html`, `test_supplier_dispatch.py`, the dispatch record, the pack, the preflight json/pdf/png. If he narrows it, his sentence governs; if he rules it, (2) follows with the preview in the report as its prediction.

**ORDER, as this reading takes it.** This transcription; then (1) as ruled, its own commit; then the stop report carrying the repair above, one word of his away; then the repair; then (2). **(3)** as ruled: the `_FRONT_RE` skip (`tools/brain/vault.py:439`, *"feat(§BH44(c)+(d)):"* unmatched) is queued and not touched. (b), (c), (d) stand. The hard stops are unchanged and govern: nothing sent or submitted, no credential anywhere, `supplier_requests_sent` 0, no derived artefact left disagreeing with its body, no hash written that its preview did not predict.
