**THE OUTREACH-CAPABLE CODE, MEASURED OVER apps/.** Mail: one `EmailMessage()` (`supplier_eml.py:155`) composes a file; no module calls `send_mail`, `get_connection`, `smtplib` or `.send()`. HTTP: `requests.get` at `spec_sheet.py:84` fetches a packaging image by URL for a PDF, not a supplier; the research family — `web_research.py` (a governed fetcher, `:179`), `web_research_tavily.py` (a search API, `:107`), `web_geometry_research.py` and `technical_geometry_research.py` (VQ-1-RESET-1B, 2026-07-28, whose queries name `site:liquidbottles.com` and `site:nicerpackaging.com`) — is imported by no view, no command and no target: the two web-research views (`views.py:2215`, `:2351`) serve stored sessions and decisions, and `visual_review.py`, which calls the governed fetcher, is imported by no live entry point. Forms: nothing in apps/ posts to one. So today no outreach path is live and none is wired, and the goal-state test makes that a measurement rather than a reading: it walks `apps/pipeline/services` for mail-transport calls, for fetch calls that name a supplier domain, for form submission, and asserts that the research fetchers are reached from no view, command or target. The research modules that name supplier sites are annotated superseded by §BH46 in their docstrings; nothing in them is deleted.

**§AZ0(u), AS §BH9(a) PINS IT.** Executor text is struck in place; owner text is annotated, never rewritten. The records, READMEs, docstrings and the pack are executor text, so each supersession is an annotation ADDED in place — a `superseded_by` field on a record, a dated line on a document, a line in a docstring — and no line is removed. Where a record is re-derived on every run (the dispatch record, the manifest, and after (d) the gate record), the annotation lives in the generator, because a hand-written field would not survive the next run. The register is owner text and receives nothing but this append and the goal report's; no marker is placed in it (§BH9(b)).

**THE BUILD, AS THIS READING TAKES IT — one concern per commit, each predicted from a repository-shaped preview and scored, the guard procedure before every seal.**
(a) SUPERSESSION. The dispatch generator emits `superseded_by: "§BH46"` and the sentence; the manifest generator the same; the tracking sheet and the pack README gain a dated annotation at their head; `supplier_dispatch.py`, `supplier_eml.py`, `supplier_sent_validation.py` and the two research modules that name supplier sites gain the line in their docstrings. `supplier_requests_sent` stays 0 in every record, and the tests that assert it — in the dispatch, eml, sent-validation and preflight files — are re-docstringed as the proof that no outreach path exists, joined by `TestNoOutreachPathIsLive`. Nothing is deleted; every record and file the pack holds stays.
(b)+(d) THE GATES SAY WHAT IS. A generator, `production_authority_gates.py`, writes `production_authority_gate.json` on every run from two inputs: Gate A's block, moved verbatim into `production_authority_gate_a.json` as the owner-ruled 2026-07-31 pass (a byte-equal extraction, and the old record stays in git), and the intake state. B–E carry `requires` unchanged, `source: "OWNER_SUPPLIED_SPEC_PACK"`, a per-item state (MISSING, REFUSED or SATISFIED, the last with its provenance record), `blocked_by: "no owner-supplied evidence intaken for this item"` naming the items, the old `blocked_code` kept beside a new `cause`, `evidence_authority_order` opening with *"owner-supplied supplier technical drawing"*, `gates_passed` computed from satisfied items, and `next_required_owner_action` *"place the spec pack"* with the missing items listed. The preflight re-embeds it and the board derives its gate lines from it. The test at `test_gate_a_final.py:365` re-anchors from *"SUPPLIER absent"* to *"no outreach verb"*, because the missing items name supplier documents by their own `requires` text; `test_production_authority_preflight.py:270` re-anchors to the owner-supplied order.
(c) THE INTAKE, two commits. First the location and the validator: `docs/production_authority_intake/` beside `production_authority/` — `spec_pack/` for the documents, `spec_pack_manifest.json` the owner's mapping of each document to the item it satisfies with `handed_over_by` and `handed_over_on`, `intake_state.json` and `intake_provenance.json` derived — and `spec_pack_intake.py`, whose nineteen rules are derived from the `requires` text: the kind of document that satisfies the item, the product it must name, dimensions with units for a drawing, a certificate or datasheet for a material claim, the colour systems named for the Pantone item, and so on, each written in words an owner can act on; refusals by name (`WRONG_PRODUCT`, `NO_DIMENSIONS`, `NO_CERTIFICATE`, `NO_PROVENANCE`, `FILE_MISSING`, `SHA_MISMATCH`, `WRONG_KIND`); provenance required before any acceptance, the sha256 measured at intake and matched to the manifest's. Then the dry-run: `dry_run()` over the location as it stands — empty — writing `dry_run.json` and `dry_run.md`, one line per item: what it needs, in the owner's words. The negative controls are tests: a document naming another product, a drawing with no dimension, a material claim with no certificate, a document with no provenance — each refused by its name.
(e) THE CAUSE. Every live instance annotated: the gate record and the preflight by regeneration, `vq2_state.json` by a cause field beside each code with the code kept, the dashboard's two sentences, the board's four lines, the pack's map; the historical records untouched and listed in the report with the reason. Then the goal report.

**WHAT THIS READING DECIDES AND WHAT IT LEAVES TO HIM.** Taken: the intake location's name; the codes kept and annotated rather than renamed, because §AZ0(u) says annotate and a code is executor text that tests pin; the dated closeouts read as history. Left for his sentence, stated in the report: whether the codes should instead be renamed, and whether the research family should be quarantined further than a docstring. The hard stops govern from here: no deletion, no rewrite of history, no outreach path left live, no gate flipped by anything but intaken evidence per item, no spec accepted without provenance.

**WHAT ALREADY WRITES DECISIONS FROM A BROWSER, MEASURED BESIDE THE SEAM AND RECORDED, NOT CHANGED.** The VQ-1 review page's decision endpoint (`apps/pipeline/vq_views.py:1081–1105`, CORR-1) is today's one browser path that writes a human decision into a tracked file, `docs/visual_quality/vq1/vq1_human_structural_review.json`: any logged-in account, the username and a timestamp, no sha256, no gate, prior decisions kept in the file's history. While it stands, any logged-in account can press ACCEPT over his REVISION_REQUIRED record and dirty the tracked tree, which breaks the goal state's clean worktree; no slice links to it until he has ruled whether it stays, moves to the seam, or is retired. Browser decisions also enter governed database rows: the Gate-1 and Gate-2 approvals (`apps/pipeline/views.py:486–488`, `:571–573`, through `_record_decision`, `:358–364`), the batch Gate-1 approval (`apps/pipeline/batch_views.py:184`), the container-profile confirmation (`views.py:1453–1476`) and the palette confirmation (`apps/dashboard/views.py:111–192`), which records every action as actor 'OWNER' whoever posts (`:182–183`). The Django admin (`config/urls.py:23`) lets both superusers add and change a GateDecision with any decided_by, and a PackagingOutput's spec sheet, where Gate 2 reads `container_human_visual_acceptance` and honours any non-empty decided_by (`apps/ire/container_production_readiness.py:67–86`). Two design-intent approvals carry no actor (GateDecision 56 and 62, from the M5/M6 traces). Read: the hard stop "a machine-written acceptance" reaches any of these a slice builds on or exposes, and the seam's no-write and acceptance tests cover the admin path. Left to him: whether the seam's acceptance becomes the writer of the key Gate 2 reads or stays apart from Gate 2, and whether the admin's write forms stand.

**THE HARD STOP ON FACES AND COLOURS, READ — two readings for his line.** The governed sets are read as the granted faces through the role layer (the catalogue's 35, the faces his (c)3 names, and the Noto trio: 38 granted faces over 37 grant rows, his own set in §BH49's hard stop, §BH49 LIVE, :21096–21178) and brand_gov plus the PRODUCTION palette. The stop is read on what the system DRAWS: a design the composers compose, in an exploration or an artefact, is a render; showing bytes the system already holds (a past artefact, a generated concept, a material and its palette) is a display, labelled with its tier and provenance, and is not a render under this stop. If he meant every picture the interface shows, his sentence says so. Slice 1 draws nothing: it streams stored bytes and calls none of the paths that render on a GET — the concept-reference thumbnail (`apps/pipeline/views.py:2029–2038`), the spec-sheet download that generates a missing PDF onto the output (`:1927–1930`), and the palette page's overlay into MEDIA_ROOT (`apps/dashboard/views.py:194–199`). For a composed design the stop carries no "as a default" qualifier, unlike §BH50's colour stop, so it has two readings. As typed, it fires on any colour a composed design draws that does not resolve through brand_gov or the PRODUCTION palette: no product composer declares a colour-role map today, every composed design falls through to the surface's own literals, and slice 2 then renders no composed design until those colours resolve — after §BH50(d) lands and, beyond it, his line on the role each dark colour takes, since accent_dark and ink carry no brand swatch in the §BH39 record (brand_gov holds Deep Rose #8B3A52 and Cocoa Rose #7A4A42 for typography, without a role) and the PRODUCTION palette is reachable from no emit (`apps/ire/materials_retrieval.py:68–70`). As §BH50's stop is read, after §BH39, a colour drawn as the surface's own literal does not fire it, and slice 2 lands with every fallback literal named on the page and in its record. Held until he rules: the first. Slices 3 and 4, ordered behind slice 2, wait with it unless he reorders. Two readings the stop needs besides, recorded for his line: the process colours (paper white, black, the die line) are the colour layer's own PROCESS source (`apps/ire/colour_roles.py:37`), in neither set, and are read as outside the stop's reach, his sentence governing; and an exempt or untagged document bypasses both layers by design — its faces resolve through `legacy_emitter_fonts`, which registers a confirmed font from any path on disk (`apps/ire/font_roles.py:247–254`, `:276–289`), and its colours come back as the surface's literals (`colour_roles.py:10–13`) — so an exploration composes only documents tagged with a non-exempt surface.

**THE OTHER HARD STOPS AND PINS, READ.** "A REFERENCE asset placed" is read at the emitter's placement seam, which refuses a REFERENCE Image ahead of every byte for every document (`apps/ire/emitters/pdf_ai.py:70–76`, `materials_placement.refuse_or_skip`). An exploration composed through that emitter inherits the refusal, and the seam's test places a REFERENCE asset in an exploration and asserts the refusal by name. Retrieval is a contract with no implementation, so placing PRODUCTION material in an exploration is built, not assumed; a preview raster of a REFERENCE asset, shown for looking, is never an exploration's source. "A slice reported complete on a number instead of my use of it": a slice is reported ready for his use, never complete; it is complete when he has opened it and used it (e), and its report names what it exposes that (b) listed unreachable. "No generation spend without my word": a paid generation call stays behind his word. Three paths the slices would sit beside, measured and not changed: any logged-in account can requeue a failed task into the paid pipeline with no daily-cap check (TaskRetryView, `apps/pipeline/views.py:1644`, `:1691–1694`; the cap is checked only at creation, `:65–68`); a provider call with no task in scope spends with no ApiCallRecord and no cap (`apps/pipeline/services/cost_ledger.py:95–96`, `:114–115`), so a paid call inside an exploration would either write the spend ledger, a governed record, or spend unrecorded; and on the packaging path, confirming dimensions calls the image provider with no cost stated on its button (fifteen flat-artwork ledger rows, $3.75). Whether an exploration may spend, on what word and on which ledger, is his. The pins held unchanged are his, typed in this goal state: the tier record, the protected regions, the tree seals, the M7 artefacts and the intake; §BH50's ORDER holds the same list and adds the exempt non-product surfaces while §BH50 runs. Each is re-measured before every seal; no REFERENCE byte is placed anywhere.

**(c)–(e) THE SLICES, READ.** "Usable in a browser" is read as served by the running dashboard under its existing login (`config/urls.py`, the `apps.dashboard` routes), reached from its navigation, not a file to open. Each slice is its own commits, gated, predicted and scored, under §AC (LIVE, :1964–2413) (d); the explorations the interface serves need no commit, gate, register entry or prediction. Slice 3 shows the 38 granted faces with which is which. Slice 4's "served from the brain" is read with the brain as it is ruled: derived and never authoritative, so every status it shows carries the file and line that owns it and the index's freshness. The dashboard has no path to the brain today (it speaks stdio only, and an import collides with the inner tools package), so building that bridge is part of the slice.

**WHAT THIS READING DECIDES AND WHAT IT LEAVES TO HIM.** Taken, each with its alternative stated above: §BH50 continuing in its own order, with §BH51's slices interleaved at its commit boundaries after his line on the survey; the purpose read as this system's scoring rule, retiring nothing by name; the survey's read-only run before this block disclosed, a supplementary map of the packaging path added, and delivery only on verified maps; exploration held in a per-session store outside the repository's directory, MEDIA_ROOT, both var/ trees and the brain's sources, its requests outside the audit-writing enforcement; acceptance captured in the browser and landed through the gate in the §BH26(a) shape, the executor copying captured fields and supplying none; the face and colour stop read strictly for composed designs until he rules, a display of stored bytes read as outside it; process colours read as outside it; explorations composing only non-exempt documents; the VQ-1 endpoint left unlinked. Left to him: whether §BH51 comes before or after §BH50's remaining parts; which account is his and how its standing is conferred; whether an acceptance refuses every other account; which bytes and what precision an acceptance binds; whether a browser click alone, authenticated and audited, is the acceptance or only its capture; whether the seam's acceptance writes the key Gate 2 reads; whether the admin's write forms stand; whether the VQ-1 endpoint stays, moves to the seam or is retired; which reading of the face and colour stop governs, and any reordering of the slices; whether an exploration may spend, and on what word and ledger; each slice's design, after he has read the survey.

digit — Warm Cream `#FAF3EC`, Blush `#F2C4CE`, Warm Gold `#CBA87D`, with Pale Petal `#F7DDE3` and Warm Nude
`#E8C9B3` beside them (`docs/brand_gov/colour_roles_1_0.json`). The wordmark is on disk at `media/brand/logo.png`,

account, taken while running §BH43(b)'s own first step, was `400 invalid_request_error: Your credit balance is too
low to access the Anthropic API`, and the Phase 4 report closed the item named-with-why on exactly that. A one-token

ruled". §BH60(a) had been answered and its target proposed (`FB-2060 白卡`, the FOCUS pressed powder, with
`BL3090` named as the runner-up and the total leakage of the `DesignReference` anatomy reported); the run
itself had not begun and does not begin until this lands.

**WHAT IS ALREADY MEASURED AT RECEIPT, stated because it narrows his (b) rather than widening it.** The
compact's own vocabulary EXISTS: `CONTAINER_EDITOR_ARCHETYPES` in `apps/pipeline/targets/ui.py` carries
`compact` with variants `rounded_rect / square / round` and closures `clasp / magnet / friction`, added at

  * `container_profile_editor_config()` returns `"defaults": {"archetype": "bottle", "variant":

### §BH66 — THE PLACEMENT TAKEN, THE NOTE HIS (b) ORDERS, AND TWO DIVERGENCES RECORDED (executor)

**Placement.** Pure append after the §BH65 block, its own commit before any act of this ruling. §BH63(b) was
checked and does not apply: §BH66 is the only block in hand. Proved against the 23,252-line HEAD `2203fee`
(prefix sha256[:16] `82738203442363c8`); the 42 typed lines round-trip byte-identical out of the blockquote
(`ee3aefcb9524978b`); nothing above this block is touched.

**HIS (a), SAID ONCE IN THE REGISTER'S OWN IDIOM, because his words never use it.** §AU1's reach is superseded
in part by his (a), as to scope only: it governs bottle, jar and tube fronts as it always has, and it no longer
governs a surface that is its product's face, which today is a compact lid and names a palette, a case and a
box lid ahead of their forms. Every word of §AU1 stands, and §AU8(a)'s contract number with it: the Arabic line
his (a) orders onto a face is the concept's element, drawn from the product record and the concept record, and
is never a second entry of `hierarchy_lines`. Which forms have a face for a primary surface is DECLARED on each
form in the one archetype declaration, with no default, never inferred from a form's name in the composer.

**THE NOTE HIS (b) ORDERS, QUOTING BOTH AND DELETING NEITHER.** On the rule's place, §W4's sentence is
superseded by §AU1, the later of his two rulings on it. §W4 (`:923–925`, signed 2026-08-18) reads: "The front
rule sits above a product name on a container, a different surface with a different print method." §AU1
(`:5654–5657`, ruled 2026-08-21) reads: "The container front, top to bottom, is: the **product name**; below
it a single **fine horizontal rule**; below that **exactly one supporting line of type**." §W4 stands in every
other word — the rule and the Gate-A divider remain two objects, and its (a) to (c) on the rule's weight are
untouched. The brain's census was simulated over this block before the append; what it reads is stated in the
commit, as measured.

**TWO DIVERGENCES FROM HIS TEXT, RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED BY THE EXECUTOR.**
1. *"A compact's lid is ninety by seventy-four millimetres."* The lid drawn on task 89 is 110 × 95 mm, a size
   declared from `BBR-CO-501` at §BH60 and measured nowhere. 90.2 × 74.1 mm is that lid's CONFIRMED DECORATION
   ZONE. His figure is the zone's, and the build lays the face out inside the zone.
2. *"No motif field as a ground behind the mark (§BA / C12)."* §BA ruled C11 the other way round in its
   heading — "the motif field is the surface the mark is printed on", a SURFACE and not a neighbour — and §BB2
   ruled C12 that a motif field IS a permitted ground, on the condition that no strand at or above ΔE 2.3
   crosses the mark's ink box. His (a) is stricter than both. Applied by his own (b) principle, that the later
   of his rulings governs: on a surface that is its product's face no motif field is placed behind the mark,
   and on every other form §BA and §BB2 stand as ruled. A reading of the two citations, not a choice between
   them; one line of the build changes if he meant §BB2's condition.

**HIS (d) ACCEPTS THREE OF THE (c) REPORT'S FIVE CORRECTIONS.** The fourth — the rule drawn above the name —
is his (b). The fifth, that the (c)1 commit message cited §BB5 where §AU1 decides the front, stands as the
report recorded it.

**Order taken.** His (a), then his (b), each its own gated commit; then §BH65(d), the clone re-run on the same
brief and the same withholding, measured with the instrument locked before (c). One report, at the end of (d).

**State at receipt.** HEAD `2203fee`. §BH65(c) complete and reported: `51508ff` → `2203fee`, ten commits.
Tasks 89 and 84 at `awaiting_gate_2`, nothing accepted. Programme spend about $10.75 of the $500 §BH55(2)
authorises; nothing spent since §BH60.

### §BH68 — THE PLACEMENT TAKEN, WHAT HIS (a) ASKS MEASURED FIRST, THE READINGS, AND SIX DIVERGENCES (executor)

**Placement.** Pure append after the §BH67 block, its own commit before any act of this ruling. §BH63(b) was

(`d63f14398a6e6b9d`); nothing above this block is touched.

**HIS (a)'S FIRST QUESTION, MEASURED AT RECEIPT: §BH59 WAS NEVER TRANSCRIBED, AND WHAT IT DESCRIBES WAS NEVER
BUILT.** The register holds no block headed §BH59, and neither do the review queue, the sitting reports or the
executor's own notes: THE BRAIN's `ruling` returns it ABSENT, and its full-text search finds the id only in §BH60's
transcription, which recorded the gap as his numbering when §BH60 arrived after §BH58 (`:22516–22517`). The ruling
that does stand on the hierarchy dimension is §BH58(b), and it ruled the other mechanism: "FIX THE CLASSIFIER" — a
classifier that READS the planner's prose. That is what is built. `direction_signature._classify_hierarchy` finds the
hierarchy family in the `focal_hierarchy` sentence, first by cue phrases ("name first", "motif leads") and then by the
§BH58(b) ordered-list reader, which takes the first ranked item and classes it by the element nouns it contains; the
planner's JSON (`design_direction_generator`, `focal_hierarchy: "..."`) declares no family at all. Task 92's second
direction is the case he names: its lead item, "Oversized ghosted Arabic letterform field", holds the noun "field", and
the reader classed a direction the planner itself calls "typography-led" MOTIF_FIRST.

**THE PASS RATE HE ASKS FOR, AS FOUND.** Five planning runs of this brief are on record: tasks 89 and 91 passed; tasks
90 (at `6b9d56a`), 92 and 93 (at `571b3e1`) failed the planner's own check, each on different codes — 90
DIRECTION_SIGNATURE_INSUFFICIENT with raster dependency in all three directions, 92 HIERARCHY_NOT_DISTINCT with
PALETTE_SYSTEMS_NOT_DISTINCT, 93 MOTIF_NOT_DISTINCT with a raster dependency. Task 94 failed in transport and never
reached the planner. The five fresh plans he orders before and after are measured in the act, not here.

**HIS (a), READ.** §BH58(b)'s classifier for the hierarchy family is superseded in part by his (a), as to that one
dimension's source only: the planner declares its hierarchy family from the known set — NAME_FIRST, MOTIF_FIRST,
MATERIAL_FIRST, LOGO_FIRST, the four `HIERARCHY_FAMILIES` the classifier already names — and the validator reads the
declaration; a family outside the set, or none, is refused by name, never guessed. The rest of §BH58 stands: its (b)'s
threshold, `MIN_MUTUAL_COMPARABLE_PER_PAIR` = 5, and every other floor — `MIN_CLASSIFIED_PER_DIRECTION` 5,
`MIN_PAIRWISE_DIFFERENCES` 3 — are his diversity bar, and they do not move. The repair loop already names collapsed
dimensions and colliding pairs for some codes (`explain_validation_failure`); the act makes every code it names say
which dimension, which directions and what each read, and nothing the validator did not measure (§BH58(e)).

**HIS (b), READ.** Both rulings stand and neither is altered: §Z1(b) (`:1382–1385`, LIVE within §Z1) and §BH67(b)4.
The repository holds no one typographic scale — each composer carries its own tier constants, the lid's name
`HERO_NAME_PT` = 9.0 among them, the size measured on bottles that his (b) retires from lids. "The typographic scale"
is read as the classical scale of the trade — 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72 pt — the
executor's reading of which scale he means, recorded so one line from him can replace it. "The largest one the lid's

(the vision read's own box, scaled to the zone; the zone's text region where the read gives none), and the largest
